The questions (1033)

Each answer is derived from the rule text above. Worked figures are re-checked against the formulas in rules 44, 45 and 50 at build time.

Chapter I — Preliminary (51 questions)

PEN-001 · Commencement · Rule 1
The CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 came into force:
  1. A From the date of their publication in the Official Gazette
  2. B From the date the National Pension System Rules came into force
  3. C From 1 January 2021, the start of the year
  4. D From 1 April 2016, retrospectively
Answer and reasoning
( A) From the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. (B) From the date the National Pension System Rules came into force. — The two instruments are separate; rule 1(2) fixes this one's own date. (C) From 1 January 2021, the start of the year. — The rules do not adopt a calendar date; they adopt the date of publication. (D) From 1 April 2016, retrospectively. — There is no retrospective commencement in rule 1(2). Rule 1(2) brings the rules into force with effect from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. They were notified by G.S.R. 868(E) dated 20 December 2021, so that is the commencement date. Notice the contrast with the 2016 Pay Rules, which were given retrospective effect from 1 January 2016: the pension rules have no such deeming provision, and a question that offers 1 January 2021 is trading on the wrong instrument. Exam-safe point: Commencement: date of publication in the Gazette, 20.12.2021. Statutory Authority: Rule 1(2), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PEN-002 · Application — the cut-off · Rule 2
The 2021 Rules apply to Government servants appointed:
  1. A On or after 1 January 2004, because the rules are new
  2. B On or before 31 December 2003, in any establishment including a contributory one
  3. C On any date, whatever the date of appointment
  4. D On or before 31 December 2003, on a pensionable establishment
Answer and reasoning
( D) On or before 31 December 2003, on a pensionable establishment. (A) On or after 1 January 2004, because the rules are new. — That is the class the rules do NOT cover; post-2003 entrants are under the NPS Rules. (B) On or before 31 December 2003, in any establishment including a contributory one. — Rule 2 expressly excludes persons entitled to a Contributory Provident Fund. (C) On any date, whatever the date of appointment. — The cut-off date is central to rule 2, not incidental to it. Rule 2 applies the rules to servants appointed on or before 31 December 2003, appointed substantively to civil services and posts borne on pensionable establishments. The cut-off is the whole architecture of the 2021 Rules: the same notification period also produced the CCS (Implementation of National Pension System) Rules, 2021, which govern those appointed after that date unless they fall in one of the Explanation cases. Exam-safe point: Cut-off: 31.12.2003, and the establishment must be pensionable. Statutory Authority: Rule 2, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PEN-003 · Induction training · Rule 2 — Explanation (1)
A servant was put on induction training in 2003 and appointed on a regular basis in 2004. Rule 2's Explanation:
  1. A Excludes him, because the regular appointment was after the cut-off — The Explanation exists precisely to bring this case in
  2. B Excludes him unless he was paid a regular salary during training — A salary or a stipend suffices; a regular salary is not required
  3. C Covers him if the training was essential for the regular appointment and the training period counted as qualifying service
  4. D Covers him whatever the terms of the training — Three conditions attach, and all three must be met
Answer and reasoning
( C) Covers him if the training was essential for the regular appointment and the training period counted as qualifying service. Explanation (1) to rule 2 brings in a servant put on induction training on or before 31 December 2003 followed by regular appointment after that date, on three conditions: completion of the training was an essential condition for the regular appointment; he was eligible for a salary or a stipend during it; and the training period was eligible to count as qualifying service under the 1972 Rules. Miss any one and the Explanation does not reach him. Exam-safe point: Induction training: three cumulative conditions, all in Explanation (1). Statutory Authority: Rule 2, Explanation (1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PEN-004 · Gratuity — three kinds · Rule 3(1)(o)
The definition of 'gratuity' in rule 3(1)(o) includes:
  1. A Retirement gratuity and commuted value of pension
  2. B Service gratuity, retirement or death gratuity, and residuary gratuity
  3. C Only service gratuity and retirement gratuity
  4. D Only retirement gratuity
Answer and reasoning
( B) Service gratuity, retirement or death gratuity, and residuary gratuity. (A) Retirement gratuity and commuted value of pension. — Commutation is pension, not gratuity. (C) Only service gratuity and retirement gratuity. — Residuary gratuity under rule 45(3) is also inside the definition. (D) Only retirement gratuity. — The definition is wider, and it names three instruments. Rule 3(1)(o) defines gratuity to include service gratuity under rule 44, retirement or death gratuity under rule 45(1), and residuary gratuity under rule 45(3). The three are different instruments with different triggers: service gratuity replaces pension where qualifying service falls short; retirement and death gratuity are the lump sum on retirement or death; residuary gratuity fills up a shortfall where a pensioner dies within five years of retiring. Exam-safe point: Three gratuities: service (r.44), retirement/death (r.45(1)), residuary (r.45(3)). Statutory Authority: Rule 3(1)(o), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PEN-005 · Permanent transfer — the option · Rule 4(1)
A servant permanently transferred from a post not governed by these rules may elect to remain under his old pension rules. The option must be exercised:
  1. A At any time before retirement — The option is time-bound, and the period runs from the transfer
  2. B Within six months of the order of permanent transfer, or of return from leave if on leave
  3. C Within three months of the transfer order, in every case
  4. D Within one year of the transfer order
Answer and reasoning
( B) Within six months of the order of permanent transfer, or of return from leave if on leave. (C) Within three months of the transfer order, in every case. — Three months is the voluntary-retirement notice period, not this option. (D) Within one year of the transfer order. — The figure is six months, extended only for a servant on leave. The proviso to rule 4(1) gives six months from the date of issue of the order of permanent transfer, or, if the servant is on leave on that date, six months from his return from leave, whichever is later. Rule 4(2) requires the option in writing to the authority making the transfer order, and rule 4(3) makes it final. Three separate sub-rules, three separate testable facts. Exam-safe point: Option: six months, in writing, and final. Statutory Authority: Rule 4, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PF-001 · Form and Format — the distinction · Rule 3(1)(k) and 3(1)(l)
The rules define a 'Form' and a 'Format' separately. Which is correct?
  1. A They are synonyms, and either word may be used for any appendix
  2. B A Format is a form prescribed by a State Government — Nothing in the definition ties a Format to a State
  3. C A Form is a form appended to the rules; a Format is a format appended to them — two separate series
  4. D A Form is used in service, a Format after retirement
Answer and reasoning
( C) A Form is a form appended to the rules; a Format is a format appended to them — two separate series. (A) They are synonyms, and either word may be used for any appendix. — Rules 3(1)(k) and 3(1)(l) define them in two separate clauses. (D) A Form is used in service, a Format after retirement. — The distinction is by appendix, not by stage of service. Rule 3(1)(k) defines a Form as a form appended to these rules; rule 3(1)(l) defines a Format as a format appended to them. The two series are appended separately and are numbered independently, which is why the rules can speak of Form 3 (nomination) and Format 3 (memorandum of charges) without confusion. When a question asks which instrument is prescribed, the answer depends on the clause, and the clause says Form or Format. Exam-safe point: Form and Format are two distinct appended series. Statutory Authority: Rules 3(1)(k) and 3(1)(l), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-028 · Who the Rules apply to · Rule 2 and O.M. 03.03.2023
The CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 apply to a Government servant appointed:
  1. A on or before 31 December 2003, subject to the exclusions in rule 2 and the option in the 2023 order
  2. B only if he was confirmed in his appointment before 2004 — Confirmation is not the test in rule 2
  3. C after 31 December 2003, if he is not covered by the National Pension System
  4. D on any date, whatever the date of appointment
Answer and reasoning
( A) on or before 31 December 2003, subject to the exclusions in rule 2 and the option in the 2023 order. (C) after 31 December 2003, if he is not covered by the National Pension System. — The converse is the point: post-2003 appointees are under the NPS unless the 2023 option applies. (D) on any date, whatever the date of appointment. — The Rules were confined to persons appointed on or before 31 December 2003. Rule 2 applies the Rules to Government servants appointed on or before 31 December 2003 who are borne on pensionable establishments, subject to eight exclusions and an Explanation that brings in several further categories. The order of 3 March 2023 adds a one-time option for a person appointed after that date against a post advertised on or before 22 December 2003. Exam-safe point: Cut-off 31.12.2003, with the 2023 option as the exception. Statutory Authority: Rule 2, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 and DoP&PW O.M. dated 03.03.2023
CU-031 · Transfer into the Rules · Rule 4(1)
A Government servant is transferred permanently to a service or post to which the CCS (Pension) Rules apply, from one to which they do not. He:
  1. A is covered only if his former service is counted for pension
  2. B must complete five years in the new post before the rules apply
  3. C becomes subject to these rules
  4. D remains under his former pension scheme until he opts
Answer and reasoning
( C) becomes subject to these rules. (A) is covered only if his former service is counted for pension. — Counting is dealt with separately in rule 13 and rule 14. (B) must complete five years in the new post before the rules apply. — No qualifying period is attached to the transfer itself. (D) remains under his former pension scheme until he opts. — Rule 4(1) applies the rules on permanent transfer; it does not preserve the former scheme. Rule 4(1) provides that a Government servant transferred permanently to a service or post to which these rules apply from one to which they do not apply becomes subject to these rules. The rule's second sub-rule deals with the converse transfer, out of the rules, and saves the pension already earned. Exam-safe point: Permanent transfer in brings the servant under the Rules. Statutory Authority: Rule 4(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-047 · Pension Disbursing Authority · Rule 3(1)(u)
Rule 3(1)(u) defines a Pension Disbursing Authority to mean:
  1. A the Head of Office that sanctioned the pension — The Head of Office sanctions and forwards; the disbursing authorities are listed in the definition
  2. B the Central Pension Accounting Office alone — That office issues the Special Seal of Authority; it does not disburse
  3. C any bank in which the pensioner holds an account — The bank must be one selected in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India
  4. D a bank selected in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India, a post office, a treasury including a sub-treasury, or an Accounts Officer
Answer and reasoning
( D) a bank selected in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India, a post office, a treasury including a sub-treasury, or an Accounts Officer. Rule 3(1)(u) defines Pension Disbursing Authority by enumeration: a bank selected in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India, a post office, a treasury including a sub-treasury, or an Accounts Officer. Rule 80(4) then requires the Pension Disbursing Authority to disburse family pension within fifteen days of receiving the Special Seal of Authority. Exam-safe point: Four kinds of disbursing authority, the bank being a selected bank. Statutory Authority: Rule 3(1)(u), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-048 · Treasury · Rule 3(1)(z)
For the purposes of the Rules, 'Treasury':
  1. A means the Reserve Bank of India acting as banker to the Government
  2. B excludes a Sub-Treasury, which is a separate office
  3. C means only a Treasury in a State capital
  4. D includes a Sub-Treasury
Answer and reasoning
( D) includes a Sub-Treasury. (A) means the Reserve Bank of India acting as banker to the Government. — That is a different office, dealt with elsewhere. (B) excludes a Sub-Treasury, which is a separate office. — The definition expressly includes it. (C) means only a Treasury in a State capital. — No such limitation appears. Rule 3(1)(z) provides that 'Treasury' includes a Sub-Treasury. The definition matters because rule 3(1)(u) makes a treasury including a sub-treasury one of the Pension Disbursing Authorities. Exam-safe point: 'Treasury' includes a Sub-Treasury, and both may disburse. Statutory Authority: Rule 3(1)(z), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
TX-0001 · Sub-rule (1) of rule 1 · Rule 1 · 1(1)
Which of the following is the text of sub-rule (1) of rule 1?
  1. A Provided that where a part of pension is withheld or withdrawn, the amount of such pension shall not be reduced below the amount of minimum pension under rule 44.
  2. B any misconduct whether resulting in pecuniary loss to the Government or otherwise. (4) the expression “civil proceedings” would mean such proceedings in respect of a civil suit filed by the Government only.
  3. C These rules may be called the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021.
  4. D “Defence Service” means services under the Government of India in the Ministry of Defence including the Defence Accounts Department, paid out of the Civil Estimates of Ministry of Defence and not subject to the Air Force Act, 1950 (45 of 1950) or the Army Act, 1950 (46 of 1950) or the Navy Act, 1957 (62 of 1957);
Answer and reasoning
( C) These rules may be called the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021. (A) Provided that where a part of pension is withheld or withdrawn, the amount of such pension shall not be reduced below the amount of minimum pension under rule 44. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. (B) any misconduct whether resulting in pecuniary loss to the Government or otherwise. (4) the expression “civil proceedings” would mean such proceedings in respect of a civil suit filed by the Government only. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. (D) “Defence Service” means services under the Government of India in the Ministry of Defence including the Defence Accounts Department, paid out of the Civil Estimates of Ministry of Defence and not subject to the Air Force Act, 1950 (45 of 1950) or the Army Act, 1950 (46 of 1950) or the Navy Act, 1957 (62 of 1957);. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. The answer reproduces the provision as notified. The three wrong options are other provisions of the same rules, so the question tests recall of this provision rather than recognition of the statute's style. Exam-safe point: sub-rule (1) of rule 1 of rule 1, in its own words. Statutory Authority: Sub-rule (1) of rule 1, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
TX-0002 · Sub-rule (2) of rule 1 · Rule 1 · 1(2)
Which of the following is the text of sub-rule (2) of rule 1?
  1. A The Head of the Organisation shall vest with the authority to decide as to whether the proposed material for publication is sensitive or non-sensitive, and whether it falls in the domain of the organisation.
  2. B They shall come into force with effect from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.
  3. C Explanation.— For the purposes of this clause, “conflict of interest” shall not include normal economic competition with the Government or its undertakings.
  4. D “Government dues” means dues as defined in sub-rule (2) of rule 67;
Answer and reasoning
( B) They shall come into force with effect from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. (A) The Head of the Organisation shall vest with the authority to decide as to whether the proposed material for publication is sensitive or non-sensitive, and whether it falls in the domain of the organisation. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. (C) Explanation.— For the purposes of this clause, “conflict of interest” shall not include normal economic competition with the Government or its undertakings. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. (D) “Government dues” means dues as defined in sub-rule (2) of rule 67;. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. The answer reproduces the provision as notified. The three wrong options are other provisions of the same rules, so the question tests recall of this provision rather than recognition of the statute's style. Exam-safe point: sub-rule (2) of rule 1 of rule 1, in its own words. Statutory Authority: Sub-rule (2) of rule 1, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
TX-0003 · Clause (i) of sub-rule (2) of rule 2 · Rule 2 · 2(2)(i)
Which of the following is the text of clause (i) of sub-rule (2) of rule 2?
  1. A Provided further that where a part of pension is withheld or withdrawn the amount of such pension shall not be reduced below the amount of minimum pension under rule 44.
  2. B in an establishment or Department of the Central Government whose employees were covered by a pension scheme other than the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 1972; or
  3. C In order to ensure that all aspects relating to the case have received proper attention, the administrative Ministry or Department shall maintain a check list in Form 2.
  4. D “Minor” means a person who has not completed the age of eighteen years; — It is the text of a different provision of these rules
Answer and reasoning
( B) in an establishment or Department of the Central Government whose employees were covered by a pension scheme other than the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 1972; or. (A) Provided further that where a part of pension is withheld or withdrawn the amount of such pension shall not be reduced below the amount of minimum pension under rule 44. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. (C) In order to ensure that all aspects relating to the case have received proper attention, the administrative Ministry or Department shall maintain a check list in Form 2. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. The answer reproduces the provision as notified. The three wrong options are other provisions of the same rules, so the question tests recall of this provision rather than recognition of the statute's style. Exam-safe point: clause (i) of sub-rule (2) of rule 2 of rule 2, in its own words. Statutory Authority: Clause (i) of sub-rule (2) of rule 2, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
TX-0004 · Sub-rule (3) of rule 2 · Rule 2 · 2(3)
Which of the following is the text of sub-rule (3) of rule 2?
  1. A a Government servant appointed after 31st December, 2003 to a civil service or post in connection with the affairs of the Union, if he fulfils the conditions for coverage under these rules in accordance with any special or general order issued by the Government in this regard.
  2. B the nature of, and the emoluments from the commercial employment taken up by the pensioner concerned; and — It is the text of a different provision of these rules
  3. C The provisional pension shall be authorised by the Accounts Officer during the period commencing from the date following the date of retirement up to and including the date on which, after the conclusion of departmental or judicial proceedings, final orders are passed by the competent authority.
  4. D “Service Book” includes service roll, if any; and — It is the text of a different provision of these rules
Answer and reasoning
( A) a Government servant appointed after 31st December, 2003 to a civil service or post in connection with the affairs of the Union, if he fulfils the conditions for coverage under these rules in accordance with any special or general order issued by the Government in this regard. (C) The provisional pension shall be authorised by the Accounts Officer during the period commencing from the date following the date of retirement up to and including the date on which, after the conclusion of departmental or judicial proceedings, final orders are passed by the competent authority. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. The answer reproduces the provision as notified. The three wrong options are other provisions of the same rules, so the question tests recall of this provision rather than recognition of the statute's style. Exam-safe point: sub-rule (3) of rule 2 of rule 2, in its own words. Statutory Authority: Sub-rule (3) of rule 2, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
TX-0005 · Clause (b) of sub-rule (1) of rule 3 · Rule 3 · 3(1)(b)
Which of the following is the text of clause (b) of sub-rule (1) of rule 3?
  1. A Provided that in a case where the Government servant immediately before his retirement or death was absent from duty on leave or otherwise or was under suspension, the day of retirement or death shall be part of such leave or absence or suspension.

Chapter II — General Conditions (101 questions)

PEN-006 · Which rules govern the claim · Rule 5(1)
A servant's claim to pension is governed by:
  1. A The rules in force when he retires, is retired, discharged, resigns or dies
  2. B Whichever set of rules is more beneficial to him
  3. C The rules in force when he was appointed
  4. D The rules in force on the date he applies for pension
Answer and reasoning
( A) The rules in force when he retires, is retired, discharged, resigns or dies. (B) Whichever set of rules is more beneficial to him. — Rule 5(1) fixes a single date; it offers no comparison. (C) The rules in force when he was appointed. — Pension is governed by the rules at the exit, not the entry. (D) The rules in force on the date he applies for pension. — The claim is judged at the event, not at the application. Rule 5(1) is a choice-of-law provision: the claim is regulated by the provisions in force at the time the servant retires, is retired, is discharged, is allowed to resign, or dies. That is why the 1972 Rules still govern servants who retired before 20 December 2021, and why the 2021 Rules reach a retirement that happens after that date even where the service was rendered under the older rules. Exam-safe point: Claim governed by the rules at the exit event. Statutory Authority: Rule 5(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PEN-007 · The last day · Rule 5(2)
The day on which a servant retires, and the date of his death, are treated as:
  1. A A half day, for pension arithmetic — The rule treats the day as completed, not as a fraction
  2. B A day of leave in every case
  3. C A day outside service, so no pay or qualifying service accrues
  4. D A completed working day — the last completed working day in the case of retirement
Answer and reasoning
( D) A completed working day — the last completed working day in the case of retirement. (B) A day of leave in every case. — Leave is the position only where he was in fact on leave immediately before. (C) A day outside service, so no pay or qualifying service accrues. — Rule 5(2) does the opposite: it makes the day count. Rule 5(2) treats the day of retirement or discharge as the last completed working day and the date of death as a completed working day. The proviso deals with the case where the servant was, immediately before, on leave or under suspension: then the day of retirement or death is part of that leave, absence or suspension. The point matters because a day more or less can move the ten-month average under rule 32. Exam-safe point: Day of retirement or death counts as a completed day. Statutory Authority: Rule 5(2), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PEN-008 · Two pensions · Rule 6(1)
Under rule 6(1), a Government servant:
  1. A Shall not earn two pensions even for wholly separate services
  2. B May always draw a second pension after re-employment
  3. C Shall not earn two pensions in the same service or post at the same time or by the same continuous service
  4. D May earn two pensions if the second is for a different post
Answer and reasoning
( C) Shall not earn two pensions in the same service or post at the same time or by the same continuous service. (A) Shall not earn two pensions even for wholly separate services. — The bar is confined to the same service or post and the same continuous service. (B) May always draw a second pension after re-employment. — Re-employment is dealt with in rule 6(2) and is also barred, subject to rules 19 and 20. (D) May earn two pensions if the second is for a different post. — The bar is on two pensions in the same service or post at the same time, not on two posts generally. Rule 6(1) bars two pensions in the same service or post at the same time or by the same continuous service. Rule 6(2) then bars a separate pension or gratuity for a period of re-employment, except as provided in rule 19 or rule 20. The two sub-rules are often confused: (1) is about double-counting one service, (2) is about a pensioner who returns to Government service. Exam-safe point: No two pensions for the same service or post at the same time. Statutory Authority: Rule 6(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PEN-009 · Withholding — the floor · Rule 7(1)(b)
Where a part of pension is withheld under rule 7(1)(b), the pension shall not be reduced below:
  1. A Fifty per cent of the pension originally sanctioned
  2. B The amount of family pension admissible
  3. C The amount of minimum pension under rule 44
  4. D There is no floor; the whole pension may be withheld
Answer and reasoning
( C) The amount of minimum pension under rule 44. (A) Fifty per cent of the pension originally sanctioned. — The proviso fixes a floor by reference to rule 44, not a percentage. (B) The amount of family pension admissible. — Family pension is a different instrument under rule 50. (D) There is no floor; the whole pension may be withheld. — The whole may be withheld, but a part may not be reduced below the floor. Rule 7(1)(b) allows the Appointing Authority to withhold or withdraw a pension, or part of it, permanently or for a specified period, where the pensioner is convicted of a serious crime or found guilty of grave misconduct. The proviso puts a floor under a partial withholding: the amount shall not be reduced below the minimum pension under rule 44. Withholding in full is a different power and is not touched by the proviso. Exam-safe point: Partial withholding: never below the rule 44 minimum. Statutory Authority: Rule 7(1)(b) and its proviso, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PEN-010 · Publication by an intelligence officer · Rule 7(4)(b)
A retired servant of an Intelligence organisation in the Second Schedule to the RTI Act publishes material on his work without clearance. The undertaking he gave was in:
  1. A Form 3
  2. B Format 1
  3. C Format 2
  4. D Form 1
Answer and reasoning
( B) Format 1. (A) Form 3. — Form 3 is the nomination for gratuity. (C) Format 2. — Format 2 is the President's sanction to institute proceedings after retirement. (D) Form 1. — Form 1 is the application for commercial employment under rule 9; the undertaking is a Format. The rulebook appends two separate series and rule 3 defines them separately: a Form is a form appended to the rules, and a Format is a format appended to them. Rule 7(4)(b) requires the undertaking to be given in Format 1, and a failure to observe it is treated as grave misconduct under rule 7. The distinction is worth learning as a pair, because the paper tests it by offering a Form where a Format is required. Exam-safe point: Publication undertaking: Format 1, not Form 1. Statutory Authority: Rules 3(1)(k), 3(1)(l) and 7(4)(b), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PEN-011 · Proceedings after retirement · Rule 8(2)(c)
Departmental proceedings not instituted while the servant was in service:
  1. A May be instituted only with the sanction of the President, in Format 2
  2. B May never be instituted after retirement
  3. C May be instituted by any authority that could have done so in service
  4. D May be instituted for any event, however old
Answer and reasoning
( A) May be instituted only with the sanction of the President, in Format 2. (B) May never be instituted after retirement. — They may, on the conditions in rule 8(2)(c), which is why the sub-rule exists. (C) May be instituted by any authority that could have done so in service. — The sanction of the President is a pre-condition, in Format 2. (D) May be instituted for any event, however old. — Clause (ii) bars an event more than four years before the institution. Rule 8(2)(c) sets three limits on proceedings not instituted in service: they shall not be instituted save with the sanction of the President in Format 2; they shall not concern an event more than four years before the institution; and they shall be conducted by such authority and place as the President directs. The proviso adds that a memorandum of charges must be communicated to the pensioner in Format 3. Exam-safe point: Post-retirement proceedings: President's sanction, four-year bar, Formats 2 and 3. Statutory Authority: Rule 8(2)(c), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PEN-012 · Provisional pension — the amount · Rule 8(4)(a)
Where proceedings are pending, the provisional pension under rule 8(4)(a) is equal to:
  1. A The minimum pension under rule 44
  2. B Fifty per cent of the pension, pending conclusion — There is no such fraction in rule 8(4)
  3. C Two-thirds of the pension that would have been admissible
  4. D The maximum pension that would have been admissible on the qualifying service up to retirement
Answer and reasoning
( D) The maximum pension that would have been admissible on the qualifying service up to retirement. (A) The minimum pension under rule 44. — The minimum is a floor elsewhere; here the amount is the maximum pension. (C) Two-thirds of the pension that would have been admissible. — Two-thirds is the compulsory-retirement provisional figure under rule 40(3). Rule 8(4)(a) authorises a provisional pension equal to the maximum pension that would have been admissible on the qualifying service up to the date of retirement — or, if the servant was under suspension on that date, up to the day before he was placed under suspension. This is the proceedings case, and it is deliberately generous because no gratuity is paid at all under rule 8(4)(c) until the proceedings conclude. Exam-safe point: Proceedings case: maximum admissible pension, and no gratuity. Statutory Authority: Rule 8(4), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PEN-013 · Recovery from pension · Rule 8(6)
Where the President orders recovery of pecuniary loss from pension, the recovery shall not ordinarily exceed:
  1. A Ten per cent of the pension
  2. B The whole pension, since it is a recovery of loss
  3. C One-half of the pension admissible on the date of retirement
  4. D One-third of the pension admissible on the date of retirement
Answer and reasoning
( D) One-third of the pension admissible on the date of retirement. (A) Ten per cent of the pension. — Ten per cent is the gratuity withholding in the rule 62 delay case. (B) The whole pension, since it is a recovery of loss. — The rule caps the rate, which is the point of sub-rule (6). (C) One-half of the pension admissible on the date of retirement. — The rule says one-third. Rule 8(6) puts a rate cap on a recovery of pecuniary loss where the President decides not to withhold or withdraw the pension: the recovery shall not ordinarily be made at a rate exceeding one-third of the pension admissible on the date of retirement. The word 'ordinarily' leaves room for an exceptional case, but the starting rule is one-third. Exam-safe point: Recovery cap: one-third of the pension at retirement. Statutory Authority: Rule 8(6), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PEN-014 · Commercial employment · Rule 9(1)
A Group 'A' pensioner wishing to take up commercial employment must obtain sanction if he does so:
  1. A Within six months of his retirement
  2. B At any time after retirement
  3. C Within one year of his retirement
  4. D Within two years of his retirement
Answer and reasoning
( C) Within one year of his retirement. (A) Within six months of his retirement. — Six months is the rule 4 option period. (B) At any time after retirement. — The rule is confined to the first year; after that no sanction is required. (D) Within two years of his retirement. — The period in rule 9(1) is one year. Rule 9(1) requires a pensioner who was a member of Central Service Group 'A' immediately before retirement to obtain the previous sanction of the Government before accepting commercial employment within one year of retirement, applying in Form 1. Rule 9(8) supplies the sanction for breach: the Government may declare that he is not entitled to the whole or part of his pension for such period as the order specifies. Exam-safe point: Commercial employment: one year, sanction in Form 1. Statutory Authority: Rule 9(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PEN-015 · Employment under a foreign Government · Rule 10(1)
A Group 'A' pensioner accepting employment under a Government outside India without permission:
  1. A Forfeits his pension permanently in every case
  2. B Forfeits pension for the period of that employment, or such longer period as the Government directs
  3. C Must refund his entire gratuity — The rule speaks of pension for the period, not of refunding gratuity
  4. D Suffers no consequence, because the pension is already sanctioned
Answer and reasoning
( B) Forfeits pension for the period of that employment, or such longer period as the Government directs. (A) Forfeits his pension permanently in every case. — The rule ties the loss to the period of employment, extendable by direction. (D) Suffers no consequence, because the pension is already sanctioned. — Rule 10(1) attaches a consequence, and it is a period-based loss. Rule 10(1) requires previous permission of the Central Government for employment under any Government outside India, and provides that no pension is payable in respect of any period for which he is so employed, or such longer period as the Government may direct. Read it against rule 9: rule 9 is commercial employment anywhere and carries a declaration power over pension; rule 10 is employment under a foreign Government and carries a period-based forfeiture. Exam-safe point: Foreign Government employment: pension lost for the period. Statutory Authority: Rule 10(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PF-003 · Memorandum of charges · Rule 8(2)(c) proviso
A memorandum of charges to be communicated to a pensioner under rule 8 is in:
  1. A Form 3
  2. B Format 3
  3. C Form 9
  4. D Format 1
Answer and reasoning
( B) Format 3. (A) Form 3. — Form 3 is the nomination for gratuity, which is a very different document. (C) Form 9. — Form 9 is a family member's claim for gratuity. (D) Format 1. — Format 1 is the intelligence organisation's publication undertaking. The proviso to rule 8(2)(c) requires the memorandum of charges to be communicated to the pensioner in Format 3. The Formats are the working papers of the proceedings side of the rules — the sanction to institute proceedings is Format 2, the charges are Format 3 — while the Forms belong mostly to the claims and certificates side. Exam-safe point: Charges memorandum: Format 3. Sanction: Format 2. Statutory Authority: Rule 8(2)(c) proviso, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PF-004 · RTI undertaking · Rule 7(4)(b)
The undertaking on post-retirement publication, required of a servant of an Intelligence organisation, is in:
  1. A Format 1
  2. B Form 2
  3. C Form 1
  4. D Format 4
Answer and reasoning
( A) Format 1. (B) Form 2. — Form 2 is the check list for commercial employment. (C) Form 1. — Form 1 begins the commercial-employment process. (D) Format 4. — Format 4 is the certificate of qualifying service. Rule 7(4)(b) requires the undertaking in Format 1. A failure to observe it is treated as grave misconduct under rule 7, which is why the undertaking is a statutory document and not an internal formality. In a case of a servant transferred out of such an organisation, rule 7(4)(c) requires the undertaking in duplicate, one copy in the service book and one kept by the organisation. Exam-safe point: Publication undertaking: Format 1, and in duplicate on transfer. Statutory Authority: Rule 7(4)(b) and (c), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PF-007 · Commercial employment application · Rule 9(1)
A pensioner applying for sanction to take up commercial employment applies in:
  1. A Format 2
  2. B Format 1
  3. C Form 1
  4. D Form 5
Answer and reasoning
( C) Form 1. (A) Format 2. — Format 2 is the President's sanction to institute proceedings. (B) Format 1. — Format 1 is the publication undertaking. (D) Form 5. — Form 5 is not the right series for this; the application is a Form, and it is Form 1. Rule 9(1) requires the application to be made in Form 1, and rule 9(5) requires the administrative Ministry to maintain a check list in Form 2. The two Form numbers sit next to each other and belong to the same procedure: the pensioner applies in Form 1 and the Ministry works the case on the Form 2 check list. A question that offers Format 1 is testing whether you noticed the word. Exam-safe point: Commercial employment: application in Form 1, check list in Form 2. Statutory Authority: Rules 9(1) and 9(5), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-004 · Competent authority to withhold pension · Rule 8(1) as substituted in 2022
After the amendment of 2022, who may withhold or withdraw a pension under rule 8(1) where the appointing authority for the post was subordinate to the President?
  1. A the President, who reserves the power to himself
  2. B the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, in every case
  3. C the Secretary of the administrative Ministry or Department
  4. D the Head of Office who processed the pension case
Answer and reasoning
( C) the Secretary of the administrative Ministry or Department. (A) the President, who reserves the power to himself. — The 2022 amendment moved the power to the Secretary where the appointing authority is subordinate to the President. (B) the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, in every case. — The Comptroller and Auditor-General acts only for the Indian Audit and Accounts Department. (D) the Head of Office who processed the pension case. — The Head of Office prepares the case; the power belongs to the authority in rule 8(1). Rule 8(1) was substituted by G.S.R. 770(E) dated 7 October 2022. The power is now exercised by the President where the President is the appointing authority for the post, by the Secretary of the administrative Ministry or Department where the appointing authority is subordinate to the President, and by the Comptroller and Auditor-General for a pensioner who retired from the Indian Audit and Accounts Department from a post below that level. Exam-safe point: President, Secretary, or C&AG, according to who appointed the pensioner. Statutory Authority: Rule 8(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 as substituted by G.S.R. 770(E) dated 07.10.2022
CU-005 · Appeal against an order under rule 8 · Rule 8(6A)
An appeal against an order withholding pension passed by the Secretary of a Ministry lies to:
  1. A no authority, because rule 8 orders are final
  2. B the President, who decides it in consultation with the Union Public Service Commission
  3. C the Union Public Service Commission directly
  4. D the Central Administrative Tribunal in the first instance
Answer and reasoning
( B) the President, who decides it in consultation with the Union Public Service Commission. (A) no authority, because rule 8 orders are final. — Only an order of the President is final; sub-rule (6A)(b) creates an appeal against any other authority's order. (C) the Union Public Service Commission directly. — The Commission is consulted; it does not hear the appeal. (D) the Central Administrative Tribunal in the first instance. — The statutory appeal under rule 8(6A) comes first; the Tribunal is a judicial remedy. Sub-rule (6A) was inserted by G.S.R. 770(E) dated 7 October 2022. Clause (a) says no appeal lies against an order made by the President. Clause (b) says an appeal against an order passed by any other authority lies to the President, who passes such orders as he deems fit in consultation with the Union Public Service Commission. Exam-safe point: Appeal lies to the President unless the President passed the order. Statutory Authority: Rule 8(6A), inserted by G.S.R. 770(E) dated 07.10.2022
CU-032 · The last working day · Rule 5(2)
The day on which a Government servant retires, is retired, is discharged or is allowed to resign is treated as:
  1. A the date from which pension begins in every case
  2. B his last completed working day, so that pension does not run from it
  3. C excluded from service altogether
  4. D a day of duty, so that it counts as qualifying service
Answer and reasoning
( B) his last completed working day, so that pension does not run from it. (A) the date from which pension begins in every case. — Pension begins from the date he ceases to be borne on the establishment, under rule 81. (C) excluded from service altogether. — The day is not removed from service; it is characterised. (D) a day of duty, so that it counts as qualifying service. — Rule 5(2) makes it the last completed working day, which is a different thing. Rule 5(2) provides that the day on which a Government servant retires or is retired or is discharged or is allowed to resign shall be treated as his last completed working day. Rule 81(1) then makes pension payable from the date on which he ceases to be borne on the establishment, and rule 81(3) pays pension for the day on which the recipient dies. Exam-safe point: Retirement day is the last completed working day. Statutory Authority: Rule 5(2), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-033 · Commercial employment: Group A officers · Rule 9(1)
A pensioner who was a member of a Central Service Group A immediately before retirement wishes to accept commercial employment within one year. He must:
  1. A obtain the previous sanction of the Government
  2. B apply to the Union Public Service Commission directly
  3. C wait out the year, since permission cannot be given before it ends
  4. D merely inform the Ministry after accepting the employment
Answer and reasoning
( A) obtain the previous sanction of the Government. (B) apply to the Union Public Service Commission directly. — The Commission is consulted in some cases; the application goes to the Government. (C) wait out the year, since permission cannot be given before it ends. — Permission may be given, and must be sought, before the employment is accepted. (D) merely inform the Ministry after accepting the employment. — Rule 9(1) requires previous sanction, not information afterwards. Rule 9(1) requires a pensioner who, immediately before retirement, was a member of a Central Service Group A, and who wishes to accept commercial employment before the expiry of one year from the date of retirement, to obtain the previous sanction of the Government. Rule 9(2) provides that sanction is not to be refused except on specified grounds, and rule 9(7) gives a right to a reasoned order and a review after thirty days. Exam-safe point: Previous sanction of the Government, within one year. Statutory Authority: Rule 9(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-034 · Refusal of permission · Rule 9(7)
Where the Government refuses permission for commercial employment or grants it subject to conditions, the applicant:
  1. A may, within thirty days of receipt of the order, ask for the reasons and for a review of the order
  2. B may appeal to the Union Public Service Commission
  3. C must wait one year before applying again — The rule provides a review, not a waiting period
  4. D has no remedy under the Rules — Rule 9(7) creates the remedy
Answer and reasoning
( A) may, within thirty days of receipt of the order, ask for the reasons and for a review of the order. (B) may appeal to the Union Public Service Commission. — The Commission may be consulted in the review; the request goes to the Government. Rule 9(7) provides that where the Government grants the permission subject to conditions or refuses it, the applicant may, within thirty days of the receipt of the order, request the Government to furnish the reasons for the order and to review it. Exam-safe point: Thirty days to seek reasons and a review. Statutory Authority: Rule 9(7), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-049 · Retirement benefits after a disciplinary finding · Rule 7(1)(b)
Rule 7 allows the Government to withhold or withdraw retirement benefits where a Government servant is found:
  1. A to hold property disproportionate to his known sources of income, in every case
  2. B to have been inefficient in the discharge of his duties — Inefficiency is dealt with through the disciplinary rules, not rule 7
  3. C to have been guilty of grave misconduct or negligence during the period of service, including service rendered on re-employment
  4. D to have failed to complete the qualifying service stated in his service book
Answer and reasoning
( C) to have been guilty of grave misconduct or negligence during the period of service, including service rendered on re-employment. (A) to hold property disproportionate to his known sources of income, in every case. — That may found a criminal case; rule 7 speaks of grave misconduct or negligence. (D) to have failed to complete the qualifying service stated in his service book. — A service-book defect is corrected under rule 57, not rule 7. Rule 7 deals with the right of the Government to withhold or withdraw pension or gratuity where the pensioner is found guilty of grave misconduct or negligence during the period of service, including service rendered on re-employment after retirement. Rule 8 then prescribes the procedure and the authority, as substituted in 2022. Exam-safe point: Grave misconduct or negligence during service, including re-employment. Statutory Authority: Rule 7(1)(b), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-050 · Sanction for proceedings instituted later · Rule 8(2)(c)(iii)
A departmental proceeding not instituted while the Government servant was in service:
  1. A may be instituted only by the President — The competent authority under rule 8(1) varies with the appointing authority
  2. B shall not be instituted after retirement except with the sanction of the authority competent to pass an order under rule 8(1)
  3. C may be instituted by any authority that could have instituted it during service
  4. D may not be instituted at all after retirement — It may be, with sanction and within the limitations the rule sets
Answer and reasoning
( B) shall not be instituted after retirement except with the sanction of the authority competent to pass an order under rule 8(1). (C) may be instituted by any authority that could have instituted it during service. — Rule 8(2)(c) requires the sanction of the competent authority. Rule 8(2)(c) provides that a departmental proceeding, if not instituted while the Government servant was in service, whether before his retirement or during his re-employment, shall not be instituted in respect of a cause of action which arose more than four years before the institution of the proceeding, and shall not be instituted save with the sanction of the authority competent to pass an order under rule 8(1). Exam-safe point: Later proceedings need the sanction of the rule 8(1) authority and a four-year limit. Statutory Authority: Rule 8(2)(c), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
TX-0035 · Sub-rule (1) of rule 5 · Rule 5 · 5(1)
Sub-rule (1) of rule 5 of the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 begins with which words?
  1. A Less than 1 year — 2 times of emoluments — It is the text of a different provision of these rules
  2. B Any claim to pension or family pension shall be regulated by the provisions of these rules in force at the time when a Government servant retires or is retired or is discharged or is allowed to resign from service or dies, as the case may be.
  3. C In the case of a Government servant who has exercised option under clause (a) of sub-rule (11), the pay which he would have drawn under the Central Government had he not been on deemed deputation shall be treated as emoluments for calculating the pensionary benefits to be paid by the Government.
  4. D Where an order imposing the penalty of dismissal or removal from service was issued before the date of commencement of these rules and the competent authority, at that time, did not examine or decide whether or not any compassionate allowance was to be granted in that case, that authority shall take a decision in this regard not later than six months from the date of commencement of these rules.
Answer and reasoning
( B) Any claim to pension or family pension shall be regulated by the provisions of these rules in force at the time when a Government servant retires or is retired or is discharged or is allowed to resign from service or dies, as the case may be. (C) In the case of a Government servant who has exercised option under clause (a) of sub-rule (11), the pay which he would have drawn under the Central Government had he not been on deemed deputation shall be treated as emoluments for calculating the pensionary benefits to be paid by the Government. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. (D) Where an order imposing the penalty of dismissal or removal from service was issued before the date of commencement of these rules and the competent authority, at that time, did not examine or decide whether or not any compassionate allowance was to be granted in that case, that authority shall take a decision in this regard not later than six months from the date of commencement of these rules. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. The answer reproduces the provision as notified. The three wrong options are other provisions of the same rules, so the question tests recall of this provision rather than recognition of the statute's style. Exam-safe point: sub-rule (1) of rule 5 of rule 5, in its own words. Statutory Authority: Sub-rule (1) of rule 5, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021

  2. B In the case of a Government servant who has rendered a qualifying service of four years and nine months or more but less than five years, his qualifying service for the purpose of this rule shall be five years and he shall be eligible for retirement gratuity in accordance with clause (a) of sub-rule (1).

(B) In the case of a Government servant who has rendered a qualifying service of four years and nine months or more but less than five years, his qualifying service for the purpose of this rule shall be five years and he shall be eligible for retirement gratuity in accordance with clause (a) of sub-rule (1). — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. The answer reproduces the provision as notified. The three wrong options are other provisions of the same rules, so the question tests recall of this provision rather than recognition of the statute's style. TX-0037 · Sub-rule (1) of rule 6 · Rule 6 · 6(1)

TX-0045 · Sub-rule (6) of rule 7 · Rule 7 · 7(6)
Sub-rule (6) of rule 7 of the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 begins with which words?
  1. A Provided that if the emoluments of a Government servant have been reduced during the last ten months of his service, average emoluments as referred to in rule 32 shall be treated as emoluments.
  2. B Where the authority competent to pass an order under sub-rule (1) is the President, the Union Public Service Commission shall be consulted before any order is passed.
  3. C subject to provisions of sub-rule (10), dependent parents (including adoptive parents) of the deceased Government servant or pensioner,
  4. D Where gratuity is granted under rule 45 to a minor member of the family of the deceased Government servant, it shall be payable to the guardian on behalf of the minor.
Answer and reasoning
( B) Where the authority competent to pass an order under sub-rule (1) is the President, the Union Public Service Commission shall be consulted before any order is passed. (A) Provided that if the emoluments of a Government servant have been reduced during the last ten months of his service, average emoluments as referred to in rule 32 shall be treated as emoluments. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. (C) subject to provisions of sub-rule (10), dependent parents (including adoptive parents) of the deceased Government servant or pensioner,. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. (D) Where gratuity is granted under rule 45 to a minor member of the family of the deceased Government servant, it shall be payable to the guardian on behalf of the minor. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. The answer reproduces the provision as notified. The three wrong options are other provisions of the same rules, so the question tests recall of this provision rather than recognition of the statute's style. Exam-safe point: sub-rule (6) of rule 7 of rule 7, in its own words. Statutory Authority: Sub-rule (6) of rule 7, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021

Chapter III — Qualifying Service (95 questions)

PF-005 · Certificate of qualifying service · Rule 30(1)
The Head of Office communicates the qualifying service determined at verification to the servant in:
  1. A Format 6
  2. B Format 5
  3. C Form 4
  4. D Format 4
Answer and reasoning
( D) Format 4. (A) Format 6. — Format 6 is the medical certificate of incapacity. (B) Format 5. — Format 5 is the relieving order on absorption in a State Government. (C) Form 4. — Form 4 is the particulars-of-family form. Rule 30(1) requires the Head of Office, in consultation with the Accounts Officer, to verify service and communicate the qualifying service determined in Format 4 on two occasions: after eighteen years of service, and when five years of service remain before superannuation. Rule 30(4) makes that verification final and not open to reopening except on a change in the rules. Exam-safe point: Qualifying service certificate: Format 4, at 18 years and at 5 years to go. Statutory Authority: Rule 30(1) and (4), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-001 · Commencement of qualifying service · Rule 11
Qualifying service commences from the date the Government servant:
  1. A takes charge of the post to which he is first appointed, substantively or in an officiating or temporary capacity
  2. B attains the age of eighteen years, in every case
  3. C completes the probation period attached to his first post
  4. D is confirmed in his first appointment — Confirmation is dealt with at rule 16; commencement is at rule 11
Answer and reasoning
( A) takes charge of the post to which he is first appointed, substantively or in an officiating or temporary capacity. (B) attains the age of eighteen years, in every case. — Service before eighteen is excluded by the second proviso, with a military-service exception. (C) completes the probation period attached to his first post. — Rule 16 separately provides that probation followed by confirmation qualifies. Rule 11 fixes commencement at the date of taking charge of the post to which the servant is first appointed, whether substantively, in an officiating capacity or on a temporary basis. Two provisos qualify it: officiating or temporary service must be followed without interruption by substantive appointment, and service before the age of eighteen does not count except in the case of military service counted for civil pension under rule 20. Exam-safe point: Qualifying service begins on taking charge, not on confirmation. Statutory Authority: Rule 11, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-002 · Service as apprentice · Rule 17
Service as an apprentice counts as qualifying service:
  1. A never, under any circumstances — There is an express exception for SAS apprentices in the two accounts departments
  2. B only where the apprentice was subsequently confirmed
  3. C in every case, because apprenticeship is a recognised form of service — Rule 17 is a rule of exclusion, not inclusion
  4. D only in the case of a Subordinate Accounts Service apprentice in the IA&AD or the Defence Accounts Department
Answer and reasoning
( D) only in the case of a Subordinate Accounts Service apprentice in the IA&AD or the Defence Accounts Department. (B) only where the apprentice was subsequently confirmed. — The exception is by department and service, not by later confirmation. Rule 17 states the general rule first: service as an apprentice shall not qualify. It then carves out the Subordinate Accounts Service apprentice in the Indian Audit and Accounts Department or the Defence Accounts Department. The examinable point is the narrowness of the exception, which sits alongside rule 16, where service on probation followed by confirmation does qualify. Exam-safe point: Apprenticeship: excluded, except SAS apprentices in IA&AD and Defence Accounts. Statutory Authority: Rules 16 and 17, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-003 · Leave that counts as qualifying service · Rule 21
Which leave counts as qualifying service without any special order?
  1. A Only earned leave and half pay leave
  2. B No leave at all counts; only duty counts
  3. C All extraordinary leave, whatever the reason for which it was granted
  4. D All leave for which leave salary is payable, and all extraordinary leave granted on medical certificate
Answer and reasoning
( D) All leave for which leave salary is payable, and all extraordinary leave granted on medical certificate. (A) Only earned leave and half pay leave. — Leave salary is the test, which also covers commuted leave and leave not due. (B) No leave at all counts; only duty counts. — Rule 21 is an inclusive provision and expressly counts leave with salary. (C) All extraordinary leave, whatever the reason for which it was granted. — Ordinary extraordinary leave counts only if the appointing authority so allows at the time of grant. Rule 21 counts all leave during service for which leave salary is payable and all extraordinary leave granted on medical certificate. The proviso allows the appointing authority, at the time of granting other extraordinary leave, to direct that it count where the servant could not join or rejoin duty because of civil commotion or was prosecuting higher scientific and technical studies. Exam-safe point: Leave with salary and medical-certificate EOL count; other EOL does not unless allowed on grant. Statutory Authority: Rule 21, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-004 · Suspension and qualifying service · Rule 23
Time under suspension counts as qualifying service where, on conclusion of the inquiry, the servant:
  1. A has the period regularised as extraordinary leave
  2. B is reinstated, whatever the findings — Reinstatement is not the test; the findings on the inquiry are
  3. C is fully exonerated, or only a minor penalty is imposed and the suspension is held wholly unjustified
  4. D is awarded any penalty short of dismissal
Answer and reasoning
( C) is fully exonerated, or only a minor penalty is imposed and the suspension is held wholly unjustified. (A) has the period regularised as extraordinary leave. — Regularising it as extraordinary leave is a different consequence under rule 27. (D) is awarded any penalty short of dismissal. — The rule requires exoneration, or a minor penalty with an unjustified suspension. Rule 23(1) counts suspension time only where the servant is fully exonerated, or where only a minor penalty is imposed and the suspension is held to be wholly unjustified. Rule 23(2) otherwise excludes it unless the competent authority expressly declares that it shall count, and rule 23(3) requires that declaration to be made by order and recorded in the service book. Exam-safe point: Suspension counts only on exoneration, or a minor penalty with unjustified suspension. Statutory Authority: Rule 23, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-005 · Withdrawal of resignation · Rule 26(6)
A Government servant resigns to take up an appointment in a private commercial company. He later asks to withdraw the resignation. The appointing authority:
  1. A may accept it with the President's approval
  2. B shall not accept the request, because the resignation was to join a private commercial company
  3. C may accept it if a comparable post is available
  4. D may accept it if the absence did not exceed ninety days
Answer and reasoning
( B) shall not accept the request, because the resignation was to join a private commercial company. (A) may accept it with the President's approval. — Rule 26(6) is an absolute bar, not a matter of higher sanction. (C) may accept it if a comparable post is available. — Availability of the post is one of the rule 26(5) conditions, which rule 26(6) overrides. (D) may accept it if the absence did not exceed ninety days. — The ninety-day condition in rule 26(5)(iii) cannot rescue a resignation of this kind. Rule 26(5) permits withdrawal in the public interest on four conditions, including absence of not more than ninety days and availability of the post. Rule 26(6) then bars withdrawal altogether where the resignation was tendered to take up an appointment in a private commercial company, or in a corporation or company owned or controlled by the Government, or in a body controlled or financed by it. Exam-safe point: Withdrawal is barred where the resignation was to join a company or body. Statutory Authority: Rule 26(5) and (6), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-006 · Interruption in service · Rule 27(1)
An interruption in service forfeits past service, except in which case?
  1. A Joining time while on transfer from one post to another
  2. B Dismissal followed by reinstatement on review
  3. C Unauthorised absence after the post has been filled substantively
  4. D Resignation accepted to join another Government post without permission
Answer and reasoning
( A) Joining time while on transfer from one post to another. (B) Dismissal followed by reinstatement on review. — Reinstatement restores past service under rule 25, but the dismissal itself was not an excepted interruption. (C) Unauthorised absence after the post has been filled substantively. — Clause (b) protects unauthorised absence in continuation of authorised leave only while the post is not filled substantively. (D) Resignation accepted to join another Government post without permission. — Rule 26 governs resignation, and the protection in rule 26(2) requires proper permission. Rule 27(1) lists five exceptions to forfeiture: authorised leave of absence; unauthorised absence in continuation of authorised leave so long as the post is not filled substantively; suspension immediately followed by reinstatement, or ending in death or retirement; transfer to non-qualifying service in the public interest; and joining time on transfer. Rule 27(2) then lets the appointing authority commute periods of absence without leave retrospectively into extraordinary leave. Exam-safe point: Joining time is an excepted interruption. Statutory Authority: Rule 27, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-007 · Finality of verification · Rule 30(4)
Verification of qualifying service under rule 30 is:
  1. A final, and not to be reopened except on a subsequent change in the rules or orders governing qualifying service
  2. B open to reopening at any time on audit objection — Only a change in the governing rules and orders reopens it
  3. C provisional until the pension case is settled — Rule 30(4) makes the verification final, not provisional
  4. D final only where the servant has completed eighteen years
Answer and reasoning
( A) final, and not to be reopened except on a subsequent change in the rules or orders governing qualifying service. (D) final only where the servant has completed eighteen years. — The eighteen-year point is one of the two occasions for verification, not a condition of finality. Rule 30(1) requires verification after eighteen years of service and again when five years remain before superannuation, with the result communicated in Format 4. Rule 30(4) makes the verification final and immune from reopening except where a subsequent change in the rules and orders governing the conditions under which service qualifies for pension necessitates it. Exam-safe point: Verification is final; only a change of rules reopens it. Statutory Authority: Rule 30(1) and (4), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-051 · Counting military service · Rule 20(1)(i)
Military service rendered before civil employment is counted as qualifying service:
  1. A in the case of a re-employed Government servant, on the conditions set out in rule 20
  2. B in every case, without conditions
  3. C only if the military service exceeded five years — No such threshold appears in the sub-rule
  4. D never, military service being governed by separate rules
Answer and reasoning
( A) in the case of a re-employed Government servant, on the conditions set out in rule 20. (B) in every case, without conditions. — Rule 20 attaches conditions, including the nature of the discharge. (D) never, military service being governed by separate rules. — Rule 20 provides for counting it in specified cases. Rule 20 governs the counting of military service towards civil qualifying service. Sub-rule (1) deals with a person who was re-employed in civil service, and clause (i) with the case where he had rendered military service before his re-employment, on the conditions the sub-rule sets out, including the character of his discharge from the military. Exam-safe point: Military service counts only on rule 20's conditions. Statutory Authority: Rule 20(1)(i), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-052 · Interruption in service · Rule 27(1)(a)
Where a Government servant's service is interrupted, rule 27 provides that:
  1. A the interruption does not amount to removal or dismissal, and the service rendered before it may be counted on the conditions in the rule
  2. B the earlier service is forfeited in every case — Rule 27 allows it to be counted on conditions
  3. C the interruption operates as a break in qualifying service unless condoned by the President
  4. D the servant must be reappointed through the Staff Selection Commission — Reappointment procedure is not what rule 27 regulates
Answer and reasoning
( A) the interruption does not amount to removal or dismissal, and the service rendered before it may be counted on the conditions in the rule. (C) the interruption operates as a break in qualifying service unless condoned by the President. — The rule's own machinery applies, not a presidential condonation. Rule 27 deals with an interruption in the service of a Government servant. Sub-rule (1) provides that the interruption shall not amount to removal or dismissal within the meaning of rule 11 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, and clause (a) provides for the counting of the service rendered before the interruption subject to the conditions in the rule. Exam-safe point: An interruption is not a removal, and the earlier service may still count. Statutory Authority: Rule 27(1)(a), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-068 · Service before the age of eighteen · Rule 11 and its provisos
A person appointed at seventeen years of age. The service rendered before he attained eighteen:
  1. A does not count as qualifying service, except in the case of military service counted for civil pension under rule 20
  2. B counts from the date of his first increment — No such rule exists
  3. C counts only if he was confirmed before he turned eighteen — Confirmation is not the test; the age is
  4. D counts in full, because service is service — The second proviso to rule 11 excludes it
Answer and reasoning
( A) does not count as qualifying service, except in the case of military service counted for civil pension under rule 20. Rule 11 makes qualifying service commence from the date the Government servant takes charge of the post to which he is first appointed, substantively or in an officiating or temporary capacity. The first proviso requires officiating or temporary service to be followed without interruption by substantive appointment, and the second proviso excludes service rendered before the age of eighteen, except in the case of military service counted for civil pension under rule 20. Exam-safe point: Boy service is excluded by the second proviso, military service being the exception. Statutory Authority: Rule 11, second proviso, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-069 · Extraordinary leave other than on medical certificate · Rule 21 and its proviso
Extraordinary leave granted because the servant could not rejoin duty on account of civil commotion counts as qualifying service:
  1. A never, whatever the cause
  2. B automatically, civil commotion being a cause beyond his control
  3. C if he produces a certificate from the district magistrate after rejoining
  4. D only where the appointing authority so directs at the time of granting it
Answer and reasoning
( D) only where the appointing authority so directs at the time of granting it. (A) never, whatever the cause. — The proviso allows the direction in this and one other case. (B) automatically, civil commotion being a cause beyond his control. — The proviso requires a direction. (C) if he produces a certificate from the district magistrate after rejoining. — The rule turns on the direction at the time of grant, not on later evidence. Rule 21 counts all leave for which leave salary is payable and all extraordinary leave granted on medical certificate without any order. Its proviso allows the appointing authority, at the time of granting other extraordinary leave, to direct that it count as qualifying service where the Government servant could not join or rejoin duty because of civil commotion, or was prosecuting higher scientific and technical studies. Exam-safe point: Commotion EOL counts only on a direction given when it was granted. Statutory Authority: Rule 21, proviso, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021

Chapter IV — Emoluments and Average Emoluments (27 questions)

PS-008 · Average emoluments across a broken month · Rule 32(3) Illustration
A servant retires on 16 July 2019. For the fractional periods of the last ten months, emoluments are computed:
  1. A by ignoring the fractional periods altogether
  2. B by taking the actual number of days in each calendar month as the denominator
  3. C by rounding each fraction up to a whole month
  4. D by multiplying the emolument by 14/30 and 16/30, whatever the number of days in the month
Answer and reasoning
( D) by multiplying the emolument by 14/30 and 16/30, whatever the number of days in the month. (A) by ignoring the fractional periods altogether. — The rule includes equal periods before the ten months so that fractions add to a full month. (B) by taking the actual number of days in each calendar month as the denominator. — The rule fixes a thirty-day month precisely to avoid that. (C) by rounding each fraction up to a whole month. — Rounding up belongs to rule 44(9), and to the amount of pension, not to average emoluments. Rule 32(3) provides that where leave without salary or suspension not counting as service falls within the last ten months, the period is disregarded and an equal period before the ten months is included, a month being reckoned as thirty days so that fractions add up to a full month. The illustration works the point: a retirement on 16 July 2019 gives fractional periods of fourteen days of September 2018 and sixteen days of July 2019, computed at 14/30 and 16/30, including for February. Exam-safe point: Thirty-day month: 14/30 and 16/30, even for February. Statutory Authority: Rule 32(3) and its Illustration, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-009 · Emoluments on deputation · Rule 31(7)
Pay drawn while on deputation to a State Government is:
  1. A ignored altogether for pension purposes — It is not ignored; the counterfactual Central pay is substituted for it
  2. B treated as emoluments only if the deputation exceeded one year — There is no duration condition in rule 31(7)
  3. C not treated as emoluments; the pay he would have drawn under the Central Government is treated as emoluments
  4. D treated as emoluments, because it is the pay actually drawn
Answer and reasoning
( C) not treated as emoluments; the pay he would have drawn under the Central Government is treated as emoluments. (D) treated as emoluments, because it is the pay actually drawn. — Actual drawal does not decide the question; rule 31(6) and 31(7) split ex-cadre from State deputation. Rule 31(6) treats pay drawn on deputation to an ex-cadre post in the same or another Central Government Department, or to the Armed Forces, as emoluments. Rule 31(7) draws the opposite conclusion for deputation to a State Government or foreign service: that pay is not emoluments, and the pay the servant would have drawn under the Central Government is treated as emoluments instead. Exam-safe point: State deputation: substitute the Central pay; ex-cadre: actual pay counts. Statutory Authority: Rules 31(6) and 31(7), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-010 · Stagnation increment · Rule 31(1) Explanation
For the calculation of retirement benefits, a stagnation increment is:
  1. A excluded, because it is not basic pay
  2. B treated as emoluments
  3. C included only where it was actually drawn for ten months
  4. D included only for gratuity, not for pension
Answer and reasoning
( B) treated as emoluments. (A) excluded, because it is not basic pay. — The Explanation to rule 31(1) expressly includes it. (C) included only where it was actually drawn for ten months. — The ten-month averaging is a rule 32 question, not a condition on the Explanation. (D) included only for gratuity, not for pension. — The Explanation speaks of retirement benefits generally. Rule 31(1) defines emoluments as basic pay under rule 9(21)(a)(i) of the Fundamental Rules immediately before retirement or on the date of death, and adds non-practising allowance for a medical officer in lieu of private practice. The Explanation then provides that a stagnation increment shall be treated as emoluments for the calculation of retirement benefits. Exam-safe point: Stagnation increment counts as emoluments. Statutory Authority: Rule 31(1) and its Explanation, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-037 · Pay on deputation · Rule 31(6)
Pay drawn by a Government servant while on deputation to an ex-cadre post in another Department, or to the Armed Forces of India, is treated as emoluments:
  1. A not at all, since emoluments mean the pay of the parent post
  2. B only if the deputation was outside India
  3. C only if the borrowing Department bears the pension liability
  4. D for the purpose of calculating pension and gratuity
Answer and reasoning
( D) for the purpose of calculating pension and gratuity. (A) not at all, since emoluments mean the pay of the parent post. — The sub-rule brings deputation pay in as emoluments. (B) only if the deputation was outside India. — No such condition appears in the sub-rule. (C) only if the borrowing Department bears the pension liability. — The rule concerns the pay reckoned, not who pays. Rule 31(6) provides that pay drawn by a Government servant while on deputation to an ex-cadre post in the same or some other Department of the Government, or to the Armed Forces of India, shall be treated as emoluments for the purpose of calculating pension and gratuity. Exam-safe point: Deputation pay counts as emoluments. Statutory Authority: Rule 31(6), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
