Chapter V — Classes of Pension and Conditions Governing their Grant (142 questions)

PF-006 · Medical certificate of incapacity · Rule 39(8)
The medical authority's certificate of incapacity for service, leading to invalid pension, is issued in:
  1. A Format 3
  2. B Form 6
  3. C Format 6
  4. D Form 5
Answer and reasoning
( C) Format 6. (A) Format 3. — Format 3 is the memorandum of charges. (B) Form 6. — Form 6 is a different instrument again; the incapacity certificate is a Format. (D) Form 5. — Form 5 is a medical certificate, but under the leave rules, not this one. Rule 39(8) requires the medical authority to issue a Medical Certificate in Format 6, and if the servant is found unfit for further service, invalid pension may be granted under rule 44 not later than forty five days from the receipt of that certificate. The forty-five-day period is the testable figure: it runs from the receipt of the Format 6 certificate, not from the application. Exam-safe point: Incapacity certificate: Format 6; invalid pension within 45 days of receipt. Statutory Authority: Rule 39(8), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-011 · Medical authority for invalid pension · Rule 39(3)
For a non-Gazetted servant whose pay exceeds ₹54,000 a month, the medical authority for invalid pension is:
  1. A any authorised medical attendant
  2. B a Medical Board
  3. C the Civil Surgeon alone
  4. D a District Medical Officer alone
Answer and reasoning
( B) a Medical Board. (A) any authorised medical attendant. — The attendant appears in the leave rules, not here. (C) the Civil Surgeon alone. — The Civil Surgeon route is for the other cases in rule 39(3)(b). (D) a District Medical Officer alone. — The District Medical Officer is within clause (b), not clause (a). Rule 39(3) fixes the authority by clause (a) and clause (b): a Medical Board for a Gazetted servant and for a non-Gazetted servant whose pay under rule 9(21) of the Fundamental Rules exceeds fifty-four thousand rupees a month; and the Civil Surgeon, a District Medical Officer, or a Medical Officer of equivalent status in other cases. Rule 39(7) adds that a lady doctor shall sit on the Board when a woman is examined. Exam-safe point: Medical Board above ₹54,000 and for all Gazetted servants. Statutory Authority: Rule 39(3) and (7), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-012 · Compassionate allowance decision · Rule 41(2)
Where a servant is dismissed, the competent authority must decide on a compassionate allowance:
  1. A not later than three months after the order imposing the penalty
  2. B at any time before the servant attains superannuation
  3. C only if the servant applies within ninety days
  4. D within six months of the order, in every case
Answer and reasoning
( A) not later than three months after the order imposing the penalty. (B) at any time before the servant attains superannuation. — Rule 41(2) sets a three-month limit. (C) only if the servant applies within ninety days. — The authority must act on its own motion or on the representation, within the same three months. (D) within six months of the order, in every case. — Six months is the rule 41(4) period, and only for penalties imposed before the rules commenced. Rule 41(1) forfeits pension and gratuity on dismissal or removal, subject to a compassionate allowance not exceeding two-thirds of the pension or gratuity that would have been admissible on superannuation retirement. Rule 41(2) requires the competent authority to decide the question on its own motion or on the servant's representation not later than three months after the penalty order. Rule 41(4) gives six months only where the penalty was imposed before the rules commenced. Exam-safe point: Three months for a live case; six months only for pre-commencement penalties. Statutory Authority: Rule 41(2) and (4), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-013 · Time limit for invalid pension · Rule 39(8)
Where a servant is found unfit for further service, invalid pension may be granted:
  1. A within six months of the medical certificate — Six months is not the period in rule 39(8)
  2. B within thirty days of the medical examination
  3. C within three months of the application for retirement
  4. D not later than forty five days from the date of receipt of the Format 6 certificate
Answer and reasoning
( D) not later than forty five days from the date of receipt of the Format 6 certificate. (B) within thirty days of the medical examination. — Thirty days is the period for requesting the examination under rule 39(3). (C) within three months of the application for retirement. — The trigger is the certificate, and the period is forty-five days. Rule 39(8) requires the medical authority to issue a Medical Certificate in Format 6 where the servant is found unfit for further service or fit only for less laborious work. Where he is found unfit, invalid pension may be granted under rule 44 not later than forty-five days from the date of receipt of that certificate. Rule 39(3) separately requires the Head of Office to request the examination within fifteen days and the examination to be held within thirty days. Exam-safe point: Invalid pension: forty-five days from receipt of Format 6. Statutory Authority: Rule 39(3) and (8), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-012 · Forfeiture after absorption in a PSU · Rule 37(29)(c) as substituted in 2025
After the amendment of 2025, where an employee absorbed in a public sector undertaking is dismissed from the undertaking for subsequent misconduct, his retirement benefits for the Government service:
  1. A are forfeited, and the undertaking's decision is subject to review by the administrative Ministry
  2. B are reduced by half but cannot be forfeited — The rule speaks of forfeiture, not reduction
  3. C are protected, because the Government service ended on absorption
  4. D are forfeited only if the Central Government separately dismisses him
Answer and reasoning
( A) are forfeited, and the undertaking's decision is subject to review by the administrative Ministry. (C) are protected, because the Government service ended on absorption. — That was the position before the 2025 amendment and is no longer the rule. (D) are forfeited only if the Central Government separately dismisses him. — The undertaking's order now operates on the Government service benefits. G.S.R. 340(E) dated 22 May 2025 substituted clause (c) of rule 37(29). Dismissal, removal or retrenchment from the public sector undertaking after absorption, for subsequent misconduct, now leads to forfeiture of the retirement benefits for the Government service as well, and the undertaking's decision is subject to review by the Ministry administratively concerned with it. The Explanation applies rules 7 and 8 read with rule 41 and sub-rule (5) of rule 44 analogously. Exam-safe point: Forfeiture now reaches the Government service benefits. Statutory Authority: Rule 37(29)(c), as substituted by G.S.R. 340(E) dated 22.05.2025
CU-013 · Autonomous bodies after the 2025 amendment · Rule 37(26)(c)
The 2025 amendment to rule 37(29)(c) changed the position for an employee absorbed in a public sector undertaking. What is the position for an employee absorbed in an autonomous body?
  1. A also changed, because the same clause governs both — The autonomous body provision is rule 37(26)(c) and was not amended
  2. B governed by the 2024 amendment instead — The 2024 amendment dealt with forms, not forfeiture
  3. C changed more strictly, because autonomous bodies are funded by the Government — No change was made to rule 37(26)(c)
  4. D unchanged: dismissal from the autonomous body does not amount to forfeiture of the retirement benefits for Government service
Answer and reasoning
( D) unchanged: dismissal from the autonomous body does not amount to forfeiture of the retirement benefits for Government service. The amendment of 2025 substituted clause (c) of sub-rule (29) only. Clause (c) of sub-rule (26), which deals with an employee absorbed in an autonomous body, still says that dismissal or removal from the body for subsequent misconduct shall not amount to forfeiture of the retirement benefits for the service rendered under the Government. Exam-safe point: PSU: forfeiture. Autonomous body: protection intact. Statutory Authority: Rules 37(29)(c) and 37(26)(c), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-038 · Relieving order on absorption · Rule 35(3)
A Government employee joins a State Government on immediate absorption. The relieving order is issued:
  1. A only after he joins the State Government — The order precedes the joining and fixes the period for it
  2. B orally, with the period confirmed by the State Government
  3. C in Format 5, and it must indicate the period within which he is to join the State Government
  4. D in Form 5, which is the family details form
Answer and reasoning
( C) in Format 5, and it must indicate the period within which he is to join the State Government. (B) orally, with the period confirmed by the State Government. — The rule requires a written order in Format 5. (D) in Form 5, which is the family details form. — Format 5 and Form 5 are different instruments; absorption uses the Format. Rule 35(3) requires the relieving order, in a case of immediate absorption, to be issued in Format 5, indicating the period within which the Government servant shall join the State Government. Its proviso allows the relieving authority to extend that period for reasons beyond the servant's control, recorded in writing. Exam-safe point: Format 5, with the joining period stated. Statutory Authority: Rule 35(3), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-039 · Joining period on absorption in a body · Rule 36(5)
Where a Government servant is absorbed in a corporation, company or body, the relieving order:
  1. A fixes no period, the matter being left to the corporation — The order must state the period
  2. B indicates the period within which he must join, which the relieving authority may extend for reasons beyond his control
  3. C must be issued in Form 6-A after the 2024 amendment — Form 6-A is the pension application form, not the relieving order
  4. D is unnecessary where the absorption is on immediate absorption basis — Rule 36(4) and (5) apply precisely to that case
Answer and reasoning
( B) indicates the period within which he must join, which the relieving authority may extend for reasons beyond his control. Rule 36(5) provides that the relieving order shall indicate the period within which the Government servant shall join the Corporation or Company or the Body, and its proviso allows the relieving authority to extend that period for reasons beyond the servant's control, recorded in writing. Exam-safe point: The relieving order states a period, extendable on record. Statutory Authority: Rule 36(5), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-040 · Invalidation and the 2016 Act · Rule 39(1)
Where a Government servant acquires a disability to which section 20 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 applies, his case is governed by:
  1. A the National Pension System rules
  2. B the provisions of that Act, read with these rules
  3. C these rules alone, the Act applying only to private employment
  4. D the CCS (Extraordinary Pension) Rules, 1939 in every case
Answer and reasoning
( B) the provisions of that Act, read with these rules. (A) the National Pension System rules. — The NPS rules govern post-2003 appointees. (C) these rules alone, the Act applying only to private employment. — Rule 39(1) expressly defers to the Act. (D) the CCS (Extraordinary Pension) Rules, 1939 in every case. — Those Rules apply to a different class of case. Rule 39(1) provides that the case of a Government servant acquiring a disability, where the provisions of section 20 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 are applicable, shall be governed by the provisions of that Act, read with these rules. Exam-safe point: Section 20 of the 2016 Act governs, read with the Rules. Statutory Authority: Rule 39(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-041 · Dismissal and forfeiture · Rule 41(1)
A Government servant dismissed or removed from service under the CCS (CCA) Rules:
  1. A forfeits his pension and gratuity
  2. B retains both, subject to a reduction ordered by the President
  3. C forfeits only the portion attributable to the period after the misconduct
  4. D retains his pension but forfeits gratuity
Answer and reasoning
( A) forfeits his pension and gratuity. (B) retains both, subject to a reduction ordered by the President. — Forfeiture is automatic; rule 41(2) allows a compassionate allowance in deserving cases. (C) forfeits only the portion attributable to the period after the misconduct. — The forfeiture is of pension and gratuity, not of a period. (D) retains his pension but forfeits gratuity. — Rule 41(1) forfeits both. Rule 41(1) provides that a Government servant who is dismissed or removed from service shall forfeit his pension and gratuity. The rule then allows the authority competent to dismiss or remove him to sanction a compassionate allowance in a deserving case, and rule 44(5) fixes its ceiling at two-thirds of the pension or gratuity that would have been admissible. Exam-safe point: Dismissal or removal forfeits pension and gratuity; compassionate allowance is the exception. Statutory Authority: Rule 41(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-053 · Invalidation: the medical board's opinion · Rule 39(9)
Where the medical authority finds the Government servant unfit for further service, the appointing authority:
  1. A may retain him in service against the medical finding
  2. B must refer the finding to the Union Public Service Commission
  3. C may invalidate him only after a second board confirms it
  4. D shall accept the finding and proceed to invalidate him, subject to the proviso
Answer and reasoning
( D) shall accept the finding and proceed to invalidate him, subject to the proviso. (A) may retain him in service against the medical finding. — The proviso deals only with a specific case, not a general power to disregard the finding. (B) must refer the finding to the Union Public Service Commission. — No such reference appears in the sub-rule. (C) may invalidate him only after a second board confirms it. — A second board is not required. Rule 39(9) deals with the course to be followed where the medical authority declares a Government servant unfit for further service, and its proviso carves out the case in which the Government servant may be retained or dealt with otherwise. The invalid pension that follows is calculated under rule 44 with the concession in the proviso to rule 44(1). Exam-safe point: The finding is acted on, subject only to the proviso. Statutory Authority: Rule 39(9), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
TX-0164 · Clause (a) of sub-rule (1) of rule 34 · Rule 34 · 34(1)(a)
Which of the following is the text of clause (a) of sub-rule (1) of rule 34?
  1. A who retires on his own volition, before attaining the age of superannuation, in accordance with the provisions of rule 43 of these rules, or rule 56 of the Fundamental Rules; or
  2. B The Directorate of Estates shall also inform the Head of Office the amount of licence fee for the retention of Government accommodation for the permissible period beyond the date of retirement of the allottee and the Head of Office shall adjust the amount of that licence fee from the amount of the gratuity together with the unrecovered licence fee, if any, mentioned in sub-rule (3).
  3. C the process specified in sub-clauses (i), (ii), (iii), (iv) and (v) shall be completed eight months before the date of superannuation;
  4. D If the amount of provisional gratuity disbursed by the Head of Office under sub-rule (3) is more than the amount finally assessed, the retired Government servant shall not be required to refund the excess amount actually disbursed to him.
Answer and reasoning
( A) who retires on his own volition, before attaining the age of superannuation, in accordance with the provisions of rule 43 of these rules, or rule 56 of the Fundamental Rules; or. (B) The Directorate of Estates shall also inform the Head of Office the amount of licence fee for the retention of Government accommodation for the permissible period beyond the date of retirement of the allottee and the Head of Office shall adjust the amount of that licence fee from the amount of the gratuity together with the unrecovered licence fee, if any, mentioned in sub-rule (3). — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. (C) the process specified in sub-clauses (i), (ii), (iii), (iv) and (v) shall be completed eight months before the date of superannuation;. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. (D) If the amount of provisional gratuity disbursed by the Head of Office under sub-rule (3) is more than the amount finally assessed, the retired Government servant shall not be required to refund the excess amount actually disbursed to him. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. The answer reproduces the provision as notified. The three wrong options are other provisions of the same rules, so the question tests recall of this provision rather than recognition of the statute's style. Exam-safe point: clause (a) of sub-rule (1) of rule 34 of rule 34, in its own words. Statutory Authority: Clause (a) of sub-rule (1) of rule 34, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
TX-0165 · Clause (b) of sub-rule (1) of rule 34 · Rule 34 · 34(1)(b)
Which of the following is the text of clause (b) of sub-rule (1) of rule 34?
  1. A furnish to the retiring Government servant a certificate regarding the length of qualifying service proposed to be admitted for the purpose of pension and gratuity and also the emoluments and the average emoluments proposed to be reckoned for retirement gratuity and pension; — It is the text of a different provision of these rules
  2. B The Accounts Officer shall also indicate in the Pension Payment Order, the names of the permanently disabled child or children and dependent parents and disabled siblings as family pensioners if there is no other member of family to whom family pension may become payable before such disabled child or children or dependent parents or disabled siblings.
  3. C a notification in the Official Gazette in the case of a Gazetted Government servant; or — It is the text of a different provision of these rules
  4. D who, on being declared surplus, opts for voluntary retirement in accordance with the provisions of the Special Voluntary Retirement Scheme for surplus employees notified by the Department of Personnel and Training vide Office Memorandum No. 25013/6/2001-Estt.(A), dated the 28th February, 2002, as amended from time to time; or

The answer reproduces the provision as notified. The three wrong options are other provisions of the same rules, so the question tests recall of this provision rather than recognition of the statute's style. Exam-safe point: clause (b) of sub-rule (1) of rule 34 of rule 34, in its own words. Statutory Authority: Clause (b) of sub-rule (1) of rule 34, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
TX-0166 · Clause (c) of sub-rule (1) of rule 34 · Rule 34 · 34(1)(c)
Which of the following is the text of clause (c) of sub-rule (1) of rule 34?
  1. A Any dues relating to damages in respect of the Government accommodation shall be recovered from the death gratuity payable to the family and if the Government accommodation is retained by the family of the deceased Government servant, the licence fee for the month in which the Government servant has died and the first three months thereafter, shall not be recovered from the family.
  2. B copies of Form 4, Form 6 and an undertaking to the Bank in Format 9, signed and submitted by the Government servant; — It is the text of a different provision of these rules
  3. C who is retired by the Government, before attaining the age of superannuation, in accordance with the provisions of rule 42 of these rules or rule 56 of the Fundamental Rules.
  4. D Provided that no interest under this sub-rule shall be payable if the delay in payment was caused on account of failure on the part of the Government servant or the pensioner or the member of the family of the Government servant to comply with the procedure laid down by the Government for processing the pension or family pension case.

(A) Any dues relating to damages in respect of the Government accommodation shall be recovered from the death gratuity payable to the family and if the Government accommodation is retained by the family of the deceased Government servant, the licence fee for the month in which the Government servant has died and the first three months thereafter, shall not be recovered from the family. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. (D) Provided that no interest under this sub-rule shall be payable if the delay in payment was caused on account of failure on the part of the Government servant or the pensioner or the member of the family of the Government servant to comply with the procedure laid down by the Government for processing the pension or family pension case. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. The answer reproduces the provision as notified. The three wrong options are other provisions of the same rules, so the question tests recall of this provision rather than recognition of the statute's style. Exam-safe point: clause (c) of sub-rule (1) of rule 34 of rule 34, in its own words. Statutory Authority: Clause (c) of sub-rule (1) of rule 34, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
TX-0167 · Clause (ii) of sub-rule (2) of rule 35 · Rule 35 · 35(2)(ii)
Clause (ii) of sub-rule (2) of rule 35 of the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 begins with which words?
  1. A If, after the particulars of Government dues have been intimated to the Accounts Officer under sub-rule (2) of rule 60, any additional Government dues come to the notice of the Head of Office, such dues shall be promptly reported to the Accounts Officer.
  2. B In order to decide the eligibility for family pension, a member of the family, other than the widow or widower of the deceased Government servant or pensioner, shall be required to submit, along with the claim for family pension, the documents referred to in the clause (b) of sub-rule (12) of rule 50.
  3. C in case a Government employee initially joins a State Government on deputation, the date from which his unqualified resignation is accepted by the Central Government.
  4. D Where the administrative Ministry or Department decides not to waive off the excess payment of pension or family pension, the retired Government servant concerned or family pensioner shall be served with a notice by the Head of Office requiring him to refund the excess payment within a period of two months from the date of receipt of notice by him.

( C) in case a Government employee initially joins a State Government on deputation, the date from which his unqualified resignation is accepted by the Central Government. (A) If, after the particulars of Government dues have been intimated to the Accounts Officer under sub-rule (2) of rule 60, any additional Government dues come to the notice of the Head of Office, such dues shall be promptly reported to the Accounts Officer. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. (B) In order to decide the eligibility for family pension, a member of the family, other than the widow or widower of the deceased Government servant or pensioner, shall be required to submit, along with the claim for family pension, the documents referred to in the clause (b) of sub-rule (12) of rule 50. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. (D) Where the administrative Ministry or Department decides not to waive off the excess payment of pension or family pension, the retired Government servant concerned or family pensioner shall be served with a notice by the Head of Office requiring him to refund the excess payment within a period of two months from the date of receipt of notice by him. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. The answer reproduces the provision as notified. The three wrong options are other provisions of the same rules, so the question tests recall of this provision rather than recognition of the statute's style. Exam-safe point: clause (ii) of sub-rule (2) of rule 35 of rule 35, in its own words. Statutory Authority: Clause (ii) of sub-rule (2) of rule 35, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
TX-0168 · The proviso to sub-rule (3) of rule 35 · Rule 35 · 35(3)#P1
Which of the following is the text of the proviso to sub-rule (3) of rule 35?
  1. A In the case of a Government servant who has retired or is retiring otherwise than on attaining the age of superannuation, the Directorate of Estates shall inform the Head of Office within one month from the date of receipt of intimation and details from Head of Office under sub-rule (2) of rule 55, if any licence fee was recoverable from the Government servant up to the date of retirement.
  2. B Provided that this period may be extended by the relieving authority for reasons beyond the control of the Government servant, which shall be recorded in writing.
  3. C The process of determination of qualifying service and qualifying emoluments shall be completed within one month of the receipt of intimation or information regarding the death of the Government servant or within one month of the receipt of intimation regarding disappearance of the Government servant, as the case may be.

(C) The process of determination of qualifying service and qualifying emoluments shall be completed within one month of the receipt of intimation or information regarding the death of the Government servant or within one month of the receipt of intimation regarding disappearance of the Government servant, as the case may be. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. (D) The amount of provisional pension and gratuity payable under sub-rule (2) or sub-rule (3) shall, if necessary, be revised on the completion of the detailed scrutiny of the records. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. The answer reproduces the provision as notified. The three wrong options are other provisions of the same rules, so the question tests recall of this provision rather than recognition of the statute's style. Exam-safe point: the proviso to sub-rule (3) of rule 35 of rule 35, in its own words. Statutory Authority: The proviso to sub-rule (3) of rule 35, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
TX-0169 · Sub-rule (4) of rule 35 · Rule 35 · 35(4)
Which of the following is the text of sub-rule (4) of rule 35?

The answer reproduces the provision as notified. The three wrong options are other provisions of the same rules, so the question tests recall of this provision rather than recognition of the statute's style. Exam-safe point: sub-rule (4) of rule 35 of rule 35, in its own words. Statutory Authority: Sub-rule (4) of rule 35, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
TX-0170 · Sub-rule (5) of rule 35 · Rule 35 · 35(5)
Which of the following is the text of sub-rule (5) of rule 35?
  1. A The Head of Office shall inform the Accounts Officer as soon as provisional family pension has been paid for a period mentioned in sub-rule (3) or for the period extended under proviso to sub-rule (1) of rule 76, as the case may be.

The answer reproduces the provision as notified. The three wrong options are other provisions of the same rules, so the question tests recall of this provision rather than recognition of the statute's style. Exam-safe point: sub-rule (5) of rule 35 of rule 35, in its own words. Statutory Authority: Sub-rule (5) of rule 35, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
TX-0171 · Clause (a) of sub-rule (6) of rule 35 · Rule 35 · 35(6)(a)
Which of the following is the text of clause (a) of sub-rule (6) of rule 35?
  1. A The Head of Office shall also address the eligible member of the family or the guardian, as the case may be, in Format 12 for making a claim for family pension in Form 10.

Answer and reasoning

Chapter VI — Premature Retirement and Voluntary Retirement (27 questions)

PS-014 · Voluntary retirement and fractional service · Rule 43(1) fourth proviso
A servant with 19 years and 10 months of qualifying service seeks voluntary retirement under rule 43. He:
  1. A is eligible, since 19 years and 10 months rounds up to 20 years
  2. B is eligible if the appointing authority condones the shortfall
  3. C is not eligible, because the rule 44(7) rounding of three months or more does not apply to rule 43
  4. D is eligible only if he gives six months' notice
Answer and reasoning
( C) is not eligible, because the rule 44(7) rounding of three months or more does not apply to rule 43. (A) is eligible, since 19 years and 10 months rounds up to 20 years. — The fourth proviso expressly disapplies the rounding for rule 43. (B) is eligible if the appointing authority condones the shortfall. — There is no condonation route in rule 43 for the twenty-year requirement. (D) is eligible only if he gives six months' notice. — Notice length is not the obstacle; the qualifying service is. Rule 43(1) allows voluntary retirement after twenty years' qualifying service on three months' notice. Its fourth proviso requires that the servant has completed, or will complete, twenty years on the intended date of retirement, and expressly disapplies rule 44(7), under which a fraction of three months or more is treated as a completed six-monthly period. Nineteen years and ten months therefore falls short, and the rule 44(8) concession of nine years and nine months is confined to pension on invalid retirement. Exam-safe point: Twenty years exact for rule 43; no rounding under rule 44(7). Statutory Authority: Rule 43(1) fourth proviso, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-015 · Curtailed notice and commutation · Rule 43(4)(b)
Where the appointing authority relaxes the three-month notice under rule 43(4), the condition is that the servant:
  1. A shall serve the balance of the notice after retirement — That would contradict the relaxation itself
  2. B shall not receive retirement gratuity until the notice period ends
  3. C shall not apply for commutation of a part of his pension before the expiry of the three-month notice period
  4. D shall forfeit one month's pension — No forfeiture of pension is prescribed
Answer and reasoning
( C) shall not apply for commutation of a part of his pension before the expiry of the three-month notice period. (B) shall not receive retirement gratuity until the notice period ends. — The bar in the rule is on commutation, not on gratuity. Rule 43(4)(a) allows a request for acceptance of less than three months' notice with reasons; clause (b) lets the appointing authority relax the notice where the curtailment causes no administrative inconvenience, on the condition that the servant shall not apply for commutation of a part of his pension before the expiry of the three-month notice period. Commutation is governed by the CCS (Commutation of Pension) Rules, 1981 under rule 84(2). Exam-safe point: Curtailed notice: no commutation until the three months would have run. Statutory Authority: Rule 43(4)(b), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-016 · Withholding permission to retire · Rule 43(3)
Which circumstance does NOT entitle the appointing authority to withhold permission to retire under rule 43?
  1. A A charge sheet has been issued and disciplinary proceedings are pending
  2. B The servant has applied for an advance of pay
  3. C Judicial proceedings on charges of grave misconduct are pending
  4. D The servant is under suspension
Answer and reasoning
( B) The servant has applied for an advance of pay. (A) A charge sheet has been issued and disciplinary proceedings are pending. — Clause (ii) covers pending disciplinary proceedings. (C) Judicial proceedings on charges of grave misconduct are pending. — Clause (iii) covers them, and the Explanation defines when they are pending. (D) The servant is under suspension. — Clause (i) of rule 43(3) covers suspension. Rule 43(3) allows permission to be withheld in three circumstances: suspension; a charge sheet issued with disciplinary proceedings pending; and judicial proceedings on charges which may amount to grave misconduct. The Explanation treats judicial proceedings as pending once a complaint or police report of which the Magistrate takes cognizance has been made. Even in those cases, the proviso permits acceptance with the approval of the President. Exam-safe point: Three grounds for withholding; the President's approval can override them. Statutory Authority: Rule 43(3) and its Explanation, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-042 · Acceptance of voluntary retirement notice · Rule 43(2)
A notice of voluntary retirement given under rule 43(1):
  1. A must be accepted within thirty days or it lapses
  2. B may be accepted with effect from an earlier date at the authority's discretion
  3. C takes effect on the date stated in it without acceptance
  4. D requires acceptance by the appointing authority
Answer and reasoning
( D) requires acceptance by the appointing authority. (A) must be accepted within thirty days or it lapses. — The rule fixes no such period. (B) may be accepted with effect from an earlier date at the authority's discretion. — Acceptance cannot advance the date. (C) takes effect on the date stated in it without acceptance. — Rule 43(2) requires acceptance, subject to its proviso. Rule 43(2) provides that the notice of voluntary retirement given under sub-rule (1) shall require acceptance by the appointing authority. Its proviso deals with the case where the appointing authority does not refuse the request before the expiry of the notice period, in which case the retirement takes effect on the date of its expiry. Exam-safe point: Acceptance is required; silence until expiry operates as it. Statutory Authority: Rule 43(2), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-043 · Withdrawal of the notice · Rule 43(6)
A Government servant who has given notice of voluntary retirement wishes to withdraw it. He:
  1. A may withdraw it at any time before the date of retirement
  2. B may withdraw it only with the consent of the President
  3. C is precluded from withdrawing it except with the approval of the appointing authority
  4. D cannot withdraw it in any circumstances — The rule permits withdrawal with approval
Answer and reasoning
( C) is precluded from withdrawing it except with the approval of the appointing authority. (A) may withdraw it at any time before the date of retirement. — Rule 43(6) restricts withdrawal to a case approved by the appointing authority. (B) may withdraw it only with the consent of the President. — The approving authority is the appointing authority. Rule 43(6) provides that a Government servant who has elected to retire under the rule and has given the necessary notice to that effect to the appointing authority shall be precluded from withdrawing his notice except with the specific approval of that authority. Exam-safe point: Withdrawal needs the appointing authority's specific approval. Statutory Authority: Rule 43(6), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-054 · Voluntary retirement: the notice period · Rule 43(3)(iii)
A notice of voluntary retirement given by a Government servant:
  1. A may be given at any time, the period being fixed by the appointing authority — The rule fixes the period
  2. B may be given one month before that date — Three months is the period in the rule
  3. C must be given at least three months before the date on which he wishes the retirement to take effect
  4. D must be given six months before that date
Answer and reasoning
( C) must be given at least three months before the date on which he wishes the retirement to take effect. (D) must be given six months before that date. — Six months is the rule 57 period for pension papers, not the notice of retirement. Rule 43(3) sets out what the notice of voluntary retirement must contain and the period it must be given before the intended date. The appointing authority may, under the rule, accept the notice with a shorter period in a case where it is satisfied that the circumstances justify it. Exam-safe point: Three months' notice, and the authority may accept a shorter one. Statutory Authority: Rule 43(3), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021

(D) The Government servants who have worked in any Intelligence or Security-related organisation included in the Second Schedule to the Right to Information Act, 2005 (22 of 2005), shall give an undertaking in regard to the above restriction in Format 1 and any failure to observe such an undertaking on. — These are the opening words of a different provision of the same rules. The answer is the provision's own opening words, cut at a sentence boundary. The other options are the opening words of other provisions, so the question tests recall of how this provision begins. Exam-safe point: sub-rule (5) of rule 43 opens in these words. Statutory Authority: Sub-rule (5) of rule 43, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021

Chapter VII — Regulation of Pension and Gratuity (104 questions)

PC-001 · Pension at 50 per cent · Rule 44(1)
A servant retires on superannuation after 33 years' qualifying service. His emoluments are ₹86,000 and his average emoluments ₹84,000. His pension under rule 44(1) is:
  1. A ₹43,000 a month
  2. B ₹1,25,000 a month, the ceiling
  3. C ₹42,000 a month
  4. D ₹86,000 a month, the last emoluments in full
Answer and reasoning
( A) ₹43,000 a month. (B) ₹1,25,000 a month, the ceiling. — The ceiling is not a rate; it caps a figure that reaches it. (C) ₹42,000 a month. — That is 50 per cent of the average emoluments, which is the lower figure; the rule takes the more beneficial. (D) ₹86,000 a month, the last emoluments in full. — The pension is 50 per cent of the emoluments, not the emoluments. Rule 44(1) takes 50 per cent of emoluments or of average emoluments, whichever is more beneficial. Emoluments are ₹86,000, so 50 per cent is ₹43,000. Average emoluments are ₹84,000, so 50 per cent is ₹42,000. The larger is ₹43,000, and it lies between the floor of ₹9,000 and the ceiling of ₹1,25,000, so it is the pension. Exam-safe point: Rule 44(1): 50% of the higher of emoluments and average emoluments. Statutory Authority: Rule 44(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PC-002 · Pension — the floor · Rule 44(1)
A servant retires with ten years' qualifying service and emoluments of ₹16,000. His pension under rule 44(1) is:
  1. A ₹9,000 a month, the minimum
  2. B ₹8,000 a month
  3. C No pension is admissible below ₹20,000 of emoluments
  4. D ₹16,000 a month
Answer and reasoning
( A) ₹9,000 a month, the minimum. (B) ₹8,000 a month. — That is 50 per cent of ₹16,000, but the rule puts a floor under it. (C) No pension is admissible below ₹20,000 of emoluments. — There is no such threshold; the floor operates on the pension, not on the pay. (D) ₹16,000 a month. — The pension is 50 per cent, not the full emoluments. Fifty per cent of ₹16,000 is ₹8,000. Rule 44(1) fixes a minimum of ₹9,000 a month, so the pension is lifted to ₹9,000. The floor is on the amount of pension, not on the emoluments, so a question that offers a pay threshold has invented a rule. Exam-safe point: Floor: ₹9,000 on the pension amount, not on the pay. Statutory Authority: Rule 44(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PC-003 · Pension — the ceiling · Rule 44(1)
A servant retires with emoluments of ₹3,00,000. His pension under rule 44(1) is:
  1. A ₹2,50,000 a month
  2. B ₹75,000 a month
  3. C ₹1,50,000 a month
  4. D ₹1,25,000 a month, the maximum
Answer and reasoning
( D) ₹1,25,000 a month, the maximum. (A) ₹2,50,000 a month. — That is not a figure in the rule at all. (B) ₹75,000 a month. — Seventy-five thousand is the ordinary ceiling for family pension, not for pension. (C) ₹1,50,000 a month. — That is 50 per cent of the emoluments, but the ceiling cuts it back. Fifty per cent of ₹3,00,000 is ₹1,50,000, which is above the maximum of ₹1,25,000 a month fixed by rule 44(1). The pension is therefore ₹1,25,000. The ceiling and the floor are both in sub-rule (1), and the paper likes to offer the family pension ceiling of ₹75,000 alongside them. Exam-safe point: Ceiling: ₹1,25,000 on pension; ₹75,000 belongs to family pension. Statutory Authority: Rule 44(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PC-004 · Nine years nine months · Rule 44(8)
A servant retires with exactly nine years and nine months of qualifying service. Under rule 44(8):
  1. A He gets service gratuity, because he has less than ten years
  2. B His qualifying service is nine years and six months after rounding
  3. C His qualifying service is treated as ten years and he is eligible for pension
  4. D He gets nothing, because the minimum is ten years
Answer and reasoning
( C) His qualifying service is treated as ten years and he is eligible for pension. (A) He gets service gratuity, because he has less than ten years. — Sub-rule (8) exists to prevent exactly that result. (B) His qualifying service is nine years and six months after rounding. — The rounding is upward to ten years, not downward. (D) He gets nothing, because the minimum is ten years. — He is inside the sub-rule (8) rounding, so he is eligible. Rule 44(8) provides that a servant who has rendered nine years and nine months or more but less than ten years shall have his qualifying service treated as ten years and shall be eligible for pension under sub-rule (1). Read it with rule 44(7), which treats a fraction of three months and above as a completed six-monthly period: the two together convert what looks like a shortfall into an entitlement. Exam-safe point: 9 years 9 months or more: treat as 10, pension admissible. Statutory Authority: Rule 44(8), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PC-005 · Service gratuity · Rule 44(2)
A servant retires after eight years of qualifying service with emoluments of ₹40,000. He is entitled to:
  1. A Nothing, because he has not completed ten years
  2. B Service gratuity of ₹3,20,000
  3. C Pension of ₹20,000 a month
  4. D Retirement gratuity of ₹1,60,000
Answer and reasoning
( B) Service gratuity of ₹3,20,000. (A) Nothing, because he has not completed ten years. — Rule 44(2) gives service gratuity precisely for that case. (C) Pension of ₹20,000 a month. — Pension needs ten years; eight years brings service gratuity. (D) Retirement gratuity of ₹1,60,000. — That is the rule 45 computation; with under ten years it is service gratuity under rule 44(2). Eight years is sixteen completed six-monthly periods. Rule 44(2) computes service gratuity at half a month's emoluments for every completed six-monthly period: ₹40,000 ÷ 2 = ₹20,000, times 16 = ₹3,20,000. This is the case rule 44(2) exists for — a servant who retires without reaching the ten years that pension requires. Exam-safe point: Service gratuity: half a month's emoluments per six-monthly period. Statutory Authority: Rule 44(2), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PC-006 · Additional pension · Rule 44(6)
A pensioner drawing a basic pension of ₹30,000 attains the age of 87. His additional pension is:
  1. A ₹12,000 — 40 per cent of basic pension
  2. B ₹9,000 — 30 per cent of basic pension
  3. C ₹30,000 — 100 per cent of basic pension
  4. D ₹6,000 — 20 per cent of basic pension
Answer and reasoning
( B) ₹9,000 — 30 per cent of basic pension. (A) ₹12,000 — 40 per cent of basic pension. — Forty per cent starts at 90. (C) ₹30,000 — 100 per cent of basic pension. — One hundred per cent starts at 100 years. (D) ₹6,000 — 20 per cent of basic pension. — Twenty per cent is the 80-to-85 band; at 87 he is in the 85-to-90 band. Rule 44(6) adds a percentage of basic pension by age band: 20 per cent from 80 to under 85, 30 per cent from 85 to under 90, 40 per cent from 90 to under 95, 50 per cent from 95 to under 100, and 100 per cent at 100 or more. At 87 the band is 85 to 90, so the addition is 30 per cent of ₹30,000, which is ₹9,000. Sub-rule (6)(b) makes it payable from the first day of the month in which it falls due. Exam-safe point: Additional pension bands: 20/30/40/50/100 per cent by age. Statutory Authority: Rule 44(6), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PC-007 · Fraction of a year · Rule 44(7)
A servant has 27 years and 4 months of qualifying service. For pension, the qualifying service is treated as:
  1. A 27 years and 6 months — the 4 months is a completed six-monthly period
  2. B 28 years — the fraction rounds up to a full year
  3. C 27 years and 4 months, counted to the month
  4. D 27 years exactly — the fraction is ignored
Answer and reasoning
( A) 27 years and 6 months — the 4 months is a completed six-monthly period. (B) 28 years — the fraction rounds up to a full year. — The rounding is to a six-monthly period, not to a year. (C) 27 years and 4 months, counted to the month. — Pension counts completed six-monthly periods, not months. (D) 27 years exactly — the fraction is ignored. — Rule 44(7) does not ignore three months or more; it promotes it. Rule 44(7) provides that in calculating the length of qualifying service, a fraction of a year equal to three months and above shall be treated as a completed six-monthly period. Four months is three months or above, so it becomes a six-monthly period, and the service is 27 years and 6 months — that is, 55 completed six-monthly periods. A fraction of less than three months would simply be dropped. Exam-safe point: Three months or more: one more six-monthly period. Less than three: dropped. Statutory Authority: Rule 44(7), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PC-008 · Rounding the pension · Rule 44(9)
A pension works out to ₹24,750.60. Under rule 44(9) it is expressed as:
  1. A ₹24,750.60, carried to the paise
  2. B ₹24,750
  3. C ₹24,760
  4. D ₹24,751
Answer and reasoning
( D) ₹24,751. (A) ₹24,750.60, carried to the paise. — The rule requires whole rupees. (B) ₹24,750. — The rule rounds to the next higher rupee, not to the nearest. (C) ₹24,760. — That rounds to the next ten rupees, which the rule does not do. Rule 44(9) requires the amount finally determined to be expressed in whole rupees, and any fraction of a rupee to be rounded off to the next higher rupee. ₹24,750.60 therefore becomes ₹24,751. Note that this is rounding up, not rounding to the nearest: ₹24,750.10 would also become ₹24,751. Sub-rule (10) applies the same rounding where pension is discontinued mid-month. Exam-safe point: Pension rounding: always to the next higher rupee. Statutory Authority: Rule 44(9), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PC-009 · Retirement gratuity · Rule 45(1)(a)
A servant retires after 32 years and 5 months of qualifying service with emoluments of ₹60,000. His retirement gratuity is:
  1. A ₹4,87,500
  2. B ₹9,90,000, the 16½-times cap
  3. C ₹9,75,000
  4. D ₹9,60,000
Answer and reasoning
( C) ₹9,75,000. (A) ₹4,87,500. — That uses one-eighth instead of one-quarter of emoluments. (B) ₹9,90,000, the 16½-times cap. — The cap is the ceiling, not the computation; on these figures the computation is lower. (D) ₹9,60,000. — That treats the 5 months as dropped; at three months or more it becomes a six-monthly period. Thirty-two years and five months gives 64 completed six-monthly periods, plus one because rule 45(4) treats a fraction of three months or more as a completed six-monthly period — 65 in all. Rule 45(1)(a) pays one-fourth of emoluments per period: ₹60,000 ÷ 4 = ₹15,000, times 65 = ₹9,75,000. The cap is 16½ times emoluments, ₹9,90,000, which is not reached, so ₹9,75,000 is the gratuity. Exam-safe point: Gratuity: one-quarter per six-monthly period, capped at 16½ times emoluments. Statutory Authority: Rule 45(1)(a) and (4), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PC-010 · Death gratuity — the middle slabs · Rule 45(1)(b)
A servant dies in service after 7 years and 2 months of qualifying service. His emoluments were ₹50,000. The death gratuity is:
  1. A ₹3,00,000
  2. B ₹1,50,000
  3. C ₹6,00,000
  4. D ₹10,00,000
Answer and reasoning
( C) ₹6,00,000. (A) ₹3,00,000. — That is the 2-times rate for under one year. (B) ₹1,50,000. — That is the service gratuity pattern, not death gratuity. (D) ₹10,00,000. — That is the 20-times rate for 11 years or more. Seven years and two months is fourteen completed six-monthly periods. The table in rule 45(1)(b) gives 12 times emoluments for 5 years or more but less than 11 years. Twelve times ₹50,000 is ₹6,00,000, and it is below the ₹20 lakh ceiling, so that is the gratuity. The slabs are 2, 6, 12, 20 times, and then half of emoluments per completed period capped at 33 times. Exam-safe point: Death gratuity slabs: 2 / 6 / 12 / 20 times, then half per period to 33. Statutory Authority: Rule 45(1)(b), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PC-011 · Death gratuity — the top slab · Rule 45(1)(b)
A servant dies in service after 21 years of qualifying service with emoluments of ₹70,000. The death gratuity is:
  1. A ₹14,00,000
  2. B ₹14,70,000
  3. C ₹16,80,000
  4. D ₹23,10,000, the 33-times cap
Answer and reasoning
( B) ₹14,70,000. (A) ₹14,00,000. — That is 20 times, which is the band below 20 years; at 21 years the half-per-period rate applies. (C) ₹16,80,000. — That computes 24 periods rather than 21. (D) ₹23,10,000, the 33-times cap. — The cap is not the rate; the computation gives less. Twenty-one years is 42 completed six-monthly periods. At 20 years or more the table gives half of emoluments for every completed six-monthly period, subject to a maximum of 33 times emoluments: ₹70,000 ÷ 2 = ₹35,000, times 42 = ₹14,70,000. The cap of 33 times is ₹23,10,000, which is not reached, so the computation stands. Exam-safe point: Top slab: half of emoluments per period, capped at 33 times. Statutory Authority: Rule 45(1)(b), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PC-012 · Residuary gratuity · Rule 45(3)
The residuary gratuity under rule 45(3) is payable where a pensioner dies within five years of retirement and the sums received together with the retirement gratuity and commuted value fall short of:
  1. A Twelve times his emoluments
  2. B Ten times his emoluments
  3. C Sixteen and a half times his emoluments
  4. D Thirty-three times his emoluments
Answer and reasoning
( A) Twelve times his emoluments. (B) Ten times his emoluments. — The figure in rule 45(3) is twelve. (C) Sixteen and a half times his emoluments. — That is the retirement gratuity cap, not the residuary benchmark. (D) Thirty-three times his emoluments. — That is the death gratuity cap. Rule 45(3) measures the shortfall against twelve times his emoluments. If the pension and gratuity actually received, together with the retirement gratuity and the commuted value of any commuted portion, come to less than twelve times emoluments, a residuary gratuity equal to the deficiency is paid to the family. The figure to hold is twelve, and it is a benchmark for this one calculation only. Exam-safe point: Residuary gratuity: the deficiency below twelve times emoluments. Statutory Authority: Rule 45(3), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PC-013 · Four years nine months · Rule 45(5)
A servant retires with four years and nine months of qualifying service. For retirement gratuity under rule 45(5):
  1. A He gets service gratuity only, because he is below five years
  2. B He gets nothing, because five years is the minimum
  3. C His service is rounded down to four years — The rounding is upward, to five years
  4. D His qualifying service is treated as five years and he is eligible for retirement gratuity
Answer and reasoning
( D) His qualifying service is treated as five years and he is eligible for retirement gratuity. (A) He gets service gratuity only, because he is below five years. — Sub-rule (5) treats him as having five years for this purpose. (B) He gets nothing, because five years is the minimum. — The minimum is reached by the deeming in sub-rule (5). Rule 45(5) provides that a servant who has rendered four years and nine months or more but less than five years shall have his qualifying service treated as five years for the purpose of this rule and shall be eligible for retirement gratuity under clause (a) of sub-rule (1). It mirrors rule 44(8), which does the same at nine years nine months for pension. The pattern to learn is the nine-month shortfall, at both thresholds. Exam-safe point: 4 years 9 months = 5 years for gratuity; 9 years 9 months = 10 years for pension. Statutory Authority: Rule 45(5), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PF-002 · Nomination for gratuity · Rule 46(1)
A Government servant, on initial appointment, makes a nomination for retirement and death gratuity in:
  1. A Form 1
  2. B Form 3
  3. C Form 9
  4. D Format 3
Answer and reasoning
( B) Form 3. (A) Form 1. — Form 1 is the application for commercial employment. (C) Form 9. — Form 9 is the claim a family member submits for gratuity. (D) Format 3. — Format 3 is the memorandum of charges to a pensioner under rule 8. Rule 46(1) requires a Government servant, on his initial appointment, to make a nomination in Form 3 conferring on one or more persons the right to receive the retirement gratuity and death gratuity payable under rule 45. The nomination goes to the Head of Office, who verifies and countersigns it under rule 46(9)(b) and has an entry made in the service book. Exam-safe point: Nomination: Form 3, filed on initial appointment. Statutory Authority: Rule 46(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PF-008 · Minor's share of gratuity · Rule 47(7)
Where there is no natural guardian, up to twenty per cent of a minor's share of gratuity may be paid on:
  1. A A succession certificate
  2. B An indemnity bond in Format 7
  3. C An affidavit sworn before a Magistrate
  4. D A guardianship certificate, which is always required
Answer and reasoning
( B) An indemnity bond in Format 7. (A) A succession certificate. — A succession certificate is the rule 49 route where there is no family and no nomination. (C) An affidavit sworn before a Magistrate. — The instrument is an indemnity bond, and it is a Format. (D) A guardianship certificate, which is always required. — The rule 47(7) procedure exists to allow payment without one, up to twenty per cent. Rule 47(7) allows payment of an amount not exceeding twenty per cent of the minor's share to a guardian without a guardianship certificate, on an indemnity bond in Format 7; the balance follows on production of the certificate of guardianship. Rule 47(6) prefers the natural guardian, and rule 47(5) makes the payment to the guardian on the minor's behalf. Exam-safe point: Minor's gratuity: 20 per cent on a Format 7 indemnity bond, balance on guardianship certificate. Statutory Authority: Rule 47(5) to (7), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-017 · Additional pension · Rule 44(6)
A pensioner drawing a basic pension of ₹40,000 attains 92 years of age. His additional pension is:
  1. A ₹16,000, being 40 per cent
  2. B ₹12,000, being 30 per cent
  3. C ₹40,000, being 100 per cent
  4. D ₹20,000, being 50 per cent
Answer and reasoning
( A) ₹16,000, being 40 per cent. (B) ₹12,000, being 30 per cent. — Thirty per cent is the band for 85 to under 90 years. (C) ₹40,000, being 100 per cent. — One hundred per cent is reached only at 100 years or more. (D) ₹20,000, being 50 per cent. — Fifty per cent is the band for 95 to under 100 years. Rule 44(6) pays additional pension by band: 20 per cent from 80 to under 85 years, 30 per cent from 85 to under 90, 40 per cent from 90 to under 95, 50 per cent from 95 to under 100, and 100 per cent at 100 years or more. At 92 the band is 40 per cent, which on a basic pension of ₹40,000 is ₹16,000. The additional pension is payable from the first day of the calendar month in which it falls due. Exam-safe point: 92 years: the 40 per cent band. Statutory Authority: Rule 44(6)(a), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-018 · Fractional qualifying service · Rule 44(7) and (8)
A servant retires with 27 years and 4 months of qualifying service. For rule 44 the service is reckoned as:
  1. A 28 years
  2. B 27 years exactly
  3. C 27 years and 9 months
  4. D 27 years and 6 months
Answer and reasoning
( D) 27 years and 6 months. (A) 28 years. — The rounding is to a six-monthly period, not to a whole year. (B) 27 years exactly. — Four months is three months or more, so it becomes a completed six-monthly period. (C) 27 years and 9 months. — The fraction becomes one six-monthly period, not two. Rule 44(7) provides that in calculating the length of qualifying service a fraction of a year equal to three months and above is treated as a completed six-monthly period and reckoned as qualifying service. Four months reaches that threshold, so 27 years and 4 months is reckoned as 27 years and 6 months. Rule 44(8) makes a separate concession for nine years and nine months or more, treating it as ten years so that pension is payable at all. Exam-safe point: Three months or more becomes a completed six-monthly period. Statutory Authority: Rule 44(7) and (8), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-019 · Rounding of pension · Rule 44(9)
A pension finally determined under rule 44 comes to ₹24,750.50. The amount payable is:
  1. A ₹24,800, rounded to the nearest hundred
  2. B ₹24,750
  3. C ₹24,750.50, because pensions may be expressed in paise
  4. D ₹24,751
Answer and reasoning
( D) ₹24,751. (A) ₹24,800, rounded to the nearest hundred. — There is no rounding to hundreds in the rule. (B) ₹24,750. — The rule rounds to the next higher rupee, not to the nearest rupee. (C) ₹24,750.50, because pensions may be expressed in paise. — Rule 44(9) requires expression in whole rupees. Rule 44(9) requires the amount of pension, service gratuity, compassionate allowance, additional pension and additional compassionate allowance finally determined to be expressed in whole rupees, with any fraction of a rupee rounded off to the next higher rupee, separately for each amount. Rule 44(10) applies the same rounding to the pension payable for a fraction of a month where pension is discontinued mid-month. Exam-safe point: Round up to the next rupee, separately for each amount. Statutory Authority: Rule 44(9) and (10), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-020 · Death gratuity rates · Rule 45(1)(b) Table
A servant dies in service with 7 years of qualifying service and emoluments of ₹50,000. The death gratuity is:
  1. A ₹1,00,000
  2. B ₹10,00,000
  3. C ₹6,00,000
  4. D ₹3,00,000
Answer and reasoning
( C) ₹6,00,000. (A) ₹1,00,000. — That is the two-times rate for less than one year. (B) ₹10,00,000. — That is the twenty-times rate, reached only at eleven years. (D) ₹3,00,000. — That is the six-times rate for one year or more but less than five years. Rule 45(1)(b) pays death gratuity by band: twice emoluments below one year, six times at one year or more but under five, twelve times at five years or more but under eleven, twenty times at eleven years or more but under twenty, and half of emoluments for every completed six-monthly period beyond twenty years, capped at thirty-three times. Seven years falls in the twelve-times band, so ₹50,000 gives ₹6,00,000. Exam-safe point: Seven years: twelve times emoluments. Statutory Authority: Rule 45(1)(b), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-021 · Residuary gratuity · Rule 45(3)
A servant retires, draws pension and retirement gratuity, and dies three years later. A residuary gratuity is payable where the sums he received:
  1. A fall short of five years' pension
  2. B fall short of twelve times his emoluments, and the deficiency is then paid to his family
  3. C fall short of sixteen and a half times his emoluments
  4. D fall short of thirty-three times his emoluments — Thirty-three times is the cap on death gratuity
Answer and reasoning
( B) fall short of twelve times his emoluments, and the deficiency is then paid to his family. (A) fall short of five years' pension. — The comparison is with twelve times emoluments, not five years of pension. (C) fall short of sixteen and a half times his emoluments. — Sixteen and a half times is the cap on retirement gratuity under rule 45(1)(a). Rule 45(3) applies where a servant who became eligible for service gratuity or pension dies within five years of retirement, including compulsory retirement as a penalty, and the sums actually received by him on account of gratuity or pension, together with the retirement gratuity and the commuted value of any commuted portion, are less than twelve times his emoluments. A residuary gratuity equal to the deficiency is then paid to the family in the manner indicated in rule 47(1). Exam-safe point: Residuary gratuity: top up to twelve times emoluments, within five years of retirement. Statutory Authority: Rule 45(3), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-022 · Death by suicide · Rule 45(2)
The death gratuity table in rule 45(1)(b) applies:
  1. A also to the death of a Government servant by suicide
  2. B only to natural deaths
  3. C only if the servant had completed one year of qualifying service
  4. D only where the family establishes the death was attributable to service
Answer and reasoning
( A) also to the death of a Government servant by suicide. (B) only to natural deaths. — Rule 45(2) extends the table to suicide expressly. (C) only if the servant had completed one year of qualifying service. — The table itself has a band for less than one year. (D) only where the family establishes the death was attributable to service. — No such condition attaches to the death gratuity table. Rule 45(2) states that the provision of clause (b) of sub-rule (1) shall also be applicable in the case of death of a Government servant by suicide. The clause is not confined to deaths in the course of duty, and the table it carries applies from the lowest band of less than one year of qualifying service. Exam-safe point: Suicide: the ordinary death gratuity table applies. Statutory Authority: Rule 45(2), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-023 · Debarring a person from gratuity · Rule 48
A son eligible for a share of gratuity is charged with abetting his father's murder. His claim:
  1. A remains suspended until the criminal proceedings conclude
  2. B is forfeited immediately on the charge being framed
  3. C is unaffected, because a charge is not a conviction
  4. D passes to his own children in the meantime
Answer and reasoning
( A) remains suspended until the criminal proceedings conclude. (B) is forfeited immediately on the charge being framed. — Suspension of the claim is the consequence; forfeiture follows conviction. (C) is unaffected, because a charge is not a conviction. — Rule 48(1) suspends the claim on the charge itself. (D) passes to his own children in the meantime. — The rule does not provide for transmission on a charge. Rule 48(1) suspends the claim of a person charged with murdering the Government servant, or abetting it, until the criminal proceedings conclude. Under rule 48(2) conviction debars him and the share passes to the other eligible members of the family, while acquittal makes the share payable to him. Rule 48(3) applies the same scheme where the death occurs after retirement, and the Explanation includes abetting a death by suicide. Exam-safe point: Charge suspends; conviction debars; acquittal restores. Statutory Authority: Rule 48, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-001 · Ceiling on gratuity · Rule 45(1) and O.M. 30.05.2024
What is the maximum amount of retirement gratuity or death gratuity admissible to a Central Government civil servant today?
  1. A Twenty-five lakh rupees, with effect from 1 January 2024
  2. B No monetary ceiling, after the 2024 amendment
  3. C Thirty lakh rupees, on the Seventh Pay Commission's second revision
  4. D Twenty lakh rupees, because that is the figure printed in rule 45(1)
Answer and reasoning
( A) Twenty-five lakh rupees, with effect from 1 January 2024. (B) No monetary ceiling, after the 2024 amendment. — The ceiling was raised, not removed. (C) Thirty lakh rupees, on the Seventh Pay Commission's second revision. — No order has gone beyond twenty-five lakh rupees. (D) Twenty lakh rupees, because that is the figure printed in rule 45(1). — The rule text is still twenty lakh rupees, but the order of 30 May 2024 raised the limit to twenty-five lakh with effect from 1 January 2024. Rule 45(1) as notified in 2021 caps gratuity at twenty lakh rupees. The Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare, by Office Memorandum No. 28/03/2024-P&PW(B)/Gratuity/9559 dated 30 May 2024, increased the maximum to twenty-five lakh rupees with effect from 1 January 2024, the date the dearness allowance reached fifty per cent. Paragraph 7 of that order says the formal amendment to the Rules will be notified separately, so the printed rule still carries the old figure and the order governs the payment. Exam-safe point: The operative ceiling is twenty-five lakh rupees; rule 45(1) still prints twenty lakh. Statutory Authority: Rule 45(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 and O.M. No. 28/03/2024-P&PW(B)/Gratuity/9559 dated 30.05.2024
CU-002 · Trigger for the gratuity increase · Rule 45(1) and O.M. 30.05.2024
The gratuity ceiling was raised from twenty lakh to twenty-five lakh rupees because:
  1. A the dearness allowance rate reached fifty per cent, which is the trigger written into the Seventh Pay Commission's scheme
  2. B the Eighth Pay Commission made its first recommendation — The Eighth Pay Commission had not reported when the order issued
  3. C the retirement age was raised to sixty-two years — No change in the age of superannuation was made
  4. D Parliament amended the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 — That Act governs private employment, not the CCS (Pension) Rules
Answer and reasoning
( A) the dearness allowance rate reached fifty per cent, which is the trigger written into the Seventh Pay Commission's scheme. The Seventh Pay Commission linked a further twenty-five per cent increase in the gratuity ceiling to the dearness allowance reaching fifty per cent. The Department of Expenditure raised dearness allowance from forty-six to fifty per cent with effect from 1 January 2024 by its order of 12 March 2024, and the pension order of 30 May 2024 followed with effect from the same date. Exam-safe point: DA at fifty per cent is the trigger, and the date is 1 January 2024. Statutory Authority: O.M. No. 28/03/2024-P&PW(B)/Gratuity/9559 dated 30.05.2024, paragraph 2
CU-003 · Scope of the twenty-five lakh ceiling · O.M. 24.10.2025
The twenty-five lakh rupee gratuity ceiling applies to:
  1. A State Government employees whose rules are modelled on the Central Rules
  2. B every employee of a body funded by the Central Government, including autonomous bodies and universities
  3. C employees of public sector undertakings and banks, who follow Central Government rates
  4. D persons governed by the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 and the CCS (Payment of Gratuity under NPS) Rules, 2021
Answer and reasoning
( D) persons governed by the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 and the CCS (Payment of Gratuity under NPS) Rules, 2021. (A) State Government employees whose rules are modelled on the Central Rules. — State Governments are expressly outside the order. (B) every employee of a body funded by the Central Government, including autonomous bodies and universities. — The order of 24 October 2025 excludes autonomous bodies, universities and societies. (C) employees of public sector undertakings and banks, who follow Central Government rates. — Public sector undertakings and banks are expressly outside the order. The order of 24 October 2025 states the scope that the order of 30 May 2024 left unstated. The twenty-five lakh rupee ceiling belongs to the two central rule sets. Public sector undertakings, banks, port trusts, the Reserve Bank of India, autonomous bodies, universities, State Governments and societies are not covered by it and continue under their own schemes. Exam-safe point: The ceiling is confined to the two central rule sets. Statutory Authority: DoP&PW O.M. F.No. 2/9/2025-P&PW(F) dated 24.10.2025
CU-014 · Additional pension by age band · Rule 44(6) and O.M. 18.10.2024
A pensioner attains eighty-two years of age. The additional pension admissible is:
  1. A twenty per cent, from the pensioner's birthday — The order fixes the first day of the calendar month in which it falls due
  2. B ten per cent, rising to twenty per cent at eighty-five
  3. C no additional pension before eighty-five — The first band begins at eighty
  4. D twenty per cent of the basic pension, from the first day of the calendar month in which the age of eighty is attained
Answer and reasoning
( D) twenty per cent of the basic pension, from the first day of the calendar month in which the age of eighty is attained. (B) ten per cent, rising to twenty per cent at eighty-five. — The table starts at twenty per cent for the band from eighty to less than eighty-five. Rule 44(6) sets the bands: twenty per cent from eighty years to less than eighty-five, thirty per cent from eighty-five, forty per cent from ninety, fifty per cent from ninety-five and one hundred per cent from one hundred years. The order of 18 October 2024 reiterates the table and confirms payment from the first day of the calendar month in which the entitlement falls due, illustrating it with a pensioner born on 20 August 1942 who draws the increment from 1 August 2022. Exam-safe point: Twenty per cent, from the first day of the birth month. Statutory Authority: Rule 44(6), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 and DoP&PW O.M. dated 18.10.2024
CU-026 · Minimum pension today · Rule 44(1)
The minimum pension payable under rule 44(1) is:
  1. A three thousand five hundred rupees per month
  2. B twelve thousand rupees per month
  3. C nine thousand rupees per month
  4. D seven thousand rupees per month
Answer and reasoning
( C) nine thousand rupees per month. (A) three thousand five hundred rupees per month. — That was the figure under the Fourth Pay Commission and is long superseded. (B) twelve thousand rupees per month. — No such minimum appears in the rule. (D) seven thousand rupees per month. — Six thousand was the figure at an earlier stage of the Seventh Pay Commission; it was raised to nine thousand. Rule 44(1) fixes pension at fifty per cent of emoluments or average emoluments, whichever is more beneficial, subject to a minimum of nine thousand rupees and a maximum of one lakh twenty-five thousand rupees per month. Neither limit has been revised by any subsequent order in the register on this platform. Exam-safe point: Nine thousand minimum, one lakh twenty-five thousand maximum. Statutory Authority: Rule 44(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-044 · Cancelling a nomination · Rule 46(7)
A nomination made under rule 46 may be cancelled:
  1. A only before retirement — The rule fixes no such limit
  2. B only by making a fresh nomination, cancellation on its own being ineffective
  3. C at any time, by a notice in writing to the Head of Office
  4. D only once, and only with the sanction of the Head of Department
Answer and reasoning
( C) at any time, by a notice in writing to the Head of Office. (B) only by making a fresh nomination, cancellation on its own being ineffective. — The proviso requires a fresh nomination to accompany the notice where a family exists, but the notice itself is the operative act. (D) only once, and only with the sanction of the Head of Department. — The rule allows cancellation at any time. Rule 46(7) allows a Government servant to cancel a nomination at any time by sending a notice in writing to the Head of Office. Its proviso requires him, along with the notice, to send a fresh nomination in the prescribed form where he has a family. Exam-safe point: Notice in writing to the Head of Office; a fresh nomination accompanies it. Statutory Authority: Rule 46(7), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-055 · Nominees for death gratuity · Rule 45(6)
Which of the following is the correct order of the family members named in the Explanation to rule 45(6)?
  1. A wife or wives; sons; daughters including married daughters; parents; siblings — A married daughter is placed after the sisters
  2. B wife or wives including a judicially separated wife; husband; sons; unmarried daughters; widowed or divorced daughters; father; mother; brothers; unmarried, widowed and divorced sisters; married daughters; children of a pre-deceased son
  3. C wife or wives; children; parents; brothers and sisters; children of a pre-deceased son — The Explanation lists the members individually, not by class
  4. D wife or wives; sons; unmarried daughters; husband; father; mother; married daughters — The husband is placed second, before the sons
Answer and reasoning
( B) wife or wives including a judicially separated wife; husband; sons; unmarried daughters; widowed or divorced daughters; father; mother; brothers; unmarried, widowed and divorced sisters; married daughters; children of a pre-deceased son. The Explanation to rule 45(6) sets out the members of the family for the purposes of rules 45 to 49. The order it prints is: wife or wives including a judicially separated wife or wives, in the case of a male Government servant; husband including a judicially separated husband, in the case of a female Government servant; sons including stepsons and adopted sons; unmarried daughters including stepdaughters and adopted daughters; widowed or divorced daughters including stepdaughters and adopted daughters; father including adoptive parents; mother including adoptive parents; brothers including stepbrothers suffering from a disorder or disability of mind; unmarried sisters, widowed sisters and divorced sisters including stepsisters; married daughters; and children of a pre-deceased son. Exam-safe point: Husband comes second, and a married daughter comes after the sisters. Statutory Authority: Rule 45(6) and the Explanation to it, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-056 · Nomination where the nominee predeceases · Rule 46(4)(i)
A Government servant may provide in his nomination that, in respect of a nominee who predeceases him:
  1. A his share shall be paid to the Government — Nothing lapses to the Government
  2. B his share shall become payable to the other nominee or nominees named in the nomination
  3. C the nomination shall stand cancelled in its entirety
  4. D his share shall fall into the estate of the Government servant
Answer and reasoning
( B) his share shall become payable to the other nominee or nominees named in the nomination. (C) the nomination shall stand cancelled in its entirety. — Clause (ii) deals with invalidity on the nominee's marriage; clause (i) preserves the share for the others. (D) his share shall fall into the estate of the Government servant. — The nomination may direct it to the other nominees instead. Rule 46(4)(i) allows a Government servant, in his nomination, to provide that in respect of any specified nominee who predeceases him, the nomination shall become invalid in respect of that nominee and the share shall become payable to the other nominee or nominees named in the nomination. Its provisos deal with a nomination made when the servant had no family, and with the case of a single nominee. Exam-safe point: The share passes to the other nominees, not to the estate. Statutory Authority: Rule 46(4)(i), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-057 · Residuary gratuity: the family members · Rule 47(1)(b)
Where a family pension of a Government servant who was not governed by the Workmen's Compensation Act becomes payable for a period less than seven years, the residuary gratuity is distributed:
  1. A among the surviving members of the family in the order the rule sets out, in the proportions mentioned
  2. B to the spouse alone, in every case — Several classes of family member are provided for
  3. C to the nominee named for gratuity, in every case
  4. D to the estate of the Government servant — Rule 47 distributes it among the family members it names
Answer and reasoning
( A) among the surviving members of the family in the order the rule sets out, in the proportions mentioned. (C) to the nominee named for gratuity, in every case. — The nomination operates in a specific situation within rule 47, not always. Rule 47(1)(b) deals with the distribution of the residuary gratuity where the family pension of a Government servant not governed by the Workmen's Compensation Act becomes payable for less than the period of seven years. It distributes the amount among the surviving members of the family in the order and proportions the sub-rule sets out, beginning with the widow or widower and the children, and reaching the more distant relatives only in default. Exam-safe point: Residuary gratuity goes to the family in the rule's order, not to the estate. Statutory Authority: Rule 47(1)(b), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021

  2.   3. C The Head of Office shall inform the Accounts Officer as soon as provisional family pension has been paid for a period mentioned in sub-rule (3) or for the period extended under proviso to sub-rule (1) of rule 76, as the case may be — It is the text of a different provision of these rules
  4. D Where the Head of Office has received an intimation that a pensioner or family pensioner has gone missing, he shall ascertain whether any family pension is payable in respect of the missing pensioner or family pensioner in accordance with sub-rule (2) and sub-rule (3) of rule 51.
