Chapter VIII — Family Pension (169 questions)

PC-014 · Family pension — normal rate · Rule 50(2)(a)(i)
A servant dies in service leaving a widow. His pay for family pension is ₹60,000. After the enhanced period ends, the family pension is:
  1. A ₹75,000 a month — the maximum
  2. B ₹9,000 a month — the minimum
  3. C ₹30,000 a month — 50 per cent of pay
  4. D ₹18,000 a month — 30 per cent of pay
Answer and reasoning
( D) ₹18,000 a month — 30 per cent of pay. (A) ₹75,000 a month — the maximum. — The maximum applies only where 30 per cent exceeds it. (B) ₹9,000 a month — the minimum. — The minimum applies only where 30 per cent falls below it. (C) ₹30,000 a month — 50 per cent of pay. — Fifty per cent is the enhanced rate, which runs for ten years and then steps down. Rule 50(2)(a)(i) sets the ordinary family pension at 30 per cent of pay, subject to a minimum of ₹9,000 and a maximum of ₹75,000 a month. Thirty per cent of ₹60,000 is ₹18,000. The enhanced rate under sub-clause (ii) is 50 per cent, but it is payable for ten years from the death and then the pension reverts to the sub-clause (i) rate under clause (b). Exam-safe point: Family pension: 30% normal, 50% enhanced for ten years. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(2), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PC-015 · Family pension — enhanced rate · Rule 50(2)(a)(ii)
A servant dies in service. His pay for family pension is ₹2,00,000. The enhanced family pension is:
  1. A ₹1,25,000 a month, the maximum
  2. B ₹75,000 a month
  3. C ₹1,00,000 a month
  4. D ₹60,000 a month
Answer and reasoning
( C) ₹1,00,000 a month. (A) ₹1,25,000 a month, the maximum. — The maximum applies only if 50 per cent exceeds it; 50 per cent of ₹2,00,000 is ₹1,00,000. (B) ₹75,000 a month. — That is the ordinary ceiling, not the enhanced one. (D) ₹60,000 a month. — That is 30 per cent, the ordinary rate. Fifty per cent of ₹2,00,000 is ₹1,00,000. The enhanced family pension under rule 50(2)(a)(ii) is 50 per cent of pay, and sub-clause (iv) puts its ceiling at ₹1,25,000. ₹1,00,000 is below that ceiling, so it stands. Had the pay been ₹3,00,000, the figure would have been cut to the ₹1,25,000 ceiling. Exam-safe point: Enhanced family pension ceiling: ₹1,25,000. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(2)(a)(ii) and (iv), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PC-016 · Family pension after retirement · Rule 50(2)(a)(iii)
A pensioner dies after retirement. The enhanced family pension is payable for:
  1. A For life — The enhanced rate is time-bound; the ordinary rate follows it
  2. B Seven years, or until he would have attained 67, whichever is less
  3. C Ten years, as on a death in service
  4. D Seven years in every case
Answer and reasoning
( B) Seven years, or until he would have attained 67, whichever is less. (C) Ten years, as on a death in service. — Ten years is the death-in-service period under sub-clause (ii). (D) Seven years in every case. — The seven years is cut short if he would have reached 67 sooner. Rule 50(2)(a)(iii) gives the enhanced family pension after a death following retirement for seven years, or up to the date the deceased pensioner would have attained sixty-seven years had he survived, whichever is less. Two provisos then cap it: it shall not exceed the pension authorised on retirement, and where that pension is below the ordinary family pension rate, the family pension is limited to the ordinary rate. Exam-safe point: After retirement: seven years or age 67 of the pensioner, whichever is less. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(2)(a)(iii), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PC-017 · Family pension — the floor · Rule 50(2)(a)(i)
A servant dies in service with pay for family pension of ₹22,000. The ordinary family pension is:
  1. A ₹9,000 a month, the minimum
  2. B ₹6,600 a month
  3. C ₹11,000 a month
  4. D Nothing, because the pay is too low
Answer and reasoning
( A) ₹9,000 a month, the minimum. (B) ₹6,600 a month. — That is 30 per cent, but the rule puts a floor under it. (C) ₹11,000 a month. — That is 50 per cent, the enhanced rate. (D) Nothing, because the pay is too low. — The floor guarantees a minimum, whatever the pay. Thirty per cent of ₹22,000 is ₹6,600, which is below the minimum of ₹9,000 fixed by rule 50(2)(a)(i). The family pension is therefore ₹9,000. The same floor of ₹9,000 applies to the enhanced rate under sub-clause (iv), so even the 50 per cent figure cannot fall below it. Exam-safe point: Family pension floor: ₹9,000, on both the ordinary and enhanced rates. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(2)(a)(i), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PC-018 · Order of eligibility · Rule 50(6)
Under rule 50(6), the order in which family pension is payable is:
  1. A Widow or widower, then children, then dependent parents, then dependent disabled siblings
  2. B All eligible members in equal shares at the same time, always
  3. C Children first, then widow or widower — The widow or widower comes first
  4. D Widow or widower, then parents, then children — Children come before parents
Answer and reasoning
( A) Widow or widower, then children, then dependent parents, then dependent disabled siblings. (B) All eligible members in equal shares at the same time, always. — Rule 50(7)(a) makes it payable to one member at a time, save in the listed cases. Rule 50(6) sets a four-step order: the widow or widower (including a post-retiral spouse and a judicially separated spouse); then children, including adopted and step children and children born after retirement; then dependent parents; then dependent siblings suffering from a mental or physical disability. Rule 50(7)(a) adds that it is not payable to more than one member at a time, subject to the listed exceptions where it is shared. Exam-safe point: Order: spouse, children, dependent parents, dependent disabled siblings. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(6) and (7), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PC-019 · Son's eligibility · Rule 50(9)(a)(i)
A son of a deceased servant, not suffering from any disability, is eligible for family pension if he is:
  1. A Unmarried, at any age, if he is a student
  2. B Below eighteen, the age of majority
  3. C Below twenty-one and unmarried — The age is twenty-five
  4. D Unmarried, below twenty-five, and not earning his livelihood
Answer and reasoning
( D) Unmarried, below twenty-five, and not earning his livelihood. (A) Unmarried, at any age, if he is a student. — There is no student concession; the age limit is absolute for a son without disability. (B) Below eighteen, the age of majority. — Eighteen is the age of majority, not the family pension limit. Rule 50(9)(a)(i) makes an ordinary son eligible only if he is unmarried, below twenty-five years and not earning his livelihood. Clause (ii) does the same for a daughter, but permits her to be unmarried, widowed or divorced — the daughter is not required to be unmarried. A son or daughter suffering from a mental or physical disability under clause (iii) has no age limit, and receives it for life on the conditions in clause (h). Exam-safe point: Son: unmarried, under 25, not earning. Daughter: unmarried, widowed or divorced. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(9)(a), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-024 · Two family pensions · Rule 50(13)
Both husband and wife are Government servants and both die. Their eligible child draws two family pensions. Where both pensions are at the ordinary rate under rule 50(2)(a)(i), the combined amount is limited to:
  1. A ₹1,25,000 per mensem
  2. B ₹1,00,000 per mensem
  3. C No limit, because two separate pensions are involved
  4. D ₹75,000 per mensem
Answer and reasoning
( D) ₹75,000 per mensem. (A) ₹1,25,000 per mensem. — That ceiling applies where either pension is at the enhanced rate. (B) ₹1,00,000 per mensem. — That figure does not appear in rule 50(13). (C) No limit, because two separate pensions are involved. — Rule 50(13) caps the sum precisely because two pensions are involved. Rule 50(13) deals with the case where both spouses were Government servants. If the surviving child is eligible to draw two pensions at the enhanced rate, or where one enhanced pension later converts to the ordinary rate, the sum is limited to ₹1,25,000 a month. Where both pensions are payable at the ordinary rate under rule 50(2)(a)(i), the sum is limited to ₹75,000 a month. Exam-safe point: Two ordinary-rate family pensions: ₹75,000 combined. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(13), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-025 · Family pension to parents · Rule 50(10)(b)
Where family pension is admissible to the parents, it is payable:
  1. A to whichever parent the Head of Office considers dependent
  2. B to the father first, and failing him to the mother
  3. C to the mother first, and failing her to the father
  4. D to both in equal shares
Answer and reasoning
( C) to the mother first, and failing her to the father. (A) to whichever parent the Head of Office considers dependent. — Dependence is a precondition; the order between the parents is fixed by the rule. (B) to the father first, and failing him to the mother. — Rule 50(10)(b) reverses the usual order and names the mother first. (D) to both in equal shares. — The rule provides a sequence, not equal shares. Rule 50(10)(a) makes family pension payable to the parents for life where no widow, widower or eligible child survives, if the parents were dependent on the servant immediately before death. Clause (b) then fixes the order: the mother first, failing which the father. The Explanation deems parents dependent where their combined income is less than the minimum family pension and the dearness relief admissible on it. Exam-safe point: Parents: mother first, then father. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(10) and its Explanation, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-026 · Change of family after retirement · Rule 50(15)(f)
A pensioner marries after retirement. He must intimate the change to the Head of Office:
  1. A by an ordinary letter; no form is prescribed
  2. B in Form 5, with a copy of the marriage certificate
  3. C in Format 5, with a copy of the marriage certificate
  4. D in Form 4, with a copy of the marriage certificate
Answer and reasoning
( B) in Form 5, with a copy of the marriage certificate. (A) by an ordinary letter; no form is prescribed. — Rule 50(15)(f) prescribes Form 5 and the certificate. (C) in Format 5, with a copy of the marriage certificate. — Format 5 is the relieving order on absorption. (D) in Form 4, with a copy of the marriage certificate. — Form 4 is the pre-retirement family particulars form, re-submitted with the pension papers. Rule 50(15)(a) requires the family particulars in Form 4 on entering service, and clause (e) requires an up-to-date Form 4 with the pension papers before retirement. Clause (f) then deals with events after retirement: where the servant marries or remarries, or a child is born, he must intimate the Head of Office in Form 5 with a copy of the marriage or birth certificate, as the case may be. Exam-safe point: Post-retirement change of family: Form 5, with the certificate. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(15)(f), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-027 · Disability certificate · Rule 50(15)(c)
Where a disability manifests in a child or dependent sibling, the fact must be supported by a medical certificate from:
  1. A the Pension Disbursing Authority — The disbursing authority has no certifying role under this clause
  2. B an authority competent to issue a disability certificate under the RPwD Act, 2016, or a Medical Board
  3. C the Head of Office's own assessment
  4. D any registered medical practitioner — Rule 50(15)(c) names two specific sources
Answer and reasoning
( B) an authority competent to issue a disability certificate under the RPwD Act, 2016, or a Medical Board. (C) the Head of Office's own assessment. — The Head of Office receives and records the certificate; he does not issue it. Rule 50(15)(c) requires the fact of a disability to be supported by a certificate from either an authority competent to issue a disability certificate under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 and the Rules of 2017, or a Medical Board comprising a Medical Superintendent, Principal, Director or Head of the Institution or his nominee as Chairman and two other members, at least one of whom is a specialist in the particular area of disability. Exam-safe point: Disability: an RPwD-authorised authority or a Medical Board. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(15)(c), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-028 · Missing servant and death gratuity · Rule 51(8)(b)
A Government servant goes missing and a police report is lodged. Death gratuity becomes payable:
  1. A when the death is conclusively established, or on expiry of seven years from the police report, whichever is earlier
  2. B on expiry of twelve years from the police report — The period is seven years
  3. C on expiry of six months from the police report
  4. D only when the death is conclusively established, however long it takes
Answer and reasoning
( A) when the death is conclusively established, or on expiry of seven years from the police report, whichever is earlier. (C) on expiry of six months from the police report. — Six months is the waiting period before family pension and gratuity may start, not the trigger. (D) only when the death is conclusively established, however long it takes. — The seven-year limb exists precisely for the case where death is never established. Rule 51(8)(a) bars payment of family pension, including arrears, and of gratuity before six months from the date of lodging the police report. Clause (b) then fixes when death gratuity becomes payable: after the death is conclusively established, or on expiry of seven years from the date of the report, whichever is earlier. Clause (c) requires any difference between death gratuity and retirement gratuity to be paid within three months of the claim. Exam-safe point: Death gratuity: conclusive proof or seven years, whichever is earlier. Statutory Authority: Rule 51(8), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-029 · Missing servant claim documents · Rule 51(5)(b)
A claim in a missing-person case must be accompanied by:
  1. A a death certificate from the registering authority
  2. B a succession certificate
  3. C an indemnity bond in Format 7, with the same reports
  4. D an indemnity bond in Format 8, with copies of the police report and the untraced report
Answer and reasoning
( D) an indemnity bond in Format 8, with copies of the police report and the untraced report. (A) a death certificate from the registering authority. — Rule 71(6)(e) expressly says the Head of Office shall not wait for one. (B) a succession certificate. — A succession certificate belongs to the rule 49 route where there is no family. (C) an indemnity bond in Format 7, with the same reports. — Format 7 is the indemnity bond for a minor's share of gratuity. Rule 51(5)(a) requires claims to be submitted after a police report has been lodged as an FIR, daily diary entry or general diary entry. Clause (b) requires the claim to be accompanied by an Indemnity Bond in Format 8 together with a copy of that report and a report from the police that the person could not be traced despite all efforts. Rule 71(6)(e) reinforces the scheme by directing the Head of Office not to wait for a death certificate. Exam-safe point: Missing person: Format 8 indemnity bond plus the two police reports. Statutory Authority: Rule 51(5) and rule 71(6)(e), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-006 · Nomination by a female Government servant · Rule 50(8) and O.M. 01.01.2024
A female Government servant whose divorce proceedings are pending may ask that family pension be paid to her eligible child in precedence to her husband. That request is made:
  1. A to the Pension Disbursing Authority after retirement only
  2. B in writing to the Head of Office, and it operates if she dies during the pendency of the proceedings
  3. C by will, since the spouse's right is a matter of succession
  4. D by a fresh nomination in Form 4, which overrides the statutory order in rule 50(6)
Answer and reasoning
( B) in writing to the Head of Office, and it operates if she dies during the pendency of the proceedings. (A) to the Pension Disbursing Authority after retirement only. — The request may be made by a serving Government servant or a pensioner, and it is made to the Head of Office. (C) by will, since the spouse's right is a matter of succession. — The order of 1 January 2024 sets a written request to the Head of Office, not a testamentary disposition. (D) by a fresh nomination in Form 4, which overrides the statutory order in rule 50(6). — Form 4 records family details; the order of eligibility in rule 50(6) is not displaced by it. The Department's Office Memorandum No. 1/1(1)/2023-P&PW(E) dated 1 January 2024 applies where divorce proceedings are pending in a competent court, or where the woman has filed a case against her husband under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, the Dowry Prohibition Act or the Indian Penal Code. Paragraph 3(a) requires a request in writing to the Head of Office, which takes effect if she dies during the pendency of those proceedings. Exam-safe point: Written request to the Head of Office, effective on death during the proceedings. Statutory Authority: DoP&PW O.M. No. 1/1(1)/2023-P&PW(E) dated 01.01.2024, paragraphs 3(a) and 4
CU-007 · Disbursal where the mother has nominated a child · O.M. 01.01.2024, paragraph 3(b)
Where the female Government servant had made such a request and dies during the proceedings, and is survived by a widower with a minor child, the family pension is payable to:
  1. A the widower, provided he is the guardian of the child, and to the child through the actual guardian if he ceases to be guardian
  2. B the widower absolutely, because the nomination lapses on death
  3. C the child and the widower in equal shares
  4. D the minor child directly, through a guardian appointed by the court
Answer and reasoning
( A) the widower, provided he is the guardian of the child, and to the child through the actual guardian if he ceases to be guardian. (B) the widower absolutely, because the nomination lapses on death. — The nomination does not lapse; it changes the order in which the pension is disbursed. (C) the child and the widower in equal shares. — The order sets a sequence, not a sharing, unless more than one person is payable at the same time. (D) the minor child directly, through a guardian appointed by the court. — The widower receives it while he remains the guardian; the child's direct right arises on attaining majority. Paragraph 3(b)(ii) of the order provides that where the deceased is survived by a widower with a minor child or a child suffering from a disorder or disability of mind, the family pension is payable to the widower provided he is the guardian; if he ceases to be the guardian it is payable to the child through the person who is the actual guardian, and when the minor attains majority and remains eligible it becomes payable to the child. Exam-safe point: Widower as guardian first; the child takes over on majority. Statutory Authority: DoP&PW O.M. No. 1/1(1)/2023-P&PW(E) dated 01.01.2024, paragraph 3(b)(ii)
CU-008 · Effect of the female-nominee order on the rule text · O.M. 01.01.2024
The order of 1 January 2024 allowing a female Government servant to nominate her child in precedence to her husband:
  1. A was struck down for want of legislative competence
  2. B substituted clause (a) of rule 50(8) in the Gazette the same day
  3. C inserted a new sub-rule (8A) into rule 50 — Sub-rule (8A) was not inserted; the order works within sub-rules (8) and (9)
  4. D was issued as an Office Memorandum, and paragraph 6 records that the formal amendment to rule 50 would be notified separately
Answer and reasoning
( D) was issued as an Office Memorandum, and paragraph 6 records that the formal amendment to rule 50 would be notified separately. (A) was struck down for want of legislative competence. — The order stands and has been reiterated in paragraph 4 of the order of 29 October 2026. (B) substituted clause (a) of rule 50(8) in the Gazette the same day. — No gazette amendment issued on 1 January 2024; the order is an Office Memorandum. The instrument is Office Memorandum No. 1/1(1)/2023-P&PW(E) dated 1 January 2024. Paragraph 6 says that a formal amendment to rule 50 "will be notified separately", and no such amendment appears in the gazette series up to the amendment rules of 2025. The rule text is therefore unchanged and the order operates as an instruction on how a case under it is to be decided. Exam-safe point: An Office Memorandum, not an amendment of the rule text. Statutory Authority: DoP&PW O.M. No. 1/1(1)/2023-P&PW(E) dated 01.01.2024, paragraph 6
CU-015 · Two wives · O.M. 29.10.2026
Where a deceased Government servant is survived by two widows, the family pension is:
  1. A withheld until a court decides which marriage is valid
  2. B paid to the first wife only, the second marriage being void
  3. C paid to the widows in equal shares, and on the death or ineligibility of one her share passes to her child or children
  4. D paid to the widow who was nominated in Form 4 — Form 4 records details; it does not displace rule 50(8)(c)
Answer and reasoning
( C) paid to the widows in equal shares, and on the death or ineligibility of one her share passes to her child or children. (A) withheld until a court decides which marriage is valid. — The Department's direction is to consult the Department of Legal Affairs on legality, not to withhold the pension. (B) paid to the first wife only, the second marriage being void. — Rule 50(8)(c) provides for equal shares; the legality of the marriage is decided first under the 2025 instruction. Rule 50(8)(c) provides that where the deceased is survived by more widows than one, family pension is paid to them in equal shares, and on the death or ineligibility of a widow her share becomes payable to her child or children who fulfil the conditions in sub-rule (9). The order of 27 October 2025 adds that where the legality of the second marriage is in question, the matter is to be settled in consultation with the Department of Legal Affairs case by case before eligibility is decided. Exam-safe point: Equal shares between widows, then to each widow's children. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(8)(c), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 and DoP&PW O.M. dated 27.10.2025
CU-016 · Divorce and judicial separation · O.M. 29.10.2026
A deceased pensioner is survived by a judicially separated widow and no child. Her claim to family pension:
  1. A fails, because a judicially separated spouse is treated as divorced
  2. B is considered under rule 50(8)(h), a decree of judicial separation not having dissolved the marriage
  3. C is decided by the court that granted the decree — The decree does not fix the pension; the Rules do
  4. D succeeds at the enhanced rate without any condition
Answer and reasoning
( B) is considered under rule 50(8)(h), a decree of judicial separation not having dissolved the marriage. (A) fails, because a judicially separated spouse is treated as divorced. — The order of 29 October 2026 distinguishes the two expressly: a divorced spouse is not eligible, a judicially separated one may be. (D) succeeds at the enhanced rate without any condition. — The claim is subject to the conditions in rule 50(8)(h) and the following clauses. The Office Memorandum of 29 October 2026 records that a decree of judicial separation permits the spouses to live separately without dissolving the marriage, so a judicially separated widow or widower may be considered under rule 50(8)(h) to (j). Where there is no eligible child the claim is examined under rule 50(8)(h). A divorced spouse is not eligible, though the children of the marriage may be. Exam-safe point: Judicial separation: eligible. Divorce: not eligible. Statutory Authority: DoP&PW O.M. No. 1/1(39)/2026-P&PW(E)/E-12002-(7) dated 29.10.2026, paragraphs 2 to 4
CU-017 · Order of eligibility · O.M. 29.10.2026
After the spouse and all children cease to be eligible, family pension under rule 50 becomes payable next to:
  1. A the dependent parents, the mother ordinarily preceding the father
  2. B the widowed mother only, the father being excluded
  3. C the married daughters, who return to the list
  4. D the dependent siblings with a disability, before the parents
Answer and reasoning
( A) the dependent parents, the mother ordinarily preceding the father. (B) the widowed mother only, the father being excluded. — The father is eligible if the mother is not; the mother ordinarily precedes him. (C) the married daughters, who return to the list. — Married daughters are excluded by rule 50(9)(n) unless disabled. (D) the dependent siblings with a disability, before the parents. — Siblings come after the parents, under rule 50(11). Rule 50(6) sets the order: widow or widower, then children, then dependent parents, then dependent siblings with a mental or physical disability. Rule 50(10)(b) provides that family pension admissible to parents is payable to the mother failing which to the father, and the order of 29 October 2026 repeats that the mother ordinarily precedes the father. Exam-safe point: Parents next, mother before father; siblings last. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(6) and 50(10)(b), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 and DoP&PW O.M. dated 29.10.2026
CU-018 · Two family pensions · Rule 50(13) and O.M. 29.10.2026
Both husband and wife were Central Government servants. Both die, and one eligible child survives. If both family pensions are payable at the ordinary rate, the combined amount is limited to:
  1. A seventy-five thousand rupees per month
  2. B the ordinary maximum, with no separate limit for two pensions
  3. C one lakh fifty thousand rupees per month
  4. D one lakh twenty-five thousand rupees per month
Answer and reasoning
( A) seventy-five thousand rupees per month. (B) the ordinary maximum, with no separate limit for two pensions. — Rule 50(13) sets a separate combined limit. (C) one lakh fifty thousand rupees per month. — No such limit appears in rule 50(13). (D) one lakh twenty-five thousand rupees per month. — That limit applies where at least one pension is at the enhanced rate. Rule 50(13) sets three limits. Where the child draws two pensions at the enhanced rate, the combined amount is limited to one lakh twenty-five thousand rupees a month. Where one pension falls from the enhanced to the ordinary rate, the combined amount is still limited to one lakh twenty-five thousand. Where both are at the ordinary rate, the combined amount is limited to seventy-five thousand rupees a month. Exam-safe point: Two ordinary pensions: seventy-five thousand. Any enhanced element: one lakh twenty-five thousand. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(13), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-019 · Claimant charged with murder · Rule 50(14)
A person otherwise eligible for family pension is charged with abetting the suicide of the Government servant. Family pension to that person:
  1. A is forfeited permanently
  2. B is paid into court until the trial ends — The rule redirects it to the other eligible member of the family
  3. C is paid, because a charge is not a conviction — Rule 50(14)(c) suspends payment on the charge itself
  4. D is not paid until the criminal proceedings conclude, and is paid meanwhile to the other eligible member of the family
Answer and reasoning
( D) is not paid until the criminal proceedings conclude, and is paid meanwhile to the other eligible member of the family. (A) is forfeited permanently. — Forfeiture follows only on conviction; on acquittal the pension becomes payable to him from the date of acquittal. Rule 50(14)(c) provides that where a person eligible for family pension is charged with murdering the Government servant or abetting it, the pension is not paid to that person until the criminal proceedings conclude. Clause (d) pays it to the other eligible member meanwhile, and the Explanation says the charge includes abetting death by suicide. Clause (e) then provides for conviction and acquittal: on conviction the person is debarred, and on acquittal the pension becomes payable to him from the date of acquittal. Exam-safe point: Charge suspends, conviction debars, acquittal restores. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(14), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-020 · Disabled child, for life · Rule 50(9)(h)
Family pension to a son or daughter suffering from a disability referred to in rule 50(9)(h) is payable:
  1. A until the age of twenty-five, like any other child
  2. B for life, whatever the date on which the disability arose
  3. C for life, provided the disability existed before the death of the Government servant or pensioner and his or her spouse
  4. D for ten years from the date of death — No such period appears in the rule
Answer and reasoning
( C) for life, provided the disability existed before the death of the Government servant or pensioner and his or her spouse. (A) until the age of twenty-five, like any other child. — The age of twenty-five is the ceiling for the first category of children, not this one. (B) for life, whatever the date on which the disability arose. — Condition (i) requires the disability to have existed before the death. Clause (h) of rule 50(9) provides for family pension for life to a son or daughter suffering from a disorder or disability of mind, including the mentally retarded, or a physical disability of the kind described, so as to render him or her unable to earn a living even after twenty-five years. Condition (i) requires the disability to have existed before the death of the Government servant or pensioner and his or her spouse. Exam-safe point: For life, but the disability must pre-date the death. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(9)(h), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-021 · Unmarried or widowed or divorced daughter · Rule 50(9)(j)
Family pension to an unmarried, widowed or divorced daughter beyond twenty-five years is payable:
  1. A only if she is the eldest child — The order of birth decides the sequence between sisters, not eligibility
  2. B for life or until she marries or remarries or starts earning her livelihood, whichever is earliest
  3. C until she attains thirty years of age — No age of thirty appears in the rule
  4. D for life, without any condition — Marriage, remarriage or earning a livelihood ends it
Answer and reasoning
( B) for life or until she marries or remarries or starts earning her livelihood, whichever is earliest. Clause (j) of rule 50(9) continues family pension to an unmarried, widowed or divorced daughter beyond twenty-five years for life or until she marries or remarries or starts earning her livelihood, whichever is earliest. Among more than one such daughter, the pension is payable in the order of birth, and a younger daughter becomes eligible when the elder next above her marries, remarries, starts earning or dies. For a widowed or divorced daughter, the widowhood or divorce must have occurred during the lifetime of the Government servant or pensioner or of his or her spouse, with a proviso for a divorce decree granted after their death where proceedings were filed during their lifetime. Exam-safe point: For life subject to three cessations, in order of birth. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(9)(j), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-022 · Family details in Form 4 · Rule 50(15)(a)
A Government servant who has no family at the time of entering service must furnish the details of family:
  1. A at the time of retirement only, in Form 6-A
  2. B in Form 4 as soon as he acquires a family
  3. C within one year of marriage, by a separate intimation
  4. D not at all, until a family pension claim arises
Answer and reasoning
( B) in Form 4 as soon as he acquires a family. (A) at the time of retirement only, in Form 6-A. — Form 6-A is the retirement form; the obligation arises on acquiring a family. (C) within one year of marriage, by a separate intimation. — The rule requires Form 4 as soon as the family is acquired. (D) not at all, until a family pension claim arises. — The rule creates a positive obligation. Rule 50(15)(a)(i) requires a Government servant, on entering service, to give the details of his family in Form 4 to the Head of Office, including the spouse, all children, parents and disabled siblings, whether or not eligible for family pension. Clause (a)(ii) provides that if he has no family he furnishes the details in Form 4 as soon as he acquires one. Clause (b) requires any subsequent change in the size of the family to be communicated, including the marriage of a child. Exam-safe point: Form 4 on acquiring a family, and on every later change. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(15)(a) and (b), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-024 · Enhanced family pension ceiling · Rule 50(2)(a)(iv)
The enhanced rate of family pension is subject to a maximum of:
  1. A two lakh rupees a month
  2. B seventy-five thousand rupees a month
  3. C one lakh rupees a month
  4. D one lakh twenty-five thousand rupees a month
Answer and reasoning
( D) one lakh twenty-five thousand rupees a month. (A) two lakh rupees a month. — No order has raised the family pension ceiling beyond one lakh twenty-five thousand. (B) seventy-five thousand rupees a month. — That is the maximum for the ordinary rate. (C) one lakh rupees a month. — That figure belongs to an earlier pay commission cycle. Rule 50(2)(a)(i) fixes the ordinary rate at thirty per cent of pay subject to a minimum of nine thousand and a maximum of seventy-five thousand rupees a month. Sub-clause (iv) applies a minimum of nine thousand and a maximum of one lakh twenty-five thousand rupees a month to the enhanced rate under sub-clause (ii) or (iii). The order of 29 October 2026 confirms both figures are current. Exam-safe point: Ordinary ceiling seventy-five thousand; enhanced ceiling one lakh twenty-five thousand. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(2)(a)(iv), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-029 · Dependent parents · Rule 50(10)
Family pension to dependent parents is payable:
  1. A to the father in every case, as the head of the family
  2. B for ten years from the date of death — No such period applies to parents
  3. C only if there is no widow and no child, and no dependent sibling
  4. D for life, if the parents were dependent on the Government servant immediately before his death
Answer and reasoning
( D) for life, if the parents were dependent on the Government servant immediately before his death. (A) to the father in every case, as the head of the family. — Rule 50(10)(b) gives it to the mother failing which to the father. (C) only if there is no widow and no child, and no dependent sibling. — Siblings come after parents, not before. Rule 50(10)(a) makes family pension payable to the parents for life where the deceased is not survived by a widow or widower or a child eligible for family pension, or where the widow or widower and all children cease to be eligible, if the parents were dependent on the Government servant immediately before his or her death. Clause (b) prefers the mother, and the Explanation deems the parents dependent if their combined income is less than the minimum family pension plus the dearness relief on it. Exam-safe point: Parents after spouse and children; mother first; for life. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(10), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-030 · Dependent sibling · Rule 50(11)
Family pension to a dependent sibling suffering from a mental or physical disability is payable:
  1. A for five years, renewable on a fresh medical certificate — The pension is for life; the certificate is annual evidence of continued eligibility
  2. B until the sibling attains twenty-five years — The age limit does not apply to a sibling with a disability
  3. C only if the sibling is unmarried — Marriage does not disqualify a sibling with a disability, by the same reasoning as rule 50(9)(i)
  4. D for life, if the sibling was wholly dependent on the Government servant immediately before his death and the disability existed before it
Answer and reasoning
( D) for life, if the sibling was wholly dependent on the Government servant immediately before his death and the disability existed before it. Rule 50(11)(a) makes family pension payable to a dependent sibling suffering from a mental or physical disability, for life, where no widow or widower, child or parent is eligible, and the sibling was wholly dependent on the Government servant immediately before his or her death. Clause (b) applies the same disability criteria as rule 50(9)(h) and (i), and its proviso requires the disability to have existed before the death. Exam-safe point: Siblings last in the order, for life, dependency and pre-existing disability required. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(11), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-058 · Enhanced family pension after retirement · Rule 50(2)(a)(iii)
Where a Government servant dies after retirement, the enhanced rate of family pension is payable:
  1. A until the family pensioner attains sixty-seven years
  2. B for seven years, whatever the pensioner's age — The sixty-seven year limit cuts the period short
  3. C for ten years from the date of death — Ten years applies to a death while in service
  4. D for seven years or until the pensioner would have attained sixty-seven years, whichever is earlier
Answer and reasoning
( D) for seven years or until the pensioner would have attained sixty-seven years, whichever is earlier. (A) until the family pensioner attains sixty-seven years. — The age is the deceased pensioner's, not the family pensioner's. Rule 50(2)(a)(iii) provides that, in the event of the death of a Government servant after retirement, the enhanced rate is payable for seven years or until the date on which the deceased Government servant would have attained sixty-seven years, whichever is earlier. Its first proviso caps the amount at the family pension admissible under sub-clause (i), and the second deals with the pension authorised on retirement where it was itself below the ordinary family pension. Exam-safe point: Seven years, cut short at the deceased's sixty-seven. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(2)(a)(iii), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-059 · Sharing family pension · Rule 50(7)(b)
Where family pension is payable to more than one member of the family at the same time:
  1. A it is paid to the eldest in full, who maintains the others — The rule requires equal shares
  2. B it is paid in the shares entered in the Pension Payment Order, which the Head of Office may vary
  3. C it is paid in equal shares, any fraction of a rupee being rounded up, subject to the overall maximum
  4. D it is paid in the proportions the widow or widower decides
Answer and reasoning
( C) it is paid in equal shares, any fraction of a rupee being rounded up, subject to the overall maximum. (B) it is paid in the shares entered in the Pension Payment Order, which the Head of Office may vary. — Rule 50(7)(b) fixes equal shares. (D) it is paid in the proportions the widow or widower decides. — The rule does not leave the proportions to a family member. Rule 50(7)(b) provides that where family pension is payable to more than one member of the family at the same time it is paid in equal shares, and if a share contains a fraction of a rupee it is rounded off to the next higher rupee. Its proviso prevents the rounding-up from carrying the total above the maximum prescribed by the rule: any excess fraction is ignored. Exam-safe point: Equal shares, fractions rounded up, total capped at the maximum. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(7)(b), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-060 · Divorced daughter: proceedings filed during life · Rule 50(9)(j)
A divorce is decreed after the death of the Government servant, but the proceedings were filed during the lifetime of the servant or his spouse. The divorced daughter's family pension:
  1. A is payable only if the court so orders
  2. B is not payable, because the divorce took place after the death
  3. C is payable from the date of divorce
  4. D is payable from the date of the servant's death
Answer and reasoning
( C) is payable from the date of divorce. (A) is payable only if the court so orders. — The proviso makes it payable by force of the rule. (B) is not payable, because the divorce took place after the death. — The first proviso saves precisely this case. (D) is payable from the date of the servant's death. — The pension begins on the divorce, not earlier. The first proviso to rule 50(9)(j)(vi) provides that family pension shall be payable to a divorced daughter from the date of divorce if the divorce proceedings were filed in a competent court during the lifetime of the Government servant or pensioner or his or her spouse but the divorce took place after their death. The second proviso prevents her pension from starting while another eligible member is already drawing it. Exam-safe point: From the date of divorce where the proceedings predate the death. Statutory Authority: Rule 50(9)(j), first proviso to clause (vi), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021

  1. A Provided that while applying the requisite checks, the Accounts Officer shall confine the verification of the correctness of emoluments for a maximum period of one year preceding the date of death or disappearance of the Government servant.
  2. B Where a widow or widower in receipt of family pension remarries and has, at the time of remarriage, a child from the deceased Government servant or pensioner who has already attained the age of majority and is eligible for family pension, the family pension shall be payable to such child after the remarriage of his father or mother.
  3. C The family pension payable to a son or a daughter shall be stopped if he or she starts earning his or her livelihood.
  4. D They shall come into force with effect from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.
Answer and reasoning
( C) The family pension payable to a son or a daughter shall be stopped if he or she starts earning his or her livelihood. (A) Provided that while applying the requisite checks, the Accounts Officer shall confine the verification of the correctness of emoluments for a maximum period of one year preceding the date of death or disappearance of the Government servant. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. (B) Where a widow or widower in receipt of family pension remarries and has, at the time of remarriage, a child from the deceased Government servant or pensioner who has already attained the age of majority and is eligible for family pension, the family pension shall be payable to such child after the remarriage of his father or mother. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. (D) They shall come into force with effect from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. The answer reproduces the provision as notified. The three wrong options are other provisions of the same rules, so the question tests recall of this provision rather than recognition of the statute's style. Chapter IX — Dearness Relief (11 questions)

PS-030 · Dearness relief to a family pensioner · Rule 52(4)
A family pensioner takes up employment under a State Government. Dearness relief on the family pension:
  1. A is suspended during the employment
  2. B is payable only if her pay is at the minimum of the scale
  3. C continues to be payable during the employment
  4. D is payable only after she retires from that employment
Answer and reasoning
( C) continues to be payable during the employment. (A) is suspended during the employment. — That is the rule for a pensioner, not for a family pensioner. (B) is payable only if her pay is at the minimum of the scale. — The minimum-of-scale condition belongs to rule 52(2), which rule 52(4) disapplies here. (D) is payable only after she retires from that employment. — Rule 52(4) preserves it during the employment. Rule 52(2) denies dearness relief to a pensioner or compassionate allowance holder who is re-employed or absorbed, subject to the three-condition proviso in rule 52(2) and the certificate regime in rule 52(3). Rule 52(4) carves family pensioners out of that denial: a family pensioner employed under the Central or State Government or a corporation, company, body or bank under them remains eligible to draw dearness relief on family pension during the employment. Exam-safe point: Family pensioner employed: dearness relief continues. Statutory Authority: Rule 52(2) to (4), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021

Chapter X — Determination and Authorisation of Pension and Gratuity (143 questions)

PS-031 · Retirement list · Rule 54(1)
Every Head of Department must prepare a list of servants due to retire within the next fifteen months:
  1. A by the 1st day of every month
  2. B by the last day of every month
  3. C by the 15th day of every month
  4. D once a year, in January
Answer and reasoning
( C) by the 15th day of every month. (A) by the 1st day of every month. — The rule fixes the fifteenth. (B) by the last day of every month. — The last day is when a copy goes to the Accounts Officer under rule 54(2). (D) once a year, in January. — The list is monthly. Rule 54(1) requires every Head of Department to have a list prepared by the 15th day of every month of all Government servants due to retire within the next fifteen months of that date. Rule 54(2) requires a copy to the Accounts Officer before the last day of every month. Rule 54(3) deals with other retirements: the Head of Office must inform the Accounts Officer within ten days of the order. Exam-safe point: List by the 15th; copy to Accounts Officer by the month's last day. Statutory Authority: Rule 54, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-032 · Start of preparatory work · Rule 56
Preparatory work for processing a pension case begins:
  1. A eight months before retirement, when the third stage begins
  2. B one year before retirement, or on proceeding on leave preparatory to retirement, whichever is earlier
  3. C on the date of the retirement order — That is the rule 58 trigger for other retirements
  4. D six months before retirement, when Form 4 and Form 6 fall due
Answer and reasoning
( B) one year before retirement, or on proceeding on leave preparatory to retirement, whichever is earlier. (A) eight months before retirement, when the third stage begins. — Eight months is a deadline within the year, not its start. (D) six months before retirement, when Form 4 and Form 6 fall due. — The six-month point is the deadline for those forms under rule 57(2)(a), not the start of preparation. Rule 56 requires every Head of Office to undertake the preparatory work one year before the date of superannuation retirement, or on the date the servant proceeds on leave preparatory to retirement, whichever is earlier. Rule 57 divides that year into three stages, with verification of service complete eight months before superannuation and the third stage beginning no later than eight months before retirement. Exam-safe point: One year out, or on leave preparatory to retirement, whichever is earlier. Statutory Authority: Rule 56 and rule 57(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-033 · Unanswered verification reference · Rule 57(1)(a)(v)
A Head of Office refers a period of service to another office for verification and receives no response within the two months allowed. The period:
  1. A is deemed to qualify for pension
  2. B is held in abeyance until the other office replies
  3. C must be verified from pay bills by the referring office
  4. D is treated as non-qualifying
Answer and reasoning
( A) is deemed to qualify for pension. (B) is held in abeyance until the other office replies. — The deeming provision exists to prevent that delay. (C) must be verified from pay bills by the referring office. — That is the sub-clause (ii) route, not the consequence of silence. (D) is treated as non-qualifying. — The rule deems the opposite where no response comes. Rule 57(1)(a)(iv) gives the office receiving a verification reference two months to verify and reply, with a proviso requiring any period incapable of verification to be flagged at once. Sub-clause (v) then provides that if no response is received within that time, the period shall be deemed to qualify for pension. Sub-clause (vi) fixes responsibility on the Secretary of the Ministry where a non-qualifying period was not communicated. Exam-safe point: Silence for two months: the period is deemed to qualify. Statutory Authority: Rule 57(1)(a)(iv) to (vi), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-034 · Verification of emoluments · Rule 57(1)(b)(v)
For calculating emoluments and average emoluments, the Head of Office verifies correctness of emoluments:
  1. A for the entire service
  2. B for the last ten months only
  3. C for the whole of the last five years — The rule expressly stops at twenty-four months
  4. D only for the twenty-four months preceding retirement, and no earlier period
Answer and reasoning
( D) only for the twenty-four months preceding retirement, and no earlier period. (A) for the entire service. — The rule expressly confines verification to twenty-four months. (B) for the last ten months only. — Ten months is the averaging window; the verification window is twenty-four. Rule 57(1)(b)(iv) requires the Head of Office to verify from the service book the correctness of the emoluments drawn or to be drawn during the last ten months of service. Sub-clause (v) then limits that exercise: to ensure those ten months are correctly shown, the Head of Office verifies correctness only for the twenty-four months preceding retirement, and not for any period before that date. Rule 63(1)(c) imposes the same limit on the Accounts Officer. Exam-safe point: Twenty-four months, not the ten-month averaging window. Statutory Authority: Rule 57(1)(b)(v) and rule 63(1)(c), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-035 · Provisional pension and gratuity · Rule 62(3)(a)
Where provisional pension and gratuity are sanctioned under rule 62, the sanction authorises:
  1. A two-thirds of pension, and the full gratuity
  2. B 100 per cent of pension, but no gratuity at all
  3. C 50 per cent of pension and 90 per cent of gratuity — Neither figure appears in rule 62(3)
  4. D 100 per cent of pension, and 100 per cent of gratuity withholding ten per cent of the gratuity
Answer and reasoning
( D) 100 per cent of pension, and 100 per cent of gratuity withholding ten per cent of the gratuity. (A) two-thirds of pension, and the full gratuity. — Two-thirds is the rule 40 provisional figure for compulsory retirement. (B) 100 per cent of pension, but no gratuity at all. — That is the position under rule 8 where proceedings are pending. Rule 62(3)(a) requires the Head of Office to authorise, from the date following retirement, 100 per cent of pension as provisional pension and 100 per cent of the gratuity as provisional gratuity while withholding ten per cent of the gratuity. Rule 62(4) requires the sanction within ten days after retirement on superannuation, or within one month of the forms for other retirements, and rule 62(6)(a) caps provisional pension at six months. Exam-safe point: 100 per cent of both, with ten per cent of gratuity withheld. Statutory Authority: Rule 62(3) to (6), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-036 · Provisional becoming final · Rule 62(7)
The final pension and gratuity are not determined within six months of the provisional sanction. The Accounts Officer:
  1. A shall refer the case to the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare
  2. B shall continue the provisional pension indefinitely — Rule 62(7) converts it instead of extending it
  3. C shall treat the provisional pension and gratuity as final and issue the PPO on expiry of the six months
  4. D shall recover the provisional pension paid — The rule converts the provisional payment; it does not recover it
Answer and reasoning
( C) shall treat the provisional pension and gratuity as final and issue the PPO on expiry of the six months. (A) shall refer the case to the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare. — No such reference is provided for in rule 62(7). Rule 62(6)(a) caps provisional pension at six months from retirement or from submission of Form 4 and Form 6, whichever is later. Rule 62(7) then provides that where the final amounts have not been determined within that period, the Accounts Officer shall treat the provisional pension and gratuity as final and issue the pension payment order immediately on the expiry of the six months. Rule 62(8) then releases the withheld gratuity. Exam-safe point: Six months: provisional becomes final. Statutory Authority: Rule 62(6) to (8), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-037 · PPO timelines · Rule 63(1)(a) and (b)
The Accounts Officer must issue the pension payment order for a superannuation retirement:
  1. A on the date of retirement itself
  2. B not later than two months before the date of retirement
  3. C within forty five days of receiving the papers
  4. D within one month of receiving the papers
Answer and reasoning
( B) not later than two months before the date of retirement. (A) on the date of retirement itself. — The rule requires issue in advance of that date. (C) within forty five days of receiving the papers. — The forty-five-day limit applies to retirements other than on superannuation under clause (b). (D) within one month of receiving the papers. — One month is the family pension timeline under rule 76(1), not this one. Rule 63(1)(a) requires the Accounts Officer, on receiving the pension case under rule 60, to apply the checks, record the enfacement in Part II of Form 7, assess pension, family pension and gratuity, and issue the pension payment order not later than two months before the date of superannuation retirement. Clause (b) gives forty-five days from receipt of the papers where the retirement is otherwise than on superannuation. Exam-safe point: Two months in advance for superannuation; forty-five days otherwise. Statutory Authority: Rule 63(1)(a) and (b), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-038 · Interest on delayed pension · Rule 65(5)(a)
A servant retires on superannuation and his pension is paid late for administrative reasons. Interest runs from:
  1. A the date following the expiry of three months from the date of retirement
  2. B the date of retirement itself
  3. C the date six months after retirement
  4. D the date following the expiry of one month from retirement
Answer and reasoning
( A) the date following the expiry of three months from the date of retirement. (B) the date of retirement itself. — Interest begins only after the three-month grace period. (C) the date six months after retirement. — Six months is the missing-person waiting period, not the interest trigger. (D) the date following the expiry of one month from retirement. — The period is three months. Rule 65(1) allows interest on arrears at the rate applicable to General Provident Fund amounts where delay is attributable to administrative reasons or lapses, unless the delay was the servant's own failure to comply with the procedure. Rule 65(5)(a) then fixes the start of the period for a superannuation retirement at the date following the expiry of three months from retirement, running to the date of payment. Exam-safe point: Interest: three months after retirement. Statutory Authority: Rule 65(1) and (5)(a), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-039 · Revision to the disadvantage of a pensioner · Rule 66(2) proviso
A clerical error in a pension authorised two years and three months ago is detected. The pension may be revised to the pensioner's disadvantage:
  1. A only with the concurrence of the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare
  2. B never, because more than two years have passed
  3. C only with the sanction of the Ministry of Finance
  4. D on the Head of Office's own authority
Answer and reasoning
( A) only with the concurrence of the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare. (B) never, because more than two years have passed. — The rule permits revision with concurrence; it does not bar it. (C) only with the sanction of the Ministry of Finance. — The Ministry of Finance is consulted under rule 66(4) on waiver of recovery, not on the revision. (D) on the Head of Office's own authority. — The proviso requires a higher concurrence after two years. Rule 66(2) protects a pension once authorised, permitting revision to the disadvantage of the pensioner only where a clerical error is subsequently detected. Its proviso adds that where the error is detected more than two years after authorisation or revision, no such revision may be ordered without the concurrence of the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare. Rule 66(3) leaves the question whether an error is clerical to the administrative Ministry. Exam-safe point: After two years: DP&PW concurrence. Statutory Authority: Rule 66(2) and its proviso, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-040 · Recovery from gratuity · Rule 67(3)
Which of these may NOT be recovered from retirement gratuity?
  1. A Arrears of income tax deductible at source
  2. B Balance of a house building advance
  3. C Arrears of licence fee for Government accommodation
  4. D A personal loan taken by the servant from a cooperative society
Answer and reasoning
( D) A personal loan taken by the servant from a cooperative society. (A) Arrears of income tax deductible at source. — Clause (b) names it expressly. (B) Balance of a house building advance. — A house building advance is Government dues under clause (b). (C) Arrears of licence fee for Government accommodation. — Clause (a) covers accommodation dues and related charges. Rule 67(2) adjusts against retirement gratuity the Government dues assessed by the Head of Office and outstanding at retirement. The Explanation defines Government dues as accommodation dues including licence fee arrears, damages, and electricity, water and PNG charges under clause (a), and under clause (b) the balance of house building, conveyance or other advances, overpayment of pay, allowances or leave salary, and arrears of income tax deductible at source. Rule 67(3) then forbids recovery of anything that is not Government dues in that sense. Exam-safe point: Only Government dues come out of gratuity. Statutory Authority: Rule 67(2) and (3), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-041 · No Demand Certificate · Rule 68(7)(a)
The Directorate of Estates must issue a No Demand Certificate after the accommodation is vacated:
  1. A within seven days of the application
  2. B within one month of the application
  3. C within fourteen days of the application
  4. D within two months of the application
Answer and reasoning
( C) within fourteen days of the application. (A) within seven days of the application. — Seven days is the rule 71(4)(c) period for a death intimation. (B) within one month of the application. — The period is fourteen days. (D) within two months of the application. — Two months is the period for the Directorate's reply under rule 68(1)(a). Rule 68(7)(a) requires the Directorate of Estates to give the No Demand Certificate within fourteen days of the application made after actual vacation of the accommodation. Clause (b) entitles the allottee to interest at General Provident Fund rates on the excess withheld gratuity if the certificate is delayed beyond that, and clause (c) makes the Directorate of Estates pay it through the Accounts Officer. Exam-safe point: Fourteen days for the No Demand Certificate. Statutory Authority: Rule 68(7), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-042 · Deemed retirement · Rule 70(2)
The office fails to issue the retirement notification on time. The servant:
  1. A continues in service until the notification issues — Rule 70(2) expressly denies that consequence
  2. B is deemed to have retired on attaining the age of superannuation, and is not entitled to continue
  3. C must apply afresh for pension — Pension follows from the deemed retirement
  4. D is entitled to pay for the period of delay
Answer and reasoning
( B) is deemed to have retired on attaining the age of superannuation, and is not entitled to continue. (D) is entitled to pay for the period of delay. — The rule does not create a right to pay for a failure to notify. Rule 70(1) requires a Gazette notification for a Gazetted servant, or an office order for a non-Gazetted servant, specifying the date of retirement within a week, with a copy to the Accounts Officer. Rule 70(2) then provides that unless specific extension orders issue, the servant is deemed to have retired on attaining the age of superannuation, and the office's failure to issue the notification does not entitle him to continue beyond that date. Exam-safe point: Deemed retirement on the superannuation date, notification or not. Statutory Authority: Rule 70, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-009 · Form 6-A at retirement · Rule 57(2)(a) as substituted in 2024
From the date the amendment rules of 2024 took effect, the retiring Government servant submits the completed family and pension particulars:
  1. A in Form 4 and Form 6, as rule 57(2)(a) originally required
  2. B in Form 10, at any time before the Pension Payment Order issues
  3. C in Form 6-A, not later than six months before the date of retirement
  4. D in Format 9, which is the bank undertaking
Answer and reasoning
( C) in Form 6-A, not later than six months before the date of retirement. (A) in Form 4 and Form 6, as rule 57(2)(a) originally required. — Form 4 and Form 6 were replaced by Form 6-A for the retirement case. (B) in Form 10, at any time before the Pension Payment Order issues. — Form 10 is the family pension claim for a death case. (D) in Format 9, which is the bank undertaking. — Format 9 is an undertaking to the bank, and the 2024 amendment replaced it in this context with Form 6-A. G.S.R. 410(E) dated 16 July 2024 substituted rule 57(2)(a) so that the Government servant submits duly completed Form 6-A to the Head of Office not later than six months before his date of retirement. It also substituted rule 57(3) so that where Form 6-A is submitted by the spouse or another member of the family, the Government servant is not entitled to commutation until he applies for it himself. Exam-safe point: Form 6-A, six months before retirement. Statutory Authority: Rule 57(2)(a), as substituted by G.S.R. 410(E) dated 16.07.2024
CU-011 · Which system carries Form 6-A · Rule 53(1) as substituted in 2024
Under rule 53(1) as substituted in 2024, a retiring official who is on e-HRMS submits Form 6-A through:
  1. A Bhavishya, in every case
  2. B e-HRMS, and only in superannuation cases
  3. C the Head of Office, who uploads it on the official's behalf
  4. D either system, at the official's choice
Answer and reasoning
( B) e-HRMS, and only in superannuation cases. (A) Bhavishya, in every case. — Bhavishya is the route for cases other than superannuation and for officials not on e-HRMS. (C) the Head of Office, who uploads it on the official's behalf. — The official submits; the Head of Office processes. (D) either system, at the official's choice. — The rule assigns the route by case and by whether the official is on e-HRMS. Rule 53(1) was substituted by G.S.R. 410(E). Unless exempted by a general or special order, the pension case is processed online through Bhavishya or e-HRMS. Retiring officials who are on e-HRMS submit Form 6-A through e-HRMS, and only for superannuation. Those not on e-HRMS, and cases other than superannuation such as voluntary retirement, premature retirement, absorption, invalidation, compulsory retirement and dismissal or removal, submit Form 6-A through Bhavishya. Exam-safe point: e-HRMS for superannuation, Bhavishya for everything else. Statutory Authority: Rule 53(1), as substituted by G.S.R. 410(E) dated 16.07.2024
CU-027 · Sanction of provisional pension · Rule 62(4)
Sanction of provisional pension in a superannuation case must issue:
  1. A within one month of the date of retirement
  2. B not later than ten days after the date of retirement
  3. C within three months of the date of retirement
  4. D on the date of retirement, together with the Pension Payment Order
Answer and reasoning
( B) not later than ten days after the date of retirement. (A) within one month of the date of retirement. — One month applies where the retirement is otherwise than on superannuation. (C) within three months of the date of retirement. — Three months is the interest trigger under rule 65, not the sanction deadline. (D) on the date of retirement, together with the Pension Payment Order. — The rule sets a deadline after retirement. Rule 62(4) requires a sanction for provisional pension to issue not later than ten days after the date of retirement in a case of retirement on superannuation, and within one month from the date of submission of the forms where the retirement is otherwise than on superannuation. Rule 65(1) then makes interest payable at the General Provident Fund rate where the sanction or payment is delayed for administrative reasons. Exam-safe point: Ten days on superannuation, one month otherwise. Statutory Authority: Rule 62(4), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-045 · Revision to the disadvantage of the pensioner · Rule 66(2)
Once pension or family pension has been authorised after final assessment, it:
  1. A may never be revised in either direction — Revision in the pensioner's favour is provided for by rule 66(1)
  2. B shall not be revised to the disadvantage of the Government servant, except as provided in rules 7 and 8
  3. C may be revised downwards only on the orders of the President
  4. D may be revised downwards at any time within five years — Rule 66(2) protects the authorised amount
Answer and reasoning
( B) shall not be revised to the disadvantage of the Government servant, except as provided in rules 7 and 8. (C) may be revised downwards only on the orders of the President. — Rules 7 and 8 are the route, not a general power of revision. Rule 66(2) provides that, subject to rules 7 and 8, pension or family pension once authorised after final assessment or revised under sub-rule (1) shall not be revised to the disadvantage of the Government servant, except in the circumstances the rule sets out. Rule 66(1) allows revision in his favour, and specifies how an arrear is computed and paid. Exam-safe point: No downward revision outside rules 7 and 8. Statutory Authority: Rule 66(2), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-061 · Unverified service: the notice · Rule 57(1)(a)(iv)
Where a period of service cannot be verified from the records, the Head of Office:
  1. A refers the matter to the Accounts Officer immediately — The Head of Office first asks the servant
  2. B issues a notice to the Government servant, and if no reply comes within the time allowed, treats the period as not countable
  3. C reports the servant for a disciplinary offence — The rule provides a notice and a determination, not a penalty
  4. D counts the period in the servant's favour by default
Answer and reasoning
( B) issues a notice to the Government servant, and if no reply comes within the time allowed, treats the period as not countable. (D) counts the period in the servant's favour by default. — Verification is required; silence in answer to the notice counts against the period. Rule 57(1)(a)(iv) provides for communication with the Government servant where a period of service is not capable of being verified from the records, and clause (v) provides that if no response is received within the time allowed, the Head of Office shall treat the period as not counting as qualifying service, subject to clause (vi), which allows it to be counted if later found to be admissible. Exam-safe point: Notice, then non-counting on silence, provisionally. Statutory Authority: Rule 57(1)(a)(iv) and (v), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-062 · Where no family member is eligible · Rule 57(3)(b)
Where the Head of Office is satisfied that there is no member of the family eligible to receive family pension, the pension papers are submitted:
  1. A by the gratuity nominee, on the conditions in the proviso
  2. B by the Head of Office himself, who signs in place of the family
  3. C to the Central Pension Accounting Office directly
  4. D not at all, until a claimant appears
Answer and reasoning
( A) by the gratuity nominee, on the conditions in the proviso. (B) by the Head of Office himself, who signs in place of the family. — The nominee submits. (C) to the Central Pension Accounting Office directly. — The papers go through the Head of Office to the Accounts Officer. (D) not at all, until a claimant appears. — The rule provides a route through the gratuity nominee. Rule 57(3)(b) provides for the case where there is no member of the family eligible to receive family pension, and its proviso, as substituted by G.S.R. 410(E) dated 16 July 2024, deals with the position where the form is submitted by the spouse or another member of the family: the Government servant is then not entitled to commutation until he applies for it himself under the CCS (Commutation of Pension) Rules, 1981. Exam-safe point: The gratuity nominee files, and commutation waits for the servant's own application. Statutory Authority: Rule 57(3)(b) and its proviso, as substituted by G.S.R. 410(E) dated 16.07.2024
CU-063 · Retirement other than on superannuation · Rule 58(2)(b)
A Government servant retiring otherwise than on superannuation submits Form 6-A:
  1. A only if the retirement was voluntary — The rule covers every retirement other than on superannuation
  2. B six months before the date of retirement — Six months is the superannuation period under rule 57(2)(a)
  3. C within one month of the Pension Payment Order — The form precedes the order
  4. D immediately after the competent authority approves the retirement or the retirement takes effect
Answer and reasoning
( D) immediately after the competent authority approves the retirement or the retirement takes effect. Rule 58(1), as substituted by G.S.R. 410(E), requires a Government servant who is retiring or has retired for reasons other than superannuation to submit Form 6-A to the Head of Office immediately after the competent authority has approved the retirement or the retirement has become effective, as the case may be. Its proviso on commutation mirrors rule 57(3). Exam-safe point: Immediately on approval or effect, not six months ahead. Statutory Authority: Rule 58(2)(b) and rule 58(1), as substituted by G.S.R. 410(E) dated 16.07.2024
CU-064 · Amount recoverable stated in the sanction · Rule 62(3)(b)(i)
The letter of sanction of provisional pension must specify:
  1. A only the amount of provisional pension — The gratuity and the recovery must both be stated
  2. B the name of the officer responsible for the delay — Responsibility is fixed under rule 65(4), separately
  3. C the date on which the final pension will be authorised — The rule does not require a forecast date
  4. D the amount recoverable from the gratuity as assessed under rule 67, and the amount of provisional gratuity after deducting it
Answer and reasoning
( D) the amount recoverable from the gratuity as assessed under rule 67, and the amount of provisional gratuity after deducting it. Rule 62(3)(b) requires the Head of Office to specify in the letter of sanction the amount recoverable from the gratuity as assessed under rule 67, and clause (i) requires the amount of provisional pension to be stated while clause (ii) requires the amount of provisional gratuity after deducting the recovery. Exam-safe point: Both figures go into the sanction: the recovery and the net gratuity. Statutory Authority: Rule 62(3)(b), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-065 · Pension Payment Order and the family · Rule 63(1)(d)
The Pension Payment Order issued by the Accounts Officer must:
  1. A name the family members only if the pensioner asks — The requirement is unconditional
  2. B name only the pensioner — Rule 63(1)(d) requires the family members to be named
  3. C include the names of the members of the family eligible for family pension, and the share of each where the pension is shared
  4. D leave the family to be added by the Pension Disbursing Authority — The Accounts Officer includes them in the order
Answer and reasoning
( C) include the names of the members of the family eligible for family pension, and the share of each where the pension is shared. Rule 63(1)(d) requires the Pension Payment Order to include the names of the members of the family eligible for family pension, and their shares where the family pension is to be shared, for example children from a wife who is not alive or children from a divorced wife. Rule 79(2)(a)(iv) then allows names to be added later on the Head of Office's communication. Exam-safe point: The order names the eligible family members and their shares. Statutory Authority: Rule 63(1)(d), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-066 · Recovery of Government dues · Rule 70(1)(b)
Government dues recoverable from the gratuity are recovered:
  1. A only by a civil court on a suit by the Government — The Rules provide for administrative recovery
  2. B by the Head of Office, who assesses the dues and adjusts them against the gratuity under the rule
  3. C only by the Accounts Officer, after the Pension Payment Order issues
  4. D only with the consent of the pensioner
Answer and reasoning
( B) by the Head of Office, who assesses the dues and adjusts them against the gratuity under the rule. (C) only by the Accounts Officer, after the Pension Payment Order issues. — The Head of Office makes the assessment and the adjustment. (D) only with the consent of the pensioner. — Certain dues are recovered without consent, as rule 77(1)(x) shows for dearness relief. Rule 70 deals with the recovery of Government dues from the gratuity. Sub-rule (1) requires the Head of Office to assess the dues and, in clause (b), to recover them from the amount of gratuity becoming payable, with the procedure and the priorities the rule sets out. Exam-safe point: Assessment and recovery both sit with the Head of Office. Statutory Authority: Rule 70(1)(b), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
TX-0417 · Sub-rule (1) of rule 53 · Rule 53 · 53(1)
Which of the following is the text of sub-rule (1) of rule 53?
  1. A In calculating the length of qualifying service, fraction of a year equal to three months and above shall be treated as a completed six monthly period and reckoned as qualifying service.
  2. B A pension or provisional pension granted or awarded under sub-rule (1) or, as the case may be, under sub-rule (2), shall not be less than the amount of minimum pension mentioned in rule 44.
  3. C Unless otherwise exempted by a general or special order of the Government, the pension case of a Government servant shall be processed through the online pension sanctioning system, namely, Bhavishya.
  4. D Where a Government servant has no family, as referred to in the explanation below sub-rule (6) of rule 45, at the time of making a nomination, the nomination made by the Government servant in favour of a person or a body of individuals under clause (ii) of proviso to sub-rule (2) shall become invalid in the event of the Government servant subsequently acquiring a family.
Answer and reasoning
( C) Unless otherwise exempted by a general or special order of the Government, the pension case of a Government servant shall be processed through the online pension sanctioning system, namely, Bhavishya. (A) In calculating the length of qualifying service, fraction of a year equal to three months and above shall be treated as a completed six monthly period and reckoned as qualifying service. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. (B) A pension or provisional pension granted or awarded under sub-rule (1) or, as the case may be, under sub-rule (2), shall not be less than the amount of minimum pension mentioned in rule 44. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. (D) Where a Government servant has no family, as referred to in the explanation below sub-rule (6) of rule 45, at the time of making a nomination, the nomination made by the Government servant in favour of a person or a body of individuals under clause (ii) of proviso to sub-rule (2) shall become invalid in the event of the Government servant subsequently acquiring a family. — It is the text of a different provision of these rules. The answer reproduces the provision as notified. The three wrong options are other provisions of the same rules, so the question tests recall of this provision rather than recognition of the statute's style.
