Chapter XI — Family Pension and Gratuity on Death or Disappearance in Service (96 questions)

PS-043 · Death of an allottee · Rule 71(4)(a)
A Government servant dies while in occupation of Government accommodation. The licence fee outstanding for the period before his death:
  1. A is recovered from the provident fund
  2. B stands waived
  3. C is recovered from the family pension
  4. D is recovered from the death gratuity
Answer and reasoning
( B) stands waived. (A) is recovered from the provident fund. — The rule provides no such recovery. (C) is recovered from the family pension. — The rule waives the pre-death licence fee. (D) is recovered from the death gratuity. — Only dues relating to damages are recovered from death gratuity. Rule 71(4)(a) waives the dues pertaining to outstanding licence fee for the period before the date of death of a servant who was an allottee. Clause (b) keeps dues relating to damages recoverable from the death gratuity, and provides that if the family retains the accommodation, no licence fee is recovered for the month of death and the first three months after it. Clause (c) requires the Head of Office to write to the Directorate of Estates within seven days. Exam-safe point: Pre-death licence fee waived; damages still recoverable. Statutory Authority: Rule 71(4), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-044 · Provisional family pension · Rule 75(1)
On death of a servant in service, provisional family pension must be drawn:
  1. A within fifteen days of receipt of the claim
  2. B within forty five days of receipt of the claim
  3. C within seven days of receipt of the claim
  4. D within one month of receipt of the claim
Answer and reasoning
( A) within fifteen days of receipt of the claim. (B) within forty five days of receipt of the claim. — Forty-five days is the invalid pension period under rule 39(8). (C) within seven days of receipt of the claim. — Seven days is the intimation period to the Directorate of Estates. (D) within one month of receipt of the claim. — One month is the rule 74(1) period for forwarding the case, and the rule 76(1) period for the Accounts Officer. Rule 75(1) requires the Head of Office, once satisfied of the claimant's eligibility, to draw provisional family pension not exceeding the maximum admissible, within fifteen days of receipt of the claim, issuing a sanction letter and drawing the amount as establishment pay is drawn. Rule 75(3) continues it for six months from the day after death unless extended under rule 76. Exam-safe point: Provisional family pension: fifteen days. Statutory Authority: Rule 75(1) and (3), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-045 · Gratuity held over · Rule 74(4)(c)
The maximum amount of gratuity that may be held over pending assessment of Government dues on a death case is:
  1. A one-third of the amount of gratuity
  2. B fifty per cent of the amount of gratuity
  3. C twenty per cent of the amount of gratuity
  4. D ten per cent of the amount of gratuity
Answer and reasoning
( D) ten per cent of the amount of gratuity. (A) one-third of the amount of gratuity. — One-third is the rule 8(6) recovery cap. (B) fifty per cent of the amount of gratuity. — No such figure appears in rule 74. (C) twenty per cent of the amount of gratuity. — Twenty per cent is the rule 47(7) minor's-share figure. Rule 74(4) requires the Head of Office to draw the Accounts Officer's attention to outstanding Government dues, including under clause (b) the amount of gratuity held over partly for adjustment of unassessed dues and partly as a margin, and clause (c) caps that held-over amount at ten per cent of the gratuity. Rule 76(5)(e) then provides for adjustment of the withheld amount against outstanding licence fee and refund of the balance. Exam-safe point: Held-over gratuity: ten per cent maximum. Statutory Authority: Rule 74(4) and rule 76(5)(e), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-023 · Provisional family pension · Rule 76
Where a Government servant dies in service and the family pension case cannot be finalised, provisional family pension is sanctioned:
  1. A by the Head of Office, and it continues until the final amount is determined
  2. B only on the orders of the Secretary of the Ministry — No such sanction is required
  3. C by the Accounts Officer, after the Pension Payment Order issues
  4. D for a maximum of six months in every case
Answer and reasoning
( A) by the Head of Office, and it continues until the final amount is determined. (C) by the Accounts Officer, after the Pension Payment Order issues. — The Head of Office sanctions; the Accounts Officer authorises the final pension. (D) for a maximum of six months in every case. — The period may be extended with the approval of the Head of Department. Rule 76 provides for provisional family pension so that the family is not left without support while the final authorisation is under process. The Head of Office sanctions it, and rule 76(2) allows the period to be extended on the case being submitted to the Head of Department. The order of 29 October 2026 restates the mechanism. Exam-safe point: Sanctioned by the Head of Office, extended through the Head of Department. Statutory Authority: Rule 76, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021

Chapter XII — Family Pension and Residuary Gratuity on Death or Disappearance of a Pensioner (38 questions)

PS-046 · Sanction of family pension on a pensioner's death · Rule 79(2)(b)(i)
A pensioner dies leaving a family member not named in the pension payment order. The Head of Office sanctions family pension:
  1. A in Format 12, within one month of the claim
  2. B in Form 13, within one month of the claim
  3. C in Format 13, within one month of receipt of the claim in Form 10
  4. D in Form 10, within three months of the claim
Answer and reasoning
( C) in Format 13, within one month of receipt of the claim in Form 10. (A) in Format 12, within one month of the claim. — Format 12 is the letter inviting the claim, not the sanction. (B) in Form 13, within one month of the claim. — Form 13 is the residuary gratuity claim. (D) in Form 10, within three months of the claim. — Form 10 is the claim itself, and the period is one month. Rule 79(2)(b)(i) applies where the pension payment order names no family member, or where the person now entitled is someone else, including a person who joined the family after retirement. The Head of Office must, within one month of receiving a claim in Form 10, sanction the family pension in Format 13 in favour of the person entitled. Rule 80(1) then requires the Accounts Officer to authorise payment within one month of the sanction. Exam-safe point: Sanction: Format 13, on a Form 10 claim, within one month. Statutory Authority: Rule 79(2)(b)(i) and rule 80(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-047 · Residuary gratuity claim · Rule 79(6)
A claim for residuary gratuity on the death of a retired servant is made in:
  1. A Form 9
  2. B Format 13
  3. C Form 13
  4. D Form 12
Answer and reasoning
( C) Form 13. (A) Form 9. — Form 9 is the death gratuity claim by a nominee or family member. (B) Format 13. — Format 13 is the Head of Office's sanction of family pension. (D) Form 12. — Form 12 is the family pension claim against a pensioner's PPO. Rule 79(6) provides that where a residuary gratuity becomes payable to the family of a deceased retired servant under rule 45(3), the Head of Office sanctions its payment on receipt of a claim in Form 13 from the person or persons eligible. Rule 45(3) grants the residuary gratuity where the sums received by the pensioner before death fall short of twelve times his emoluments within five years of retirement. Exam-safe point: Residuary gratuity: claim in Form 13. Statutory Authority: Rule 79(6) and rule 45(3), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-010 · Form 6-A in place of Form 10 · Rule 80(5) proviso as substituted in 2024
Where a Government servant dies after retirement and no member of the family is eligible for family pension, the person in whose favour a gratuity nomination was made may submit:
  1. A Form 4 together with Format 9 — Both were subsumed into Form 6-A for this purpose
  2. B Form 10, because the gratuity nominee has no other route
  3. C Form 6-A in place of Form 10, giving his or her bank account details in Form 6-A
  4. D no form at all, the gratuity being paid on the nomination itself
Answer and reasoning
( C) Form 6-A in place of Form 10, giving his or her bank account details in Form 6-A. (B) Form 10, because the gratuity nominee has no other route. — The proviso substituted in 2024 gives the gratuity nominee Form 6-A instead. (D) no form at all, the gratuity being paid on the nomination itself. — A claim form is still required; the proviso names it. The first proviso to rule 80(5)(a) was substituted by G.S.R. 410(E) dated 16 July 2024. Where there is no member of the family eligible to receive family pension on the death of the Government servant, a member of the family in whose favour a nomination was made for payment of gratuity is allowed to submit Form 6-A in place of Form 10, and must indicate the details of his or her bank account in Form 6-A. Exam-safe point: Gratuity nominee: Form 6-A instead of Form 10. Statutory Authority: Rule 80(5)(a), first proviso, as substituted by G.S.R. 410(E) dated 16.07.2024
CU-046 · Authority to pay after sanction · Rule 80(1)
On receipt of the sanction under rule 79 for family pension or residuary gratuity, the Accounts Officer shall authorise payment:
  1. A within one month from the date of receipt of the sanction
  2. B within ten days from the date of receipt of the sanction
  3. C without any time limit, the sanction being sufficient authority
  4. D within three months from the date of receipt of the sanction
Answer and reasoning
( A) within one month from the date of receipt of the sanction. (B) within ten days from the date of receipt of the sanction. — Ten days is the Special Seal of Authority step in rule 80(3). (C) without any time limit, the sanction being sufficient authority. — The rule fixes a period. (D) within three months from the date of receipt of the sanction. — Three months is the interest trigger for delayed gratuity, not the authorisation period. Rule 80(1) requires the Accounts Officer, on receipt of the sanction under rule 79, to authorise the payment within one month from the date of receipt of the sanction. Its first proviso makes interest payable where gratuity is delayed beyond three months from the date of submission of the claim for administrative reasons, and rule 80(3) gives the Central Pension Accounting Office ten days to issue the Special Seal of Authority. Exam-safe point: One month to authorise; ten days for the seal; three months for the interest trigger. Statutory Authority: Rule 80(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021

Chapter XIII — Payment of Pensions (13 questions)

PS-048 · Pension for the day of death · Rule 81(3)
Pension, including family pension, is payable:
  1. A only up to the last working day of the month
  2. B for the day on which its recipient dies
  3. C for the whole month in which the recipient dies
  4. D up to the day before the recipient dies
Answer and reasoning
( B) for the day on which its recipient dies. (A) only up to the last working day of the month. — That is the payment convention in rule 83(2), not the accrual. (C) for the whole month in which the recipient dies. — The rule fixes the day of death, not the whole month. (D) up to the day before the recipient dies. — Rule 81(3) includes the day of death. Rule 81(1) makes pension other than family pension payable from the date the servant ceases to be borne on the establishment. Rule 81(2) makes family pension payable from the day after the death or ineligibility, subject to rule 76(2)(d) and rule 79(3)(iv). Rule 81(3) then provides that pension, including family pension, is payable for the day on which its recipient dies. Exam-safe point: The day of death is a pension day. Statutory Authority: Rule 81, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-049 · Payment of monthly pension · Rule 83(2)
A monthly pension is payable:
  1. A on or after the last working day of the month to which it relates, except March
  2. B on the first working day of every month without exception
  3. C in advance, on the first day of the month to which it relates
  4. D on the last working day of every month without exception — March is the exception
Answer and reasoning
( A) on or after the last working day of the month to which it relates, except March. (B) on the first working day of every month without exception. — Only March is paid on or after the first working day of April. (C) in advance, on the first day of the month to which it relates. — Payment is on or after the last working day, not in advance. Rule 83(1) requires gratuity to be paid in lump sum. Rule 83(2) makes a pension fixed at monthly rates payable monthly on or after the last working day of the month to which it relates, except for the month of March, when it is payable on or after the first working day of April. Rule 82 confines all pensions and gratuities to rupees in India. Exam-safe point: Last working day, with March paid in April. Statutory Authority: Rules 82 and 83, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-067 · Other rules that apply to payment · Rule 84(1)
The procedure for the payment of gratuity, of pension, of pension undrawn for more than a year, and of pension in respect of a deceased pensioner is governed by:
  1. A the Treasury Rules of the Central Government, save as otherwise provided in these rules
  2. B the Central Civil Services (Commutation of Pension) Rules, 1981
  3. C the Payment of Arrears of Pension (Nominations) Rules, 1983
  4. D the General Financial Rules, 2017 — Rule 84(1) names the Treasury Rules
Answer and reasoning
( A) the Treasury Rules of the Central Government, save as otherwise provided in these rules. (B) the Central Civil Services (Commutation of Pension) Rules, 1981. — Those Rules govern commutation, under rule 84(2). (C) the Payment of Arrears of Pension (Nominations) Rules, 1983. — Those Rules govern nomination for arrears, under rule 84(3). Rule 84 applies other rules to the payment of pension. Sub-rule (1) applies the Treasury Rules of the Central Government to the procedure for payment of gratuity, pension, pension undrawn for more than a year, and pension in respect of a deceased pensioner; sub-rule (2) applies the CCS (Commutation of Pension) Rules, 1981 to commutation; and sub-rule (3) applies the Payment of Arrears of Pension (Nominations) Rules, 1983 to nomination for arrears. Exam-safe point: Treasury Rules for payment, Commutation Rules for commutation, Arrears Rules for nomination. Statutory Authority: Rule 84(1), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021

Chapter XIV — Miscellaneous (16 questions)

PS-050 · Interpretation · Rule 85
A doubt arises on the interpretation of the pension rules. It is referred to:
  1. A the Central Administrative Tribunal — The Tribunal adjudicates disputes; it is not the interpretative authority
  2. B the Ministry of Finance (Department of Expenditure) in every case — The Ministry of Finance is consulted on waiver of recovery under rule 66(4)
  3. C the Comptroller and Auditor General — The C&AG audits; it does not decide interpretation
  4. D the Government in the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare or the Department of Personnel and Training, depending on the rule or subject
Answer and reasoning
( D) the Government in the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare or the Department of Personnel and Training, depending on the rule or subject. Rule 85 requires a doubt on the interpretation of the rules to be referred for decision to the Government in the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare or the Department of Personnel and Training, depending on the rule or the subject on which a decision is required and the Department concerned with it. Rule 86 separately allows a Ministry to relax a rule causing undue hardship, with the concurrence of one of those two Departments. Exam-safe point: Interpretation: DP&PW or DoPT, by subject. Statutory Authority: Rules 85 and 86, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-051 · Power to relax · Rule 86 proviso
A Ministry wishes to relax a rule that is causing undue hardship. It may do so:
  1. A only with the approval of the President
  2. B on its own authority, recording reasons
  3. C only through a fresh notification amending the rules
  4. D by order recording reasons, with the concurrence of DP&PW or DoPT
Answer and reasoning
( D) by order recording reasons, with the concurrence of DP&PW or DoPT. (A) only with the approval of the President. — The concurrence required is departmental, not presidential. (B) on its own authority, recording reasons. — The proviso requires the concurrence of one of the two Departments. (C) only through a fresh notification amending the rules. — Rule 86 is a relaxation power, not an amendment route. Rule 86 permits a Ministry or Department satisfied that a rule causes undue hardship to dispense with or relax it by order for reasons recorded in writing, to the extent and on the exceptions and conditions it considers just and equitable. The proviso forbids any such order except with the concurrence of the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare or the Department of Personnel and Training, according to the rule or subject. Exam-safe point: Relaxation: reasoned order plus DP&PW or DoPT concurrence. Statutory Authority: Rule 86 and its proviso, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-052 · Repeal and saving · Rule 87(2)(c)
A pension case of a servant who retired before the 2021 Rules commenced is pending on commencement. It is decided:
  1. A under the 2021 Rules, because they are now in force
  2. B by the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare
  3. C under the old rules, as if the 2021 Rules had not been made
  4. D under whichever set of rules is more beneficial
Answer and reasoning
( C) under the old rules, as if the 2021 Rules had not been made. (A) under the 2021 Rules, because they are now in force. — Rule 87(2)(c) saves the old law for pending cases. (B) by the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare. — The saving prescribes the law, not a new authority. (D) under whichever set of rules is more beneficial. — The saving is not a beneficial-choice provision. Rule 87(1) repeals the old rules, including the CCS (Pension) Rules, 1972, so far as they provide for matters now contained in the 2021 Rules. Rule 87(2) saves nominations, family particulars and pension applications made under the old rules, and requires pending cases of authorisation of pension under clause (c), and of gratuity and family pension under clause (d), to be disposed of under the old rules as if the new rules had not been made. Exam-safe point: Pending cases: the old rules still govern. Statutory Authority: Rule 87, CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
PS-053 · Saving of nominations · Rule 87(2)(a)
A nomination for gratuity made under the 1972 Rules before commencement of the 2021 Rules:
  1. A lapses on commencement and must be re-made
  2. B is deemed to have been made under the corresponding provisions of the 2021 Rules
  3. C continues under the 1972 Rules indefinitely — It is deemed to be made under the new rules
  4. D must be re-executed in Form 3 within six months
Answer and reasoning
( B) is deemed to have been made under the corresponding provisions of the 2021 Rules. (A) lapses on commencement and must be re-made. — Rule 87(2)(a)(i) saves it rather than letting it lapse. (D) must be re-executed in Form 3 within six months. — No re-execution period is imposed on a saved nomination. Rule 87(2)(a) treats every nomination for gratuity, every form giving family details for family pension, and every formal application for sanction of pension made under the old rules as made under the corresponding provisions of the 2021 Rules. Clause (b) deals with the opposite case, requiring a nomination or family form not yet made to be made under the new rules after commencement. Exam-safe point: Old nominations carry over as if made under the new rules. Statutory Authority: Rule 87(2)(a) and (b), CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021
CU-025 · NPS to CCS coverage · O.M. 03.03.2023
A Central Government civil employee appointed in 2005 against a post advertised in 2003 asks to be covered by the CCS (Pension) Rules instead of the National Pension System. That is possible:
  1. A on a fresh recruitment against a pre-2004 vacancy
  2. B in no case, since posts after 31 December 2003 are outside the Rules
  3. C under the one-time option in the order of 3 March 2023, where the post was advertised on or before 22 December 2003
  4. D by an order of the appointing authority in each case, at its discretion
Answer and reasoning
( C) under the one-time option in the order of 3 March 2023, where the post was advertised on or before 22 December 2003. (A) on a fresh recruitment against a pre-2004 vacancy. — The option attaches to the post and the individual, not to a fresh appointment. (B) in no case, since posts after 31 December 2003 are outside the Rules. — The order of 3 March 2023 creates a one-time option that reaches such cases. (D) by an order of the appointing authority in each case, at its discretion. — The option is exercised by the employee and considered by the appointing authority under the order. The notification of 22 December 2003 introduced the National Pension System, and the rules were amended on 30 December 2003 so that they ceased to apply to persons appointed after 31 December 2003. The Department's order of 3 March 2023 gives a one-time option to a central civil employee appointed against a post advertised or notified on or before 22 December 2003, who is covered by the NPS on joining, and provides for the option to be placed before the appointing authority. The option, once exercised, is final. Exam-safe point: One-time option for pre-22.12.2003 vacancies, under the 2023 order. Statutory Authority: DoP&PW O.M. No. 57/05/2021-P&PW(B) dated 03.03.2023

Questions people actually ask (10)

Each answer is tied to the rule that decides it. Nothing here is stated without a rule citation.

What is the difference between a Form and a Format under these rules?

Rule 3(1)(k) defines a Form as a form appended to these rules. Rule 3(1)(l) defines a Format as a format appended to them. They are two appended series, separately numbered, so Form 3 is the gratuity nomination (rule 46) while Format 3 is the memorandum of charges (rule 8(2)(c)). The prescribing clause, not the familiarity of the number, decides which one an answer needs.

Authority: Rules 3(1)(k) and 3(1)(l)

Does qualifying service begin on confirmation?

No. Rule 11 begins it on the date the servant takes charge of the post to which he is first appointed, whether substantively, in an officiating capacity or on a temporary basis. Confirmation matters at rule 16, which says probation followed by confirmation qualifies, but it is not the commencement date.

Authority: Rules 11 and 16

How is a broken month handled in the average emoluments?

A month is reckoned as thirty days, so fractional periods in the last ten months are multiplied by 14/30, 16/30 and so on, whatever the calendar length of the month, February included. Rule 32(3) works this through on a retirement dated 16 July 2019.

Authority: Rule 32(3) and its Illustration

What is the pension ceiling, and does it apply to family pension?

Ordinary pension is subject to a minimum of ₹9,000 and a maximum of ₹1,25,000 a month under rule 44(1). Family pension is subject to the same minimum, but its ordinary maximum is ₹75,000 under rule 50(2)(a)(i), rising to ₹1,25,000 for the enhanced rate under rule 50(2)(a)(iv).

Authority: Rules 44(1) and 50(2)

Is the ₹20 lakh gratuity ceiling still the operative figure?

The text of rule 45(1), as notified in 2021, caps retirement gratuity and death gratuity at twenty lakh rupees. The ceiling was raised to twenty-five lakh rupees with effect from 1 January 2024 by a subsequent Office Memorandum, so a question that quotes the rule and a question that quotes current practice have different answers. This platform states the rule text and flags the change.

Authority: Rule 45(1) proviso

Which Forms does a retiring servant actually file?

Form 4 for family particulars and Form 6 for the pension claim, each with a Format 9 undertaking to the bank, not later than six months before retirement under rule 57(2)(a). Form 7 is then completed by the Head of Office and the Accounts Officer under rules 59 and 63, and forwarded under a Format 10 covering letter.

Authority: Rules 57(2), 59, 60 and 63

What happens if the pension papers are not ready by the retirement date?

Rule 62 authorises 100 per cent of pension as provisional pension and 100 per cent of gratuity as provisional gratuity while withholding ten per cent of the gratuity, and rule 62(4) requires that sanction within ten days after retirement on superannuation. If the final amounts are still not determined six months later, rule 62(7) makes the provisional amounts final.

Authority: Rule 62

How long must a family wait after reporting a missing servant?

Six months from lodging the police report before family pension, including arrears, and gratuity may be paid, under rule 51(8)(a). Death gratuity becomes payable once death is conclusively established or on expiry of seven years from the report, whichever is earlier, under rule 51(8)(b).

Authority: Rule 51(8)

Can pension be reduced after it has been authorised?

Only for a clerical error, under rule 66(2). If the error is detected more than two years after authorisation, the revision needs the concurrence of the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare. Rule 66(4) then requires the Ministry to examine waiver of any resulting overpayment with the Ministry of Finance.

Authority: Rule 66

Which rules still govern a case pending when the 2021 Rules commenced?

The old rules. Rule 87(1) repeals the 1972 Rules so far as the new rules cover the same matters, but rule 87(2)(c) and (d) require pending pension, gratuity and family pension cases to be disposed of under the old rules as if the new rules had not been made.

Authority: Rule 87(2)

How this was built

The rule text is transcribed from the gazette and every one of the 87 rules is present; the build fails if a rule number is missing, if a question cites a rule the build does not hold, if a Form or Format cites a sub-rule that cannot be resolved, or if a worked rupee figure does not re-derive from the formula it claims to apply. The Formats are separated from the Forms throughout, because the statute separates them in rule 3 and a question that asks for one has a different answer from a question that asks for the other.
